chapters.title: Chapter 201 | Elena
paragraphs: Dexter looked at her.

He looked at the girl who had followed him to a rooftop because she wanted to know where he was, the girl who had remembered his birthday when no one else did. The girl who had spent what was probably a significant portion of her money on a secondhand sweater for a boy that the rest of the estate treated like furniture.
He looked at her, and he felt so thing breaking inside of him; twisting like a key unlocking an old doo.
"Jasmine," he said.
She turned her head and looked at him with her cute eyes.
Dexter held his gaze as he looked at her.
"Thank you,"
Those two words were inadequate for what she had gone through to give her the gifts but his words meant everything.
Those words that couldn’t possibly carry the weight of what he actually meant.
But Jasmine smiled as though she understood what he meant.
The quiet smile started at the corners of her mouth and spread slowly to her eyes.
"You’re welcome," she said.
Then she turned back to the sunset.

They sat together on the crumbling wall of the forgotten rooftop, shoulder to shoulder, watching the sky burn itself out in shades of gold and crimson and violet. The city hummed below them but none of it mattered.

The rooftop was ugly, but sitting there, in a blue sweater that was slightly too large, beside a girl who had remembered his birthday, Dexter Ashford felt something he had never felt before in his fourteen years of life.
He felt like he belonged somewhere.
The weeks that followed were the happiest of his life.

They developed a routine. Every evening, after their respective duties were finished, they would meet on the rooftop. Sometimes they talked about everything, about nothing, about the heroes they admired. About the places they wanted to visit. About the lives they dreamed of living once they escaped the Ashford estate.
Sometimes they didn’t talk at all. They simply sat together and watched the city change colors as the sun moved across the sky.
Jasmine told him about her family. Her younger brother, who wanted to be a hero when he grew up. Her older sister, who had married a merchant and moved to another city.
Dexter told her about his mother. About the fragments of information he had gathered over the years from servants who had been present when she was alive.

Her name was Elena. She had been brought to the Ashford estate as a servant when she was sixteen. She had been quiet. Gentle. She had sung while she worked, soft melodies that the other servants remembered years after her death.
She had died giving birth to him.
That was all he knew.
Jasmine listened to every word. She didn’t interrupt nor did she offer hollow platitudes. She simply listened, her hand finding his, interlacing with his and holding on.

One evening, three months after the birthday sweater, they sat on the wall watching a particularly spectacular sunset. The sky was doing something unusual. The clouds had arranged themselves into long, thin bands that caught the light and glowed like rivers of molten gold flowing across a violet sky.
Jasmine leaned her head against his shoulder.
"Dexter?"
"Yeah?"
"When you leave this place, and you will leave this place, where will you go?"
Dexter was quiet for a moment. He had thought about leaving. Every day. Every hour. The desire to walk through the Ashford estate gates and never return was like a real demon whispering in his mind.

But the Ashford family would never let him go, knowingl he was still connected to them by blood. Even if he ran away, he had no money, no resources, no education, and an F-Rank mana affinity that made him less valuable than the lowest hired servant.
"I don’t know," he said honestly. "Anywhere. Everywhere. Somewhere far from here. Somewhere quiet. Maybe a small house. With a garden. And a kitchen where I can cook whatever I want."
"You like cooking?" Jasmine lifted her head from his shoulder and looked at him with genuine surprise.

"I love cooking," Dexter said. He had never admitted this to anyone. In the Ashford estate, cooking was a servant’s job. A menial task. Not something a person did because they enjoyed it. "When I was younger, I used to sneak into the kitchen after everyone had gone to sleep. I would take whatever ingredients were left over and just... cook. Experiment. Try different combinations. See what worked and what didn’t."
He paused. "The head cook caught me once. She didn’t report me. She just gave me a recipe book and told me to clean up after myself."
Jasmine stared at him.
Then she smiled.
It was the widest smile he had ever seen on her face. Bright. Unfiltered. The kind of smile that rearranged everything he thought he knew about the way faces worked.
"What?" he asked, suddenly self-conscious.
"Nothing," she said. "I just think you’re full of surprises."
She leaned her head back against his shoulder.
"When you open your restaurant," she said, her voice drowsy and warm, "I want to be your first customer."
Dexter looked down at her. Her eyes were closed. Her lashes were dark crescents against her cheeks. Her breathing was slow and even. The sunset painted her face in gold.
"When I open my restaurant," he said quietly, "you’ll be more than a customer."

He wasn’t sure what he meant by that. He wasn’t sure what he was trying to say. He was fourteen. He had never been on a date. He had never held a girl’s hand before Jasmine. He didn’t know the right words for the things he was feeling, because nobody had ever taught him the vocabulary of tenderness.
But Jasmine smiled without opening her eyes.
"I know," she whispered.
They stayed on the rooftop until the stars came out.

The city below had transformed into a sea of lights. Towers and streets and homes, each one a small point of illumination in the vast darkness. From above, it looked like a reflection of the sky. As if the stars had fallen and settled on the earth, creating a second constellation that hummed with life.
Jasmine had fallen asleep against his shoulder.
Dexter sat perfectly still, not wanting to disturb her. The blue sweater kept him warm. The stars kept him company. The weight of her head on his shoulder kept him grounded.
He didn’t sleep. He didn’t want to and he wanted to stay in this moment for as long as it lasted.
The Ashford estate would surely notice and someone would see them and would report.
But Dexter at that moment didn’t care. Be just wanted to stay up there with her.

chapters.title: Chapter 202 | The Meeting
paragraphs: Dexter reached the restaurant at 12:40 PM.

He had ten minutes to make up for. His jacket was torn at the shoulder from the fight. His knuckles were bruised and the adrenaline from the confrontation at Harvest Homes was still humming through his veins like electricity through a live wire.
None of it showed on his face.
He walked through the restaurant entrance with the calm, composed expression of a man who had not, in fact, just been thrown through a wall by a four-meter Ultra Realm expert thirty minutes ago.
The receptionist looked up and smiled.
"Good afternoon, sir. Welcome. How may I help you?"
"I’m Dexter Ashford. I have a reservation. Booth 24."
The receptionist checked the tablet in front of her. Her eyes moved across the screen. Then she looked up, her smile brightening.
"Welcome, Mr. Ashford. Your party is already seated. Please head down the main hallway, second door on your left."
Dexter thanked her and walked through the dining area.
The restaurant was busier and every table was occupied.
Waiters wove between chairs carrying steaming plates of meals.
He reached the hallway, Booth 24.
He placed his hand on the door handle, pushed it open, and stepped inside.
When he stepped inside, there were six people seated in the booth.
He had expected five.
A few meant three or four, maybe five at most. Dexter had prepared himself for a small, informal gathering of mid-rank heroes who wanted to swap war stories and discuss squad formation over a meal.
He had not prepared himself for six.

He had especially not prepared himself for the woman sitting alone in the corner chair, sipping a glass of palm wine with the unhurried patience of someone who was accustomed to being the most important person in any room she entered.
Dexter controlled his expression.

It took effort. A significant amount of effort. His brain registered the scene in a single, comprehensive snapshot, processing every face, every posture, every detail in the fraction of a second before his expression could betray his surprise.
He smiled.

The booth was a private room. Circular table. Seating for eight. The lighting was warm. The walls were decorated with handwoven textiles in geometric patterns of indigo and gold. A large platter of assorted appetizers sat in the center of the table, surrounded by glasses and bottles.

Five men sat in a loose circle around one side of the table. They were relaxed. Comfortable. The body language of people who had been chatting long enough to settle into their seats and claim their territory.
The sixth person sat alone.
Aurora.
The youngest S-Rank hero in the Hero Association.

She sat in the corner chair, separated from the others by a gap of empty space that was clearly not accidental. The five men had arranged themselves on the opposite side of the table, grouped together in a cluster that spoke volumes about their collective willingness to sit within arm’s reach of someone who could probably level the building if she sneezed.

Aurora didn’t seem to mind. She leaned against the table with one elbow, her glass of palm wine held loosely in her hand, her dark eyes fixed on Dexter with an expression of quiet, evaluating interest.
Dexter catalogued the other faces.

Cole who was called Plasmatic Man. Seated at the center of the group. He was the one who had organized this meeting. Mid-twenties. Clean-shaven. Blue t-shirt and jeans. His plasma energy was fully suppressed, giving no hint of the devastating power he could wield.
To Cole’s left was a man Dexter recognized from the outbreak. Blitz. A speed-type hero whose talent allowed him to move at extraordinary velocities for short bursts.

He had been the one pulling injured civilians from collapsed buildings during the attack, darting in and out of danger zones with a fearlessness that had impressed even the veteran responders. He was slender. Wiry. His features were sharp, his eyes constantly moving, scanning the room with the restless energy of someone whose brain operated at a faster clock speed than everyone else’s.
To Cole’s right was a man Dexter recognized but did not like.
Bullet Spear Man.

His real name was apparently something else, but everyone in the hero community knew him by his combat moniker. He was tall. Muscular. His arms were thick, and his hands were large. He carried a collapsed spear harness on his back, the weapon’s shaft visible above his shoulder. His face was handsome in a rough, aggressive way. Strong jaw. Cropped hair. A scar running from his left ear to his collar.
Dexter remembered him from the outbreak.
He remembered what Bullet Spear Man had done.

During the Goblin attack, when a group of civilians had been cornered in an alley by a pack of six-star beasts, Bullet Spear Man had been in a position to rescue them directly. Instead, he had positioned himself at the opposite end of the alley and attacked the monsters from behind, using the civilians as bait.
The strategy was effective. The distracted monsters were easier to kill from behind. The civilians survived, though two of them were injured in the process.

Dexter understood the tactical logic. He understood that sometimes, in combat, difficult choices produced better outcomes than heroic ones. He understood that Bullet Spear Man’s decision had resulted in fewer total casualties than a direct rescue attempt might have.
But understanding logic and trusting a person were two different things.
A man who would use civilians as bait would use teammates as bait. Given the right circumstances. Given the right tactical calculation. Given the right price.
Dexter did not trust Bullet Spear Man.
He nodded politely, smiled and said nothing beyond the basic social courtesies.
The fourth person was a man called Gridlock. A defensive specialist. His talent allowed him to create localized force fields that could absorb and redirect kinetic energy.
During the outbreak, he had used his barriers to create safe zones where civilians could shelter while the combat heroes engaged the monsters.

chapters.title: Chapter 203 | Aurora
paragraphs: The fifth was the Tank. His actual hero name was Bulwark, but everyone called him the Tank because it was more accurate. His talent was straightforward and devastatingly effective. Extreme durability. His body could absorb physical punishment that would kill most heroes. Blades bounced off his skin.
Blunt force that would shatter bones merely bruised. During the outbreak, he had stood in front of a charging six-star Dark Hound and let it slam into him at full speed.
One Six arm goblin had broken its neck on impact but the Tank had gotten a bruise.
He was the quietest of the group. Sitting at the edge of the circle, his massive arms folded across his massive chest with a calm look.
Five heroes. All of them from the outbreak.
And then Aurora.

Dexter took the empty seat that Cole was pointing to. It was on the opposite side of the table from Aurora, positioned between the Tank and Gridlock. He sat down, settled into the chair, and looked at the group.
"I’m sorry for being late," he said. "I got held up."
The others waved dismissively.
"No worries, no worries," Cole said, grinning. "We understand."
Blitz leaned forward. "If it were some of us, we might have been even later. I got stuck in traffic on the way here. Literally had to run the last three blocks."
Gridlock nodded solemnly. "I was early. I’m always early."
"That’s because you have no life," Bullet Spear Man said with a smirk.
"That’s because I’m responsible," Gridlock replied, completely unfazed.
The table chuckled.

Dexter smiled. The banter was easy. Natural. The kind of exchange that happened between people who had shared a dangerous experience and come out the other side with a bond that was hard to articulate but impossible to deny.
He glanced at Aurora.

She was still watching him. Her dark eyes were steady. Unblinking. Her expression was neutral, giving nothing away. She sipped her palm wine with the slow, deliberate patience of someone who was content to observe until she had seen enough.
Cole leaned toward Dexter. His voice dropped to a murmur that was pitched just below the threshold of the others’ conversation.
"We had already gathered here before you arrived," Cole said quietly. "We were expecting you. Then she walked in."
He glanced at Aurora.
"She said she wanted to meet you. Specifically."
Dexter blinked. "Do you know why?
Cole shook his head. "No. She hasn’t said. She’s been sitting there since she arrived, drinking palm wine and not talking to anyone."
He paused.
"I suspect she’ll tell you when she’s ready."
Dexter looked at Aurora again. She met his gaze for a brief moment, then returned her attention to her glass.
"Okay," Dexter said.
He turned back to the group and let the conversation carry him.
The discussion flowed naturally. They talked about the outbreak.
Blitz talked about the rescues of how close to being with death as he saved a few heroes from the clutches of death.
The Tank said very little. When asked about his experience, he simply said, "I stood in front of things. The things broke."
Dexter listened to Bullet Spear Man’s account and said nothing.

’Bullet Spear Man is competent and he kills without hesitation. But his priorities are wrong. He values results over people and sees civilians as resources, not as lives. And a person who sees other people as resources will eventually see you the same way.
’I cannot be on a squad with this man.’
The thought was firm.

Dexter continued chatting with the others, avoiding direct conversation with Bullet Spear Man without making it obvious. He laughed at Blitz’s jokes. He complimented Gridlock’s barrier technique. He nodded respectfully at the Tank.
And throughout it all, Aurora sat in her corner. Sipping her drink while watching silently.
After the discussion had wound down and the appetizers had been substantially reduced, Cole reached for his glass and tapped it with a spoon.
Ting. Ting
The table quieted.
Cole stood. He raised his glass with a genuine, unguarded smile.
"Today, one of the reasons we gathered here is to thank Dexter for what he did during the outbreak.
His voice was warm and sincere. The voice of a man who genuinely believed that he owed his life to the person sitting across from him.
"Dexter, we say thank you. For giving us a second chance at life."
He raised his glass higher.
"Cheers."
"Cheers!" the table echoed.
Glasses rose. Blended. The sound of glass meeting glass rang through the booth like a small, musical bell.
Blitz grinned and Gridlock nodded solemnly as the Tank raised his glass witb his large hands.
Even Bullet Spear Man raised his drink, his smirk softening into something that resembled genuine gratitude.
Dexter looked at the glass in front of him. Amber liquid. The sharp, smoky scent of aged whiskey.
He picked it up.
"I accept your appreciation," he said. "Thank you."
He downed the drink in one smooth motion.

The whiskey burned down his throat, spreading warmth through his chest. It wasn’t the Emperor Void Flame. It wasn’t mana circulation. It was simpler than that. Rougher. The warmth of alcohol shared between people who had bled together.

The heroes clapped. They cheered. They took their own drinks and downed them with the enthusiastic commitment of people who believed that any problem could be temporarily improved by the application of sufficient alcohol.

The atmosphere lightened. The formality dissolved. What remained was something more honest. More human. Five people who had fought beside each other, survived, and come back to talk about it over food and drinks.

Dexter found himself genuinely enjoying the company. Blitz’s manic energy was infectious. Gridlock’s dry, deadpan humor caught him off guard more than once. Even the Tank, in his monosyllabic way, contributed moments of unexpected comedy.
At one point, Blitz asked the Tank why he never dodged attacks.
The Tank looked at Blitz as though the question had offended his ancestors.
"Why would I dodge?" he said. "Dodging means moving. Moving means effort. Standing still is free."
The table erupted.

"We were expecting you.
Then she walked in."
He glanced at Aurora.
"She said she wanted to meet you.
Specifically."
Dexter blinked.
"Do you know why?
Cole shook his head.
"No.
She hasn’t said.
She’s been sitting there since she arrived, drinking palm wine and not talking to anyone."
He paused.
"I suspect she’ll tell you when she’s ready."
Dexter looked at Aurora again.
She met his gaze for a brief moment, then returned her attention to her glass.
"Okay," Dexter said.
He turned back to the group and let the conversation carry him.
The discussion flowed naturally.
They talked about the outbreak.
Blitz talked about the rescues of how close to being with death as he saved a few heroes from the clutches of death.
The Tank said very little.
When asked about his experience, he simply said, "I stood in front of things.
The things broke."
Dexter listened to Bullet Spear Man’s account and said nothing.
’Bullet Spear Man is competent and he kills without hesitation.
But his priorities are wrong.
He values results over people and sees civilians as resources, not as lives.
And a person who sees other people as resources will eventually see you the same way.
’I cannot be on a squad with this man.’
The thought was firm.
Dexter continued chatting with the others, avoiding direct conversation with Bullet Spear Man without making it obvious.
He laughed at Blitz’s jokes.
He complimented Gridlock’s barrier technique.
He nodded respectfully at the Tank.
And throughout it all, Aurora sat in her corner.
Sipping her drink while watching silently.
After the discussion had wound down and the appetizers had been substantially reduced, Cole reached for his glass and tapped it with a spoon.
Ting.
Ting
The table quieted.
Cole stood.
He raised his glass with a genuine, unguarded smile.
"Today, one of the reasons we gathered here is to thank Dexter for what he did during the outbreak.
His voice was warm and sincere.
The voice of a man who genuinely believed that he owed his life to the person sitting across from him.
"Dexter, we say thank you.
For giving us a second chance at life."
He raised his glass higher.
"Cheers."
"Cheers!" the table echoed.
Glasses rose.
Blended.
The sound of glass meeting glass rang through the booth like a small, musical bell.
Blitz grinned and Gridlock nodded solemnly as the Tank raised his glass witb his large hands.
Even Bullet Spear Man raised his drink, his smirk softening into something that resembled genuine gratitude.
Dexter looked at the glass in front of him.
Amber liquid.
The sharp, smoky scent of aged whiskey.
He picked it up.
"I accept your appreciation," he said.
"Thank you."
He downed the drink in one smooth motion.
The whiskey burned down his throat, spreading warmth through his chest.
It wasn’t the Emperor Void Flame.
It wasn’t mana circulation.
It was simpler than that.
Rougher.
The warmth of alcohol shared between people who had bled together.
The heroes clapped.
They cheered.
They took their own drinks and downed them with the enthusiastic commitment of people who believed that any problem could be temporarily improved by the application of sufficient alcohol.
The atmosphere lightened.
The formality dissolved.
What remained was something more honest.
More human.
Five people who had fought beside each other, survived, and come back to talk about it over food and drinks.
Dexter found himself genuinely enjoying the company.
Blitz’s manic energy was infectious.
Gridlock’s dry, deadpan humor caught him off guard more than once.
Even the Tank, in his monosyllabic way, contributed moments of unexpected comedy.
At one point, Blitz asked the Tank why he never dodged attacks.
The Tank looked at Blitz as though the question had offended his ancestors.
"Why would I dodge?" he said.
"Dodging means moving.
Moving means effort.
Standing still is free."
The table erupted.

chapters.title: Chapter 204 | Join Our Squad
paragraphs: Cole suddenly set his glass down and leaned forward, resting his forearms on the table.
"Now that we’ve gotten that out of the way, we should probably talk about why we’re actually here."
The table went quiet.
"The five of us have been talking," Cole continued. "Since the outbreak. We’ve been discussing the idea of forming a squad."
He looked around the table.
"A standard squad consists of six people and we currently have five people here.
Cole’s gaze moved to Dexter.
"We’d be very honored if you become our sixth member."
Dexter looked at Cole and then stated at the others who nodded and smile at him.
Bullet Spear Man was leaning back in his chair, with a neutral expression in hhs face.
Cole continued. "You saved our lives. And from what we’ve seen, you’re the kind of person who doesn’t abandon his position, no matter what comes at you."
He paused.
"That’s the kind of person we want watching our backs."

Dexter remained silent as he stared at the five people before him. Logically, joining a squad is quite useless and would simple tie him to multiple people and take his time to use to take care of his wives.
But if he could join a squad, it would be easier to hunt and clear dungeons with them when they familiarize themselves with their techniques, strengths and weaknesses.
Moroever, he wouldn’t need to respond to every single Monster outbreak nearby. As clearing one dungeon would automatically give him the month off.
Moreover, if he hopes to actually be able to get a land in this city, he would need lots of money and lots of connections that even the Ashford family can’t influence.
Surely, the incident with the housing agent would happen again so he needed all these things. But it’s a gradual process.
The others seem to hold their breathe as they waited for Dexter’s response.
"Alright."
Cole exhaled slowly.
"That’s exactly what we were hoping you’d say."
He extended his hand across the table.
"Welcome to the squad, Dexter."
Dexter looked at the hand.
He thought about his wives, about the house he didn’t have, the money he had lost, the fight he had just been in. The enemies that were circling his family like wolves around a campfire.
Dexter reached across the table and shook Cole’s hand.
"Thabk you.
"Welcome to the squad," Cole repeated, grinning.
The table broke into applause as Blitz whooped, Gridlock clapped and the others smiled.
Dexter smiled and from the corner of his eyes, he saw Aurora set down her glass and turned to look at him with a small smile.
Dexter chose to ignore it.
The conversation continued as they drank, they laughed and discussed.
Dexter found himself relaxing as the tension from the Harvest Homes confrontation and the adrenaline that had been simmering beneath his skin since the fight with the old man disappeared.
He hadn’t realized how much he had needed this.
Dexter checked his phone and saw it was 2:30 PM.
He had been here for almost two hours. The girls had been alone since morning but he had left food for them in the kitchen, so they wouldn’t go hungry. But food wasn’t the issue.
The issue was that three disabled women were sitting in a house in a neighborhood that had suffered two monster outbreaks in three weeks.
Even if he was sure nothing would happen, his mind wasn’t settled.
They might need him but here he was, drinking whiskey and having fun. A pang of guilt struck his chest and Dexter chose to ignore it as he chuckled at Gridlock’s joke.
However, the guilt strangely spread through his entire body, making him frown. He didn’t expect to have such a reaction.
Dexter sighed and he immediately stood up.
"I’m really sorry to cut this short, but I have to go. I hope you all understand where I’m coming from."
The table looked at him as the five people, each carrying a slightly different expression.
Cole smiled first. "Yes, yes. We understand. There’s no need to explain.
Blitz nodded rapidly. "We get it, man. Family first."
Gridlock inclined his head. "Of course."
The Tank nodded with a small smile while Bullet Spear Man said nothing as he simply raised his glass in a lazy salute.

Dexter smiled. "I apologize once again. You guys have fun and text me the details of when the combat training will occur. I’ll make sure to come early this time and make sure there are no unexpected incidents to delay me."
Cole laughed. "We’ll hold you to that."
Dexter smiled, raised a hand in farewell, and walked toward the door.
He opened the door and stepped into the hallway, closing it behind him.
He had taken three steps down the corridor when he heard the door open behind him again. He didn’t turn around immediately, but his Enhanced Hearing picked up the sound.
Reaching the restaurant lobby, he crossed it, stepped through the front door, and onto the sidewalk.
Halfway to his SUV, keys already in hand, he felt something.
His eyes flashed and he immediately turned around.
Aurora was there.
She hadn’t been there a second ago but she had suddenly appeared in a split second.
Ultra Realm experts possessed an ability transcending conventional movement not teleportation, exactly.
Teleportation involved instantaneous matter displacement, bypassing space but the ability Ultras possess was different.
It was a burst speed their bodies move at.

It was instantaneous repositioning. They could move from one location to another within their line of sight in a fraction of a second, their body translating through space with such speed that it looked like teleportation.
The range was roughly a hundred meters and anything within their visual field was reachable in an instant.
This was what made Ultra Realm experts so fundamentally different from Superhumans.
Dexter’s brows furrowed slightly.
"You wanted to see me," he said.
He had been waiting for this moment since he first saw her in the booth.

chapters.title: Chapter 205 | I Have A Preposition For You
paragraphs: Aurora looked at him for a long, silent moment.
Her eyes studied his face as she studied him.
She was an S-Rank hero.
She had fought and killed creatures that would have slaughtered entire squads of lower-rank heroes. She could read people the way Dexter read ingredients.
"Yes," she said finally. "I wanted to meet you. But it has proven quite difficult to get a hold of you."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "I’m not that hard to find."

"You are, actually," Aurora replied, her voice carrying a trace of genuine frustration. "Getting your contact information from the Hero Association was impossible. They said you explicitly refused to have your details shared."
She paused.
"It is the first time I have been rejected."
Dexter shrugged. "There’s a first time for everything."
Aurora’s eyes flashed with interest.
She didn’t respond immediately as she let the silence between them stretch even further, still staring at Dexter with the same interest.
Dexter’s brows remained furrowed, his mind working through possibilities.
’Why is she looking at me like that? What does she want?’
’She is an S-Rank hero and one of the youngest S-Rank in the association. She has access to the best squads, the best resources and the best missions. So what does she want’
At that moment, Aurora opened her mouth.
"During the monster outbreak," she said, her voice dropping to a register that was meant for his ears only, "you were in quite a hurry to leave. As if you sensed something."
She paused.
"Did something happen to your wives?"
Dexter’s eyes flashed.
He studied her face for a moment, she was perceptive and knew it was about his wives.
"Yes," Dexter said. "But the situation was under control."
Aurora nodded slowly as the answer seemed to satisfy her.
"You are quite different from what the news says about you," she said in a normal tone as she stared at Dexter.
"You care quite a bit about your wives, don’t you?"
Dexter shrugged. "The news likes to exaggerate everything. Don’t believe everything you hear. Most of it is false. Or at least heavily exaggerated."
Aurora’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"Is that so?" she asked.
"Yes."
Dexter didn’t like her tone.
"What does it matter to you?"
Aurora remained silent for a moment.
"I was curious."
"Curiosity can get people into trouble."
"So can hiding your strength."
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
Aurora continued calmly.

"During the monster outbreak, everyone thought you were only a relatively ordinary Superhuman. Yet you appeared in the middle of the battlefield and killed monsters far beyond what someone at your supposed level should have been capable of."
Dexter’s expression remained unchanged. "Perhaps I’m simply stronger than I look."
"I thought so." Aurora’s eyes flashed faintly. "That is why I wanted to meet you."
Dexter folded his arms. "And now that you’ve met me?"
"I haven’t decided yet."
Dexter almost laughed. "You followed me out of a restaurant just to tell me that?"
"No." Aurora looked directly into his eyes. The gold flecks in her irises caught the light, giving them an almost luminous quality. "I wanted to ask you something."
Dexter’s expression became slightly more serious. "Go ahead."
Aurora was silent for several seconds. The sounds of the city filled the gap between them.
Finally, she spoke.
"Join my team."
Dexter blinked.
"Your team?"
"Yes."

Dexter frowned. "As you saw, I already have a team. Moreover, the Hero Association has already paired you with some of the most talented heroes of our generation. The best in the city. So I don’t think there is any space for me to join you."
Aurora shook her head. "Not that team. Nor a Association-sanctioned squad."
She paused.
"Another team. I have a proposition for you.
Her eyes flicked to the left. Then to the right. Scanning the street. The parked cars. The restaurant entrance behind them. The pedestrians walking past on the far side of the road.
"But it is quite a delicate matter," she said, her voice dropping half a register. "And I can’t say it out here. In case of listening ears."
As she said this, she looked directly behind Dexter. At his SUV.
Dexter blinked.
He understood what she meant and knew wanted him to invite her into the vehicle so she could speak further and away from potential eavesdroppers.
His first instinct was to refuse.
He didn’t know this woman. While he knew her reputation, her public profile and her hero ranking, he didn’t know her.
But then he thought about what had happened an hour ago.
The fight at Harvest Homes, there would surely be repercussions.
Harvest Homes was not a small company.
It was a registered, legitimate business with political connections, financial resources, and at least several Ultra Realm expert on its payroll.
The Ashford name might carry enough weight to deter direct retaliation. But they might even make the retaliation even stronger so he needed connections, allies.
Rachel was an option but he didn’t know Rachel’s full background.

Grandma Lucy was another option. The old woman who could disperse an Ultra-Rank aura with a tap of her finger. But he didn’t know her story either. Didn’t know her limitations. Didn’t know whether her protection extended beyond the sidewalk in front of his house.
Aurora was different.
Aurora was an S-Rank hero, one of the youngest S-Rank in the Association.
An Ultra Realm expert and her name alone carried more weight than most families in Stargate City. If she was associated with him, even loosely, it would give pause to anyone considering retaliation.
And she wanted something from him, which meant there was room for negotiation. Room for a mutually beneficial arrangement that could provide him with the backing he needed.
He would hear her out. If her proposition was unacceptable, he could simply tell her to leave.
Dexter nodded.
"Okay."
He walked to the passenger side and opened the door for Aurora.
Aurora looked at him for a brief moment before she then entered the vehicle.
Dexter walked around to the driver’s side and slid behind the wheel and then closed the door.
The moment Aurora entered, her face changed slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 206 | The 4th Dimension
paragraphs: Aurora’s face changed the moment she settled into the passenger seat.
Her eyes moved across the entire interior of the entire vehicle and her face kept changing even more rapidly.
Her fingers reached out she suddenly knocked on the glass panel of the passenger window as her brows furrowed.
Aurora had been inside many vehicles and had ridden in Type 2 transports during Association deployments.

She had been chauffeured in Type 3 vehicles too and had even entered a Type 4 vehicle once, owned by young master Crowell from one of the Nine Families who had attempted to impress her with his family’s wealth.
While she had been unimpressed by the young master, the type 4 car stood out to her.
But this vehicle was truly different.
The interior was simpler than the Type 4 Car and at first glance, it looked like a perfectly ordinary SUV with a slightly nicer interior than average.
But Aurora was born with an S-rank mana affinity. She could sense intense mana radiating off every part of the entire vehicle.
The Type 4 vehicle owned by the young master Crowell sas beautiful and strong but this vehicle gave Aurora the feeling of an expert in hiding.
Like a crouching tiger and a hidden dragon. It was wierd. It was when she tapped on the glasses that she confirmed her suspicion.
"This car is above Type 4," Aurora murmured.
Dexter had just settled into the driver’s seat when he heard her words. He froze for a second, then forced his expression to remain neutral.
He was quite surprised she had figured it out so quickly.
It’s no wonder she was one of the most talented young generations.
The vehicle was in its default mode and he hadn’t activated any of its Type-6 features and had deliberately kept it in its dormant state precisely to avoid this kind of situation.
But Aurora had detected it anyway.
Her composure broke as she turned toward him with stunned expression on her face.
"I’m right, aren’t I?" she said, her voice carrying absolute certainty. "This is above Type 6."
Her face instantly turned serious.
"Who exactly are you?"
Not to mention how impossible it was to find a vehicle above Type 4, the price of the vehicle would definitely be astronomical!
While Dexter was the illegitimate son of the Ashford family, he was clearly a nobody but yet, he had a Type 5 Vehicle with him!
This meant he wasn’t just hiding his strength, he might also possess a hidden background.
Even if one had the money to purchase the vehicle, the moment it enters the City’s Auction, it would definitely be fought by the entire Nine Families.
A type 5 weapon wasn’t that rare, but a type 5 vehicle was.
Dexter blinked expressionlessly and waved his hand offhandedly.
"This is just a random vehicle I bought," he said in a dissmissive tone.
"Now, do you want to tell me exactly what you want to say, or do you want to continue admiring an ordinary vehicle?"
Aurora stared at him.
She knew he was lying, and he knew she knew.
She also knew he knew she knew.
But Aurora didn’t press. Very few things surprised her and Dexter certainly had slightly exceeded her expectations.
But that was that.
If she knew it was actually type 6, her reaction would definitely be way different.
She had been slightly hesitant to involve Dexter, as she needed a wild card but the vehicle’s discovery had simply made the decision easier.
If Dexter had access to Type 4 object, then it was like she had suspected, Dexter definitely wasn’t ordinary.
Her expression turned very serious as she turned and stared forward through the glass and spoke.
"I found a map."
Hearing this, Dexter was quite confused.
’If you found a map, keep it. What does it have to do with me?’ Bhe he waited for her to finish hee words.
"A map leading to a portal."

Aurora continued. "A portal leading to the 4th Dimension."
Dexter blinked.
The words didn’t register immediately as those words were rarely spoken or heard by Dexter. It was a concept very unfamiliar to him.
The mysterious 4th Dimension.
The 3rd Dimension was space, length, width, and depth. The dimension in which all known life existed, the dimension in which Stargate City stood.
But they call this realm the 4th dimension because no one truly knows its realm name and not just anyone could enter into that realm
What was known about the Fourth Dimension could be summarized in a very short list.
But as it settled in Dexter’s mind and he remebered the fragments and pieces he heard from people over the years, his face started to change as his face changed slightly.
He stared at Aurora with a stunned expression in his face.

"Yes."
Dexter’s mouth opened. Then closed. Then opened again.
"That’s not possible," he said. "Portals to the 4th Dimension don’t exist. Its only pure fiction and science that everyone else ignores because it’s fantasy."
Aurora glanced at him but continued staring at the outside world.

"Once your rank in the hero association reaches A rank, you gain clearance and access to some materials and learn somethings are very much true. The information leaked so the Hero Association put it out there because they know humans try to rationalize everything. "No."

chapters.title: Chapter 207 | Treasure Trove
paragraphs: Aurora glanced at Dexter as though he had suddenly grown a second head.
Her eyebrows furrowed. She continued to look at him for a long moment, her dark eyes searching his face for any sign that his refusal was a negotiating tactic rather than a genuine rejection.
She found none. Suddenly, she smirked and then turned to face forward, looking through the windshield at the pedestrians walking past the restaurant.
She remained silent for a while, Dexter also remained silent. A pigeon landed on the hood, stared at its own reflection in the windshield for a few seconds, and flew away.
Ot was at that moment that Aurora spoke.
"All right. Rachel said you would reject."
Dexter blinked. His eyebrow rose sharply.
"You know Rachel?"
Aurora nodded. "Yeah. We are quite familiar with each other."
Dexter’s brows furrowed.
"Was she the one who told you about me?" Dexter asked carefully. "Did she point you in my direction for this expedition?"
Aurora shook her head slightly. "She knows almost nothing about this mission. But when I mentioned that I was considering you for the expedition team, she smiled. And she said you would never agree."
Aurora glanced at Dexter from the corner of her eye.
"Which, now that I’m looking at it, is quite correct."
Dexter blinked. "Oh."
Aurora looked at Dexter.
"The expedition is in three months," she said. "I told you that already but didn’t want to say this," she continued.
Dexter waited.
"Although we are entering the Fourth Dimension, we are not truly entering the Fourth Dimension."
Dexter blinked his eyes. "What does that mean?"
"The location we’re entering is a space connected to the fourth dimension. It’s like a dungeon but not truly one as there is a chance we could actually head outside 4th dimension.
Aurora’s tone became solemn.
"It is believed to be the death place of a Legend Realm expert.
Dexter’s pupils constricted.
Legend Realm which is above Transcendent and even Above Supreme. The highest cultivation realm that existed.

There were no Legend Realm experts alive in this country. There were none alive anywhere, as far as anyone knew. The last confirmed sighting of a Legend Realm existence had been over two hundred years ago.
A death place of a Legend Realm expert was a massive treasure trove of knowledge, techniques, resources, and power.
"That is the only thing I can tell you," Aurora continued. "As for which Legend Realm expert it was, I can’t reveal that information. Not until you are committed to the expedition."
She let the information settle.
"It was said that there are techniques inside that pocket space. Techniques to advance past the Transcendent Realm. Techniques to reach the Supreme Realm. Perhaps even beyond."
Each realm was exponentially more difficult to reach than the last. Talent alone was not enough!

The gap between Ultra and Transcendent was considered the greatest bottleneck in cultivation. Thousands of Ultra Realm experts across the country spent their entire lives trying to break through and failed.
Anyone who broke through to the Supreme Realm would gain absolute power and authority.

"You should think much deeper about it," Aurora said. Her voice was quiet but insistent. "You are already at the Superhuman Realm. You will break through to the Ultra Realm eventually. But above Ultra is Transcendent. And to break through to the Transcendent Realm, talent is not enough."
She looked at him.
"You have three months until the expedition. But you have two months to change your mind. After that, the preparation window closes and I proceed with or without you."
She reached for the door handle.
"My contact information is with Rachel. You can also obtain it from the Hero Association if you prefer."
She didn’t wait for Dexter to respond.
The passenger door opened and warm afternoon air rushed in as Aurora stepped out, closed the door behind her, and walked away without looking back.
Dexter sat alone in the SUV.
He stared at the space where Aurora had been sitting as he thought about what she had said.
The death place of a Legend Realm expert. A pocket dimension within the 4th Dimension, Techniques to advance past the Transcendent Realm. Possibly beyond.
It was true that reaching the Transcendent and Supreme Realms was extraordinarily difficult. For most hero, it was impossible.
Even the most gifted heroes in the city, the Auroras and the S-Rank prodigies, would eventually hit that wall and stop.
’But I am not most people! I have the10,000xInvestment Multiplier System.’
Every investment he made in his wives, returned to him multiplied a hundredfold.
As long as he continued to invest in his wives, the system would continue to advance his strength.
He was not afraid of encountering a bottleneck.
He wasn’t sure if the system could break through natural cultivation bottlenecks, the fundamental barriers between major realms that existed independent of mana quantity or talent level.
But that was a problem for the future.
He was currently at the Tenth Stage of the Superhuman Realm.
Each of those barriers was a bridge he would cross when he reached it.
For now, the system was sufficient.
What the system could not do, however, was heal his wives.

The system gave him the tools to help them. But the healing was slow. Incremental. Mira’s right arm had moved after three weeks of sustained, daily effort. At that rate, full recovery could take months. Years.
The Fourth Dimension, according to Aurora, offered a 50 percent chance of finding a cure.
Dexter shook his head.
’Not now. I have time. Two months to decide.’
He started the engine. Pulled away from the curb and merged into traffic.
Twenty minutes later, he turned onto his street and the bungalow came into view.
The freshly painted fence gleamed in the late afternoon light and the repaired window caught the sun and threw it back without a crack or a blemish.
He looked at the house and felt something settle in his chest.
He had been gone for hours which was probably the longest he had been away from his wives since they moved in.
’I kind of miss them.’
The thought actually caught him offguard.

chapters.title: Chapter 208 | Home Coming
paragraphs: Dexter smiled and opened the gate, walked up the path, and unlocked the front door.
He stepped inside and sighed in relief.
’Finally home!’
It felt like he had been out of the house for a long time when he had just been out for about 8 to 19 hours.
His opened his eyes and what he saw made his expression freeze and his heart skip a tiny bit.
At that moment, Mira was sitting in her wheelchair exactly one meter from the front door and was facing the entrance as though she had been waiting for hours.
Her crimson eyes were fixed on the doorway and as Dexter came in, her eyes immediately locked in on him.
Dexter blinked.
He let out an awkward smile and spoke.
"I’m home."
Mira continued staring at him without blinking, her crimson eyes boring into his face intensely.
Then she spoke.
"Who is she?"
Dexter’s face filled with genuine confusion.
"Who are you talking about?"
Mira smiled and it was not a warm smile.
"The fourth wife, of course," Mira said.
Dexter swallowed.
"Stop joking. Of course there is no fourth wife. You three are enough for me."
Mira glanced at him.
"Three?" she repeated. "Three is never enough for a man."
She leaned her head forward slightly in her wheelchair.
"Don’t worry. I won’t be angry. Just tell me who she is."
Dexter scratched the back of his head. "I am serious, Mira. There is no one else."
Mira continued staring at him and her expression didn’t soften.
"This is your opportunity to tell me the truth," she said. "I promise I won’t tell the other two girls."
She paused.
"I might even support you in collecting a fourth wife."
Dexter stared at her. "What?"
"Just tell me who she is." Mira tilted her head. "And how was she?"
Dexter frowned. "What do you mean, how was she?
Mira shrugged with exaggerated nonchalance. "Of course I have to ask. How was she compared to us?"
Dexter’s mouth opened. Then closed. Then opened again.
"I have no idea who you are talking about, Mira."
Mira smiled wider.
"Does she have a better figure than me?"
"No," Dexter said immediately. The response was instinctive. Reflexive. The product of a survival instinct that had been honed by three weeks of living with three women.
"Oh, that means she’s prettier than me?"
"No!"
Mira blinked. Then she smirked.
"Oh," she said. "So it was a prostitute."
Dexter pressed his palm against his face.
"Mira. There is no other woman."
Mira stared at him for several seconds. Her expression was unreadable.
"So you’re are saying you didn’t go to see a woman?"
"Dexter immediately shook his head. "Like I told you before I left, I went to see the heroes I fought with and also to get a place for us to live."
Mira nodded her head slowly and then she leaned back in her wheelchair.
"Then why do you smell like another woman?"
Dexter’s face changed slightly.
’This girl is quite perceptive. Didn’t know she had an extraordinary sense of smell!’
His mind raced as it hit him.
Aurora.
She had been sitting in the passenger seat of his SUV for a few minutes. And he had been sitting in that same cabin for the twenty-minute drive home.
He had never expected her scent to linger on him to the extent that Mira would notice.
But Mira had noticed.

Because Mira was not an ordinary person. She was a former A-Rank hero with S-Rank mana affinity. Even with her cultivation sealed and her body crippled, her sensory perception was far beyond that of a normal human.
And she had caught him.
Mira’s smile became even more dangerous.
"Oh, did you think I wouldn’t notice?" she asked. Her voice was sweet. Honeyed.
"You were gone for hours," she continued. "You said you were meeting some heroes.
Dexter replied quickly. "I was."
Mira’s smile widened by a fraction. "So the hero you went to meet was a woman."
It wasn’t a question. It was a conclusion. Delivered with the finality of a judge reading a verdict.
Dexter’s mouth twitched.
’This is getting dangerous.’
He tried again. "There isn’t another woman, Mira."
"So explain this scent," Mira said. Her voice was no longer sweet. It was flat. Direct. The voice of a woman who had moved past the interrogation phase and was now demanding evidence.
Dexter stood in the entryway, as he sighed.
Then he noticed a figure in the corridor.
Lyra was standing at the edge of the hallway, partially hidden by the doorframe.
Her dark eyes were fixed on Dexter as she smiled in amusement. She seemed to be enjoying this.
Dexter took in a deep breath and exhaled slowly.
"What do you know about the Fourth Dimension?"
Mira’s face changed drastically as the dangerous smile on her face vanished as her crimson eyes widened.
"Who told you about the Fourth Dimension?" she asked.
Dexter blinked.

He was surprised by her reaction. Not by the fact that she knew about the Fourth Dimension. He had suspected she might, given her previous status as one of the city’s top heroes. But the intensity of her response surprised him.
Then he told her everything from the beginning.
He didn’t have to as he could have just ignored her told her but then, he chose to tell her everything.
He told her about the squad meeting.About Cole and Blitz and Gridlock and the Tank, about the squad formation and his acceptance.
Then he told her about Aurora.
About how she had followed him to the parking lot, her proposition, the portal, the death place of a Legend Realm expert.
He told her everything and Mira listened quietly.
When Dexter finished, Mira was quiet for a long time.
Then she said something that surprised both of them.
"You could go."
Dexter stared at her.
"I’m sorry?"
"You could go," Mira repeated. "With the speed of your advancement, you will enter the Ultra Realm in a year or two. Maybe sooner. And within five years, you might reach the peak of Ultra Realm."

Mira’s smile widened by a fraction.
"So the hero you went to meet was a woman."
It wasn’t a question.
It was a conclusion.
Delivered with the finality of a judge reading a verdict.
Dexter’s mouth twitched.
’This is getting dangerous.’
He tried again.
"There isn’t another woman, Mira."
"So explain this scent," Mira said.
Her voice was no longer sweet.
It was flat.
Direct.
The voice of a woman who had moved past the interrogation phase and was now demanding evidence.
Dexter stood in the entryway, as he sighed.
Then he noticed a figure in the corridor.
Lyra was standing at the edge of the hallway, partially hidden by the doorframe.
Her dark eyes were fixed on Dexter as she smiled in amusement.
She seemed to be enjoying this.
Dexter took in a deep breath and exhaled slowly.
"What do you know about the Fourth Dimension?"
Mira’s face changed drastically as the dangerous smile on her face vanished as her crimson eyes widened.
"Who told you about the Fourth Dimension?" she asked.
Dexter blinked.
He was surprised by her reaction.
Not by the fact that she knew about the Fourth Dimension.
He had suspected she might, given her previous status as one of the city’s top heroes.
But the intensity of her response surprised him.
Then he told her everything from the beginning.
He didn’t have to as he could have just ignored her told her but then, he chose to tell her everything.
He told her about the squad meeting.About Cole and Blitz and Gridlock and the Tank, about the squad formation and his acceptance.
Then he told her about Aurora.
About how she had followed him to the parking lot, her proposition, the portal, the death place of a Legend Realm expert.
He told her everything and Mira listened quietly.
When Dexter finished, Mira was quiet for a long time.
Then she said something that surprised both of them.
"You could go."
Dexter stared at her.
"I’m sorry?"
"You could go," Mira repeated.
"With the speed of your advancement, you will enter the Ultra Realm in a year or two.
Maybe sooner.
And within five years, you might reach the peak of Ultra Realm."

chapters.title: Chapter 209 | Serious Dexter!
paragraphs: Mira paused.
"But talent alone is not enough to break through from Ultra to Transcendent. "
She looked at him.
"So yes. Eventually, you will have to go. If you want to advance past Ultra, you will need access to something that exists beyond our dimension. That’s just reality."
Dexter blinked. He hadn’t expected this. He had expected Mira to list every reason why he couldn’t leave.
Instead, she was giving him permission.
"But," Mira continued, and her voice hardened, "you are not going with Aurora."
Dexter blinked again. "What?"
"You are not going with Aurora," Mira repeated. Each word was enunciated with the precision of a hammer driving nails.
"But it is Aurora who knows the location of the portal," Dexter said. "She has the map. She has the coordinates. She’s the one organizing the expedition."
Mira’s jaw tightened. Her crimson eyes flashed.
"I don’t care," she said. "You are not going with that woman."
Dexter stared at her. The pieces were falling into place. The jealousy from moments ago.
"Are you jealous?" he asked carefully. "Is there something between you and Aurora? A rivalry?"
Mira snorted coldly.
"Aurora," she said. The name left her lips like something distasteful. "That bitch."
Dexter raised both eyebrows.
"People try comparing her to us, to the three of us. They say she’s the youngest S-Rank. The most talented hero of her generation. The pride of Stargate City."
Her crimson eyes burned.
"That bitch took my place."
"I was the youngest hero in the city’s history," Mira said.
"Then the dungeon happened. And we were crippled. And suddenly, the spotlight needed somewhere else to shine. And there she was. Aurora."

"Nobody would even know her name if it wasn’t for the fact that the three of us were removed from the picture," Mira said. "She got her S-Rank because there was no one left to compete with. The youngest S-Rank? Please."
She glared at Dexter.
"And now she wants to take our husband."
The last sentence came out with a venom that made the air in the entryway feel several degrees warmer.
"Absolutely not," Mira said. "You are not going anywhere with that woman."
Dexter looked at her.
He could argue.
But he didn’t.

"All right, all right," Dexter said, holding up both hands. "I didn’t want to go in the first place. So I won’t go with her. If I ever want to get to the Fourth Dimension, I’ll find another way. Are you satisfied?"
Mira glanced at Dexter.
She blinked, Then she smirked a small, self-satisfied smirk.
But Dexter could see the smile she was trying to suppress.
She was pleased.
Dexter chuckled at her poorly concealed satisfaction. She eqs cute.
"Did you get to eat?" he asked.
Mira shrugged. "I wasn’t hungry."
Dexter’s brows furrowed.
The amusement drained from his face. What replaced it was a cold seriousness.
"You shouldn’t do that," he said.
Mira was a bit surprised by his tone. She looked at him. The playfulness in her expression faded when she saw his face.
"Do what?" she asked.
"Not eat the food I made for you," Dexter said in a calm but firm tone.
"Every meal I make for you girls is very important. Not to me. To you. Every dish is designed to accelerate your recovery."
He held her gaze.
"So you should not skip the food I make. You should always eat. Every time with no exceptions, alright?"
Mira’s brows furrowed at his commanding tone.
She opened her mouth and wanted to instinctively retort but she saw Dexter’s expression and knew he was dead serious.
She blinked and closed her mouth and then nodded her head
"All right," she said. "All right. I will eat the food you make."
"Always," Dexter added.
"Always," Mira repeated, her voice quieter than usual.
Dexter nodded. "Good."
He straightened up from his kneeling position.
"I’ll go set up the table. Come to the dining room in five minutes."
He turned and walked toward the corridor, leaving Mira sitting in her wheelchair with an expression that hovered between annoyed and something she would rather die than identify.
Dexter reached the corridor.
Lyra was gone.
She had been there minutes ago, but the hallway was now empty.
Dexter walked to the girls’ room and pushed the door open.
Lyra was sitting cross-legged on the bed. The Primordial Beast Egg rested in her lap, and her eyes were closed as she cultivated.
Or pretending to cultivate.
Dexter knew better but he didn’t call her out on it.
"I’m back," he said.
Lyra’s eyes remained closed. She nodded once.
Dexter frowned.
"Have you eaten?"
Lyra’s eyes stayed closed. She shook her head.
Dexter’s frown deepened. He projected his thoughts toward her through their telepathic connection, ensuring the message was unmissable.
"Food will be ready in five minutes. Come to the dining room. No room for negotiation."
He didn’t wait for a response and simply closed the door and walked to the backyard.
Selene was on the swing.

Even with the perpetual cold that lived inside her body, the frost that crept beneath her skin and seeped into her bones, she still preferred the outdoors. It was a contradiction that Dexter had noticed but never questioned.

Perhaps the open air helped. Perhaps the breeze carried away some of the cold energy that accumulated around her. Perhaps she simply liked the feeling of space around her, the absence of walls and ceilings, after years of being confined indoors.
She was cultivating. Her silver-white hair hung still around her shoulders. The swing moved gently in the breeze, giving her the appearance of a ghost suspended between earth and sky.
The moment his foot touched the backyard porch, Selene’s head turned toward him. Her Echolocation had detected his approach through the vibrations of his footsteps on the wooden boards.
"You’re back," she said. Her voice was soft and quiet. Aimed roughly in his direction.
Dexter smiled. "Yes. I’m back."
He paused. "Hope everything was all right while I was gone."
"Yes," she said. "Everything was fine."
Dexter nodded. Then asked the question he asked the other two girls.
"Have you eaten?"
Selene blinked. Her pale, sightless eyes widened slightly. Then she slowly shook her head.
Dexter frowned.

He knew she couldn’t see his expression. She was blind. His furrowed brow and tightened jaw were invisible to her. So he did something he rarely did. He let his voice carry the weight that his face couldn’t communicate to her.
"Do you girls only eat when I’m around?"
Selene was silent.

"Food will be ready in two minutes," Dexter continued. "Come and eat immediately. And next time, when I’m not here, you must eat the food I prepare. It’s not just food. It’s medicine. It helps your healing. Every meal is designed to push back the frost inside your body. Skipping them is not an option."
He paused.
"Please make sure to eat. Even when I’m not around."
Selene was slightly stunned by his tone. He didn’t usually speak like this. Not to her.
But tonight he was stern towards her.
She slowly nodded her head and said quietly.
Okay,"
Dexter held his position for a moment longer. Then he exhaled, nodded once, and turned back toward the house.
"Good. Two minutes."
He walked to the kitchen and began plating the food.
He placed the stew into four bowls. Positioned them on the wooden dining table. Placed a spoon beside each bowl. Poured four cups of warm Star-Shaped Leaf tea.
Then he waited.

chapters.title: Chapter 210 | When Will You Perform Your Marital Duties
paragraphs: Mira arrived first.
She parked herself at the table, her crimson eyes scanning the bowls and then, aroma hit her, despite her earlier claim of not being hungry, her nostrils flared at the sweet smell.
Selene arrived second and walked carefully from the backyard and found her chair by memory, her fingers brushing the edge of the table as she sat down with her hands in her lap and waited.
Lyra was surprisingly the last to come as she came out from the bedroom without the Primordial Beast Egg as she walked to the table, sat down.
Dexter sat down at his own seat.
"Lets eat." he said.
They all ate in silence.
As Dexter ate his own portion he observed the girls and noticed something different about Mira.
She was eating slowly and she was still in her first portion. She hadn’t asked for more.
Dexter frowned slightly.
Although this was the second time he was noticing it, it was still unusual. Lyra’s appetite had been massive for weeks.
She ate more than any human being he had ever encountered but now she wasn’t eating like usual.
Dexter discreetly activated his system interface and pulled up Lyra’s status panel.
[Name: Lyra Vance](Switch)
[Shadow Corruption Level: 0%]
The shadow corruption that had been at two percent for days, that the system had warned could reach one hundred percent and transform her body into a portal to the Shadow Realm, was completely gone.
Dexter frowned as the corruption level had reduced all the way to 0 so what was happening?
He checked Mira’s own.
[Name: Mira Calloway]
[Meridian Damage: 65% (Improved: 25% healed)]
[Nerve Regeneration: Right arm fully functional. Left arm: 15% nerve activity detected. Legs: 8% nerve activity detected.]
The Phoenix Heart Elixir, dissolved into the Celestial Dawn Nectar Bowl, had accelerated the repair significantly.
Her left arm was showing early signs of nerve activity. Her legs, while still far from functional, were beginning to respond.
Dexter closed the system interface.
The girls were all making progress and everything he was doing wasn’t wasted.
He placed Lyra behavior at the back of his mind as he continued to eat in silence.
Then, without warning, Dexter felt something.
He raised his head and saw Lyra was staring at him. He wanted to say so thing and then she suddenly smirked mischievously.
Dexter’s spoon paused halfway to his mouth as he stared at Lyra.
’So, husband.’
Lyra raised her head.
Her dark eyes locked onto Dexter across the table.
Her voice resonated through the minds of all three women and Dexter simultaneously.
"When are we going to perform our marital duties?"
The dining table immediately went silent and one could even hear pin drop throughout the entire house.
Mira’s Spectral Arms froze mid-motion, the spoon suspended between the bowl and her mouth.
Selene’s hand stopped halfway to her cup, her fingers hovering in the air.
Dexter, who had been in the middle of drinking a glass of water, felt the liquid travel down the wrong pipe.
"Pfffttt!!!"
He turned his head sharply to the side and spat out a mouthful of water to the side of the table rather than the table, or any of his wives.
He turned back sharply to Lyra as slight redness creeped up his neck.
"Stop speaking nonsense," he said. "What marital duties?"
Lyra’s mysterious smile widened.
"Don’t act as if you haven’t been thinking about it."
Dexter opened his mouth but before he could speak, Lyra’s voice sounded through their minds.
"Three beautiful women in a house with a single man, of course you’ll be tempted."
She tilted her head slightly.
"I don’t blame you. So which of us do you think you will start with? Me? Selene? Or Mira?"
Dexter stared at her.
Then he frowned. If it was Mira who said this, he wouldn’t have been worried but it was Lyra who said this instead.
"Are you okay?" he asked in a concerned tone.
Lyra shrugged. "What do you mean? I’m feeling quite alright.
Dexter frowned deeper. He subtly activated his system interface again, pulling up Lyra’s status panel while maintaining eye contact.
[Name: Lyra Vance](Switch)
[Shadow Corruption Level: 0%]
Dexter blinked.
Switch?
He stared at the word in the bracket beside Lyra’s name. He had never seen this tag before. The system had displayed various mental states for the girls. But he had never seen the world switch.
’What the hell did "switch" mean?’
Dexter closed the interface.
"Finish your food," he said, his voice carrying a firmness that was designed to end the conversation. "Your food is getting cold."
Lyra snorted softly.
"Fine. Don’t answer."
She picked up her spoon.
"But we all know who you will choose first."
Dexter raised an eyebrow despite himself. "Oh? Who do you think I will choose?"
Lyra smirked. "Of course you will choose Mira first."
Mira’s Spectral Arms jerked, causing the spoon to clatter against the rim of the bowl. Selene’s gaze changed slightly and a chill seem to rise through the entire house.
Dexter looked at Lyra for a long moment, then he smirked back.
"What makes you think I wouldn’t choose you first?"
The silence that followed was absolute as all three women stared at him, stunned.
Mira’s crimson eyes went wide and her mouth opened slightly.
Selene’s hand lowered her cup to the table with a soft click as her sightless eyes glanced at Dexter’s direction, and through her Echolocation, she was tracking his heartbeat.
Lyra’s smirk froze on her face as she blinked her eyes rapidly. She had wanted to tease Dexter but hadn’t expected to be teased back.
Dexter then chuckled.
"If you are done with your shenanigans, finish your food, so you can heal up and cultivate. I have to wash the plates and cultivate and deal with some matters."
He returned his attention to his own bowl and resumed eating calmly like what had happened earlier was nothing.
The three women slowly resumed eating as the atmosphere had shifted slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 211 | That’s Lyra
paragraphs: Selene finished her food first.
She placed her spoon neatly beside her bowl, stood up, and drifted toward the backyard without a word.
Mira finished second and also left.
It was obvious theh had been slightly unsettled by what had happened.
Lyra who was always the first to finish was the last to finish this time.
Dexter watched her from across the table, his own bowl long since empty.
’Something is wrong.’
After the other two had left, Dexter turned his attention toward Lyra.
She was still sitting at the table, quietly eating.
Dexter flipped his right hand.
A packet of chips appeared in his palm.
He held it out toward her.
"Do you want some?"
Lyra glanced at the chips.
Then she looked directly at Dexter.
Her expression suddenly changed.
She leaned back, dropped her spoon onto the table, and folded her arms.
"Are you testing me?"
Dexter’s brows furrowed.
A strange feeling settled in his chest.
Testing her?
He deliberately kept his voice casual.
"Testing you? Why would I test you?"
Lyra stared at him for several seconds.
"Why do you think I’m testing you?"
Lyra’s gaze shifted toward the chips before returning to Dexter.
Then she chuckled.
Without another word, she stood up and walked toward the bedroom.
Dexter watched her back disappear through the doorway.
His brows furrowed even deeper.
Something is definitely wrong with her.
He didn’t immediately follow.
Instead, he took a deep breath, collected the girls’ plates, and washed the dishes.
He finished the dishes. Dried his hands. Walked to his room.
He sat on his bed, cross-legged and closed his eyes.
He wanted to cultivate but his mind wouldn’t settle.
He thought about Lyra, the diary, the voice, the "Switch" tag.
He opened his eyes, checked the time. 7:00 PM.
He stood up and walked to the living room.

Mira was in her wheelchair by the window. Cultivating. Her crimson hair caught the last light of the evening, turning it to burnished copper. Her Spectral Arms were folded behind her back, motionless. Her breathing was slow and steady.
"Ready for your massage," Dexter said.
Mira opened her eyes.

In the past, there had always been a beat of hesitation before she agreed. A momentary flash of resistance. Pride battling practicality. The instinct to refuse warring with the knowledge that the massage was helping.
Tonight, there was no hesitation.
She nodded immediately.
The right arm was proof that his efforts were working so she didn’t fight him anymore. Well, not about this.
Dexter wheeled her to the bedroom.
As he pushed the wheelchair through the doorway, he saw Lyra.
She was sitting cross-legged on the bed, the Primordial Beast Egg cradled in her lap. Her eyes were closed as she was cultivating.
She opened her eyes as Dexter and Mira entered and looked at them and she understood what was happening.
All of a sudden, she suddenly smiled warmly as the cold Lyra from the dining room was gone.
She picked up the egg, cradling it carefully against her chest, and slid off the bed. She walked past Dexter, her shoulder brushing his arm as she passed.
’Take care.’
She said in his mind and then she left the room.
Dexter watched her go.
’She’s back to normal uhn?’
He shook his head. The oscillation between her personality was making him think she might have aplit personality or something.
He needed to cook the Harmony Congee. Tomorrow. First thing in the morning. Before anything else happened.
He turned back to Mira.
He lifted her from the wheelchair and placed her on the bed. Face down. He removed her blouse. Unclasped her bra. Draped a towel across her lower back for modesty.
He pulled on the Shockwave Glove. Applied the Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil. Set the vibration to its lowest setting.
He began.

The Massage Sutra guided his hands along the precise pathways of her meridian system. The Shockwave Glove hummed softly against her skin, sending gentle, penetrating vibrations deep into the muscle tissue. The Grade-4 oil seeped into her pores, its medicinal properties working in conjunction with the technique to stimulate nerve regeneration and repair damaged pathways.
He started with her shoulders. Moved to her upper back. Her spine. Her lower back.
The room was quiet. The glove hummed. The oil glistened. Mira’s breathing was slow and even.
Then she spoke.
"Are you spooked?"
Dexter’s hands paused for a fraction of a second. Then resumed.
"What do you mean?"

"Lyra," Mira said. Her voice was muffled by the pillow. Relaxed. The particular tone of someone who was comfortable enough to speak about things that would normally be left unsaid. "She’s been like that for a while."
Dexter’s hands paused again. Longer this time.
"What do you mean, like that?"
Mira turned her head slightly on the pillow. One crimson eye was visible, aimed sideways at nothing in particular.
"She’s been like that from a young age," Mira said. "Don’t be surprised if she behaves a bit unusual around you."
Dexter’s brow furrowed. His hands resumed their mechanical motion, but his mind was no longer on the massage.
"She’s been like this since childhood?"
Mira nodded against the pillow. "Yeah. One minute she can be smiling at you. Warm. Sweet. The kindest person you’ve ever met. And the next minute..."
She paused.
"She can just decide to kill you."
Dexter’s brows furrowed even deeper.
"For no reason at all," Mira continued. "No provocation. No warning. No trigger. Just like a switch."
Dexter stared at the back of Mira’s head.

"Which is why everyone is wary of her," Mira said. "Everyone in the hero community. The Hero Associatio, the Nine Families and even the Villian’s organizations. Nobody dares to cross Lyra Vance. Not because she’s the strongest. But because she’s the most unpredictable."
Dexter chuckled. But the chuckle was hollow. "She’s been alright for the past few weeks. I don’t think it’s like that."
Mira shrugged.
"It was worse three years ago before the dungeon incident."
She paused.
"She was the most troublesome hero in all of Stargate City. Absolutely no one dared to speak, move, or breathe wrong in her presence. She tried dueling with anyone strong. "
"If I and Selene weren’t strong enough, she might have defeated us too."

chapters.title: Chapter 212 | Bloodline Manifestation
paragraphs: Dexter’s hands had stopped moving entirely. He was staring at Mira’s back, his mind struggling to reconcile the image she was painting with the girl who kissed his cheek over chips.
"Luckily, that wasn’t the case," Mira said. "But after the dungeon incident she became less predictable and ..."
Mira searched for the word.
"Quiet."
She exhaled slowly.
"Most people in the city were relieved. Every hero in the city breathed easier because the troublemaker had been neutralized."
Dexter’s throat tightened.
"She has more enemies than me and Selene combined," Mira continued. "Even if you multiplied that combination by two.
She paused again.

"If it weren’t for the fact that the assassins wanted to kill all three of us, I would have suspected the assassins came for Lyra specifically. With the amount of enemies she has made, it would have made more sense."
The room was very quiet.
"But now that she can use mana again and her cultivation is returning..."
She didn’t finish the sentence. She didn’t need to as Dexter understood she she meant.
Dexter frowned. He had only seen the cute side of Lyra, the shy, food-obsessed girl.
Mira seemed to read his thoughts.
"She probably likes you," Mira repeated.
"I suspected you might have died during the first week from unknown circumstances in your sleep."
Dexter sat on the edge of the bed,
’I guess I will have to keep an eye on her.’
Dexter made a quiet decision as his hands worked from Mira’s legs, to her upper thigh.
The glove’s vibration, which he had been gradually increasing throughout the session, was now at a moderate setting as it went through Mira’s internal body.
"Hmm."
Mira suddenly let out a moan which made Dexter’s heart skipped a beat.
The atmosphere in the room froze as the temperature seem to increase
Dexter immediately cleared his throat and chose to think about something else like Lyra as he continued the massage.
He loved upper to Mira’s spine but then, his fingers found something.
Two marks on her shoulder blades. One on each side, unning from the center of each blade downward, tracing a path along the curve of her back before disappearing beneath the towel line.
Dexter’s hands stopped as he frowned. His fingers traced the length of the first mark and it was roughly ten inches long.
The skin was vivid red, the color of fresh inflammation and the marks looked like whip wounds. As though someone had taken a lash to her back, twice, in perfectly symmetrical strokes.
But nobody had touched Mira’s back except him. He had massaged her every day for two weeks. He had seen every inch of her skin. These marks had not been there yesterday.
"Mira," Dexter said, his voice careful. "Did something happen to you while I was gone?"
Mira, face down on the bed, shrugged. "No."
She paused. "Why?"
Another shrug. "Do you think we’re hiding a man in the house?"
Dexter chuckled despite his concern. "You can’t hide a man. Even if you wanted to."
Mira snorted coldly at his mockery. Then she shifted slightly on the bed, adjusting her position as his fingers returned to the marks.
"That kind of hurts," she said suddenly.
body part that had been numb for three years.
She frowned into the pillow. "Is something there?"
"Yes," Dexter said. "Something is there."
Mira’s brow furrowed. "Huh?"
"Oh."
Her expression shifted from confusion to something more introspective. As though she was searching her memory for something she hadn’t thought important until now.
"I had a dream," she said.
Dexter’s fingers paused on the marks.
"Last night," Mira continued. "I had a dream that I had wings. A pair of wings ripped out from my back. And I flew through the air like a phoenix or dragon. I’m not sure."
"The pain of the wings ripping through my back felt very real," she said. "I could feel the skin tearing, the muscles stretching. The bones pushing outward. It was...
She trailed off.
"And it is at that exact spot you are touching."
Dexter stared at the two marks and his mind went to two words.
’Bloodline Awakening.’
He had given all three girls the Bloodline Evolution Crystal weeks ago and had expected them to awaken their bloodlines relatively quickly, given the pace of their other improvements.
But the bloodline hadn’t awakened. Not for Mira. Not for Lyra. Not for Selene. Weeks had passed, and the system had shown no indication that the Bloodline Evolution Crystal had taken effect.
Dexter had begun to wonder if the crystal was defective. Or if the girls’ damaged bodies were unable to process the crystal’s energy while their meridians were still shattered.
Now he had his answer.
The awakening was happening but it was happening. The marks on Mira’s back were the physical manifestation of a bloodline trying to emerge.
Wings.

The dream, the pain, the marks, all of it pointed to the same conclusion. Whatever bloodline the Evolution Crystal was granting Mira, it involved wings and probably a phoenix bloodline, or something similar.

And the process was underway. Her body was changing at a cellular level, the dormant bloodline genes being activated and integrated into her physical structure. The marks were the first visible sign. The dream was the first conscious experience of the transformation.
’It won’t be long now. A month. Maybe two. The bloodline will fully manifest.’
Mira chuckled softly into the pillow.
"This kind of feels like bloodline awakening," she said. The chuckle was self-deprecating.
Then she shook her head against the pillow.
"No one in our family has ever awakened a bloodline, in the entire history of the Calloway family. We are talented and strong but we have never been a bloodline family."
She paused.
"It would be nice, though. If I actually awakened one. We might have had the strength to rival those top three families. The Ashfords. The Sterlings. The Montclairs."
"But it’s impossible, right?"
