chapters.title: Chapter 213 | Matter Of Time
paragraphs: Dexter’s hands resumed their motion as he continued the massage, working around the marks carefully to avoid direct contact with the sensitive areas while still channeling mana into the surrounding tissue.
"Nothing is impossible," he said in a casual tone. "What would happen if I actually managed to awaken a bloodline?" He asked.
Mira was silent for a while, then she shook her head.
"There is no need Imagining the impossible. Sticking to reality is better."
She paused.
"I am already happy by the fact that I can finally move my right hand. And I am healing. Every day, I feel a little stronger and that is enough."
"Asking for a bloodline would be asking for too much."
Dexter smiled knowingly.
He knew because he had given them the bloodline. The Bloodline Evolution food, quietly integrated into their bodies weeks ago. It was only a matter of time.
He was looking forward to it, looking forward to the moment when all three women discovered their talent.
The looks on their faces would be worth it.
He massaged Mira every day and saw her skin. He could detect the subtle changes in her body that signaled the bloodline’s emergence.
He didn’t massage Lyra or Selene.
He had no way of knowing what was happening beneath their skin and no way of monitoring the progress of a transformation that might already be underway without their knowledge.
This thought led to another thought.
The body massage Sutra wasn’t just a relaxation technique. It stimulated meridian function and accelerated the body’s natural healing processes.
If he applied the same technique to Selene and Lyra, their healing rates would increase dramatically.
But how could he tell two women, one of whom was blind and the other deaf and mute, that he wanted to rub oil on their bodies and press vibrating gloves against their skin?
How could he frame it in a way that didn’t make him sound like a pervert who just wanted to touch them and want satisfied with just touching one of them.
’I want to rub oil on your body and press vibrating gloves against your skin. Strictly for medical purposes, I promise.’
No version of that sentence existed that didn’t make him sound like a pervert.
He glanced at Mira, then an idea formed.
He could tell Mira and then if she agreed, she could communicate the proposal to Selene and Lyra.
Dexter turned to Mira.
"How would you feel if I started giving Selene and Lyra massages?"
The question landed in the quiet bedroom like a stone in still water.
Mira’s eyes opened.
"The massage technique I use on you," Dexter continued, "It stimulates healing at a cellular level, accelerates the body’s natural recovery process."
He paused.
"If I apply the same technique to Selene and Lyra, their healing rates would increase significantly."
He looked at Mira.

"In a month or two, Selene might show improvement in her vision, Lyra might show improvement in her hearing and by the end of the year, both of them could be significantly further along in their recovery than they would be without the massages."
The room suddenly went silent and in that instant, the temperature in the room increased drastically
Dexter’s eyes widened as he looked at her. Her eyes were closed and her expression was normal but Dexter could feel waves of incredible heat radiating off of her like a lava.
But in that split second, the rising temperature returned to normal as though it had been an illusion.
Mira then shrugged.
"They are also your wives," she said in a light tone. "You can do whatever you want to them."
Dexter blinked.
The words were fine as she acknowledged what he said, but Dexter’s spine tingled.
The brief, flash-fast spike in temperature that had originated from her body and disappeared before it could be confirmed.
’She is angry.’
And it was the quiet type of anger!
She was jealous.

The jealousy of a woman who had something that was hers, a daily ritual, a private intimacy, a shared moment between husband and wife that nobody else was part of, and was now being told that this thing might be shared with others.
The massage was not just a medical procedure to Mira. It was the one part of her day that was exclusively hers. The time when Dexter’s attention was focused entirely on her.
And now he was proposing to extend that same intimacy to the other two.
Dexter understood it Immediately and sighed.
’I mess up again, didn’t I?’
Each wife had something that was uniquely theirs. A specific form of interaction that defined their relationship with him and separated it from their relationships with each other.
With Lyra, it was food. Snacks. Chips. Pastries. The small, edible gifts that made her eyes light up and her lips curve into brilliant smiles.
With Selene, it was warmth. The nightly cultivation sessions.
With Mira, it was the massage.
Each of these was sacred.
Sharing them across all three would dilute it.
The massage might increase the other two’s healing rates. That was true.
But logic was not the only operating principle in a household of three women and one man. Sometimes, preserving the emotional ecosystem was more important than optimizing the physical one.

The girls already had the Grand Cosmos Scripture. They didn’t need meridians to cultivate. Their Star Nodes were absorbing mana independently. The massage’s primary function, meridian stimulation, was largely redundant for them. Its secondary function, general healing acceleration, was helpful but not critical.
The benefit was incremental. The cost was disruption and it was not worth it.
Maybe later. When things had settled. When the bloodline awakenings were further along he would try again.
But not today.
Dexter shook his head.
"Never mind," he said. "I was just thinking out loud. Forget I said anything."
Mira’s eyes remained closed. Her expression remained neutral. The temperature in the room remained normal.
But something in the quality of her silence shifted.
The rest of the massage proceeded in silence.

Mira didn’t speak a single word or a complaint. She lay on the bed and accepted the massage with the passive, closed-eyed stillness of a woman who was processing something internally and did not wish to be disturbed while doing so.
When it was done, Dexter cleaned the oil from her skin, dressed her, and placed her in her wheelchair.
"Thank you," she said without looking at him and wheeled herself out of the room.
Her Spectral Arms operated the wheels, carrying her down the hallway and into the living room without a backward glance.
Dexter stood in the bedroom doorway and watched her go.
’She’s definitely angry.’
He shook his head.
’Definitely behaving like a jealous cat.’
Dexter found this simultaneously exasperating and endearing.
Dexter shook his head again and walked to his room.
He cleaned up andcultivated for an hour,
After an hour, he opened his eyes and stretched. The tension from the day’s events faded and he stood up and walked to the kitchen.

It was late, nearly eight o’clock. The girls had eaten a substantial meal at five, so a heavy dinner wasn’t necessary. But they needed something before bed. A light meal that would provide sustained nourishment through the night without overwhelming their digestive systems.

He prepared a simple rice porridge. Plain. Gentle. Easy on the stomach. He added a thin slice of ginseng root for warmth and a handful of goji berries for their restorative properties. No mana infusion. No special techniques. Just good, simple food that would sit well in a body that was already processing the day’s accumulated spiritual energy.
He ladled the porridge into four bowls and called the girls.
They came.
Mira arrived first.
She ate quickly and finished before the others and then, she wheeled herself away from the table without a word and headed for the window in the living room..
Dexter watched her go.
’Yep. Still angry.’

"What would happen if I actually managed to awaken a bloodline?" He asked.
Mira was silent for a while, then she shook her head.
"There is no need Imagining the impossible.
Sticking to reality is better."
She paused.
"I am already happy by the fact that I can finally move my right hand.
And I am healing.
Every day, I feel a little stronger and that is enough."
"Asking for a bloodline would be asking for too much."
Dexter smiled knowingly.
He knew because he had given them the bloodline.
The Bloodline Evolution food, quietly integrated into their bodies weeks ago.
It was only a matter of time.
He was looking forward to it, looking forward to the moment when all three women discovered their talent.
The looks on their faces would be worth it.
He massaged Mira every day and saw her skin.
He could detect the subtle changes in her body that signaled the bloodline’s emergence.
He didn’t massage Lyra or Selene.
He had no way of knowing what was happening beneath their skin and no way of monitoring the progress of a transformation that might already be underway without their knowledge.
This thought led to another thought.
The body massage Sutra wasn’t just a relaxation technique.
It stimulated meridian function and accelerated the body’s natural healing processes.
If he applied the same technique to Selene and Lyra, their healing rates would increase dramatically.
But how could he tell two women, one of whom was blind and the other deaf and mute, that he wanted to rub oil on their bodies and press vibrating gloves against their skin?
How could he frame it in a way that didn’t make him sound like a pervert who just wanted to touch them and want satisfied with just touching one of them.
’I want to rub oil on your body and press vibrating gloves against your skin.
Strictly for medical purposes, I promise.’
No version of that sentence existed that didn’t make him sound like a pervert.
He glanced at Mira, then an idea formed.
He could tell Mira and then if she agreed, she could communicate the proposal to Selene and Lyra.
Dexter turned to Mira.
"How would you feel if I started giving Selene and Lyra massages?"
The question landed in the quiet bedroom like a stone in still water.
Mira’s eyes opened.
"The massage technique I use on you," Dexter continued, "It stimulates healing at a cellular level, accelerates the body’s natural recovery process."
He paused.
"If I apply the same technique to Selene and Lyra, their healing rates would increase significantly."
He looked at Mira.

"In a month or two, Selene might show improvement in her vision, Lyra might show improvement in her hearing and by the end of the year, both of them could be significantly further along in their recovery than they would be without the massages."
The room suddenly went silent and in that instant, the temperature in the room increased drastically
Dexter’s eyes widened as he looked at her.
Her eyes were closed and her expression was normal but Dexter could feel waves of incredible heat radiating off of her like a lava.
But in that split second, the rising temperature returned to normal as though it had been an illusion.
Mira then shrugged.
"They are also your wives," she said in a light tone.
"You can do whatever you want to them."
Dexter blinked.
The words were fine as she acknowledged what he said, but Dexter’s spine tingled.
The brief, flash-fast spike in temperature that had originated from her body and disappeared before it could be confirmed.
’She is angry.’
And it was the quiet type of anger!
She was jealous.

The jealousy of a woman who had something that was hers, a daily ritual, a private intimacy, a shared moment between husband and wife that nobody else was part of, and was now being told that this thing might be shared with others.
The massage was not just a medical procedure to Mira.
It was the one part of her day that was exclusively hers.
The time when Dexter’s attention was focused entirely on her.
And now he was proposing to extend that same intimacy to the other two.
Dexter understood it Immediately and sighed.
’I mess up again, didn’t I?’
Each wife had something that was uniquely theirs.
A specific form of interaction that defined their relationship with him and separated it from their relationships with each other.
With Lyra, it was food.
Snacks.
Chips.
Pastries.
The small, edible gifts that made her eyes light up and her lips curve into brilliant smiles.
With Selene, it was warmth.
The nightly cultivation sessions.
With Mira, it was the massage.
Each of these was sacred.
Sharing them across all three would dilute it.
The massage might increase the other two’s healing rates.
That was true.
But logic was not the only operating principle in a household of three women and one man.
Sometimes, preserving the emotional ecosystem was more important than optimizing the physical one.
The girls already had the Grand Cosmos Scripture.
They didn’t need meridians to cultivate.
Their Star Nodes were absorbing mana independently.
The massage’s primary function, meridian stimulation, was largely redundant for them.
Its secondary function, general healing acceleration, was helpful but not critical.
The benefit was incremental.
The cost was disruption and it was not worth it.
Maybe later.
When things had settled.
When the bloodline awakenings were further along he would try again.
But not today.
Dexter shook his head.
"Never mind," he said.
"I was just thinking out loud.
Forget I said anything."
Mira’s eyes remained closed.
Her expression remained neutral.
The temperature in the room remained normal.
But something in the quality of her silence shifted.
The rest of the massage proceeded in silence.
Mira didn’t speak a single word or a complaint.
She lay on the bed and accepted the massage with the passive, closed-eyed stillness of a woman who was processing something internally and did not wish to be disturbed while doing so.
When it was done, Dexter cleaned the oil from her skin, dressed her, and placed her in her wheelchair.
"Thank you," she said without looking at him and wheeled herself out of the room.
Her Spectral Arms operated the wheels, carrying her down the hallway and into the living room without a backward glance.
Dexter stood in the bedroom doorway and watched her go.
’She’s definitely angry.’
He shook his head.
’Definitely behaving like a jealous cat.’
Dexter found this simultaneously exasperating and endearing.
Dexter shook his head again and walked to his room.
He cleaned up andcultivated for an hour,
After an hour, he opened his eyes and stretched.
The tension from the day’s events faded and he stood up and walked to the kitchen.
It was late, nearly eight o’clock.
The girls had eaten a substantial meal at five, so a heavy dinner wasn’t necessary.
But they needed something before bed.
A light meal that would provide sustained nourishment through the night without overwhelming their digestive systems.
He prepared a simple rice porridge.
Plain.
Gentle.
Easy on the stomach.
He added a thin slice of ginseng root for warmth and a handful of goji berries for their restorative properties.
No mana infusion.
No special techniques.
Just good, simple food that would sit well in a body that was already processing the day’s accumulated spiritual energy.
He ladled the porridge into four bowls and called the girls.
They came.
Mira arrived first.
She ate quickly and finished before the others and then, she wheeled herself away from the table without a word and headed for the window in the living room..
Dexter watched her go.
’Yep.
Still angry.’

chapters.title: Chapter 214 | Others Had Died With That Gaze
paragraphs: Mira arrived first.
She ate quickly and to Dexter’s shock, she finished before the others and then wheeled herself away from the table without a word and headed for the window in the living room.
Dexter watched her go.
’Yep. Still angry.’
Dexter frowned angrily. ’While I understand that she might be jealous, she’s well aware I didn’t marry just her right?’

He has tried to be understanding to the girls to the extent that others in his situation might even call him a whimp. But Dexter had suffered from his family which was why he was considerate to the girls because they had also being bullied by their own families.
But enough is enough. If he kept on keeping quiet, they would think he’s a real push over while he’s just trying his best to understand them.
Fine, they were the pride and talent of the city but now, it’s a different case.
Dexter who was thinking about this suddenly paused as he heard Lyra’s voice spoke in his mind.
’D-Dexter, c-can I have... more.’
Even till now, she was still hesitant about asking for more.
Dexter’s mind calmed a bit because as a Food smith, he felt quite proud when others ask for more of his food.
"Of course. Give me a second."
Dexter smiled as he went to bring more meals for her.
And just like that, much to Dexter’s surprise, Lyra actually ate eight portions.
Thankfully, he had been prepared ahead of time and had prepared extra meals.
But even his precautions hadn’t been enough and by the eighth portion, the supply was running so low that he had to give her half of his own bowl to satisfy the final round.
She ate it with a all with a smile as then stared as Dexter with a gaze Dexter hadn’t seen in a long time.
’What was that?’
He had seen that gaze in other’s face but only one had lived till now while the others had died.
And now, he was seeing that gaze in another’s person.
’I’m probably wrong.’
Dexter stood at the sink as he started washing the plates.
"Bang Bang Bang"
Three sharp knocks at the gate.
’Who?’
Dexter’s Enhanced Hearing activated and in a split second, he identified the heartbeat before the third knock landed.
It was Tessa.
He dried his hands and walked to the gate.
In his way, he saw Mira was in the living room and was cultivating by the window.
She didn’t look up nor did she acknowledge his movement when he walked by like she sometimes does.
She was definitely still sulking and Dexter at this moment was alredy tired of it.
Dexter sighed and walked out of the house and then opened the gate.
Tessa stood on the other side with her usually smile on her face. Her curly red hair bounced in the evening breeze as her green eyes sparkled at the sight of him.
Suddenly, she tilted her head as the grin on her face faded slightly and was replaced by a curious look on her face.
"You’re in a bad mood," she said without question.
Dexter was a bit surprised but he simply shrugged. "Not particularly. How are you doing and how were sales today?"
The word "sales" was the magic incantation and Tessa’s grin returned instantly.
"Sales were fantastic!" she declared. "Way more customers than we expected. Some people came specifically to order your meals in batches this time."
"We sold the first thirty portions at the standard price in under eight hours. Then, for the remaining twenty portions, I even had to increase the price."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Increased it to what?"
"Eight thousand Dollars per portion."
Dexter stared at her.
"Eight thousand?"

"Eight thousand," Tessa said with a proud smile on her face. "The demand was so high that people were willing to pay double. I sold the last twenty portions at eight thousand each, and every single one was gone before closing."
She crossed her arms and tilted her chin upward.
"I’m smart, aren’t I?"
Dexter chuckled at her smartness and her cuteness.
"Yes, yes," he said. "You are definitely very smart."
And Dexter wasn’t even kidding. She had identified a supply-demand imbalance in real time, adjusted pricing on the fly, and maximized revenue without losing a single customer.
In a few years, with the right resources and guidance, Tessa was definitely going to be a force to be reckoned with in the business world.
Tessa pulled out her phone and transferred the day’s earnings to Dexter’s account.
Dexter’s phone buzzed and he checked the notification.
[Transfer received: 340,000 Dollars]
The number pushed his account balance back toward the seven-figure mark. The one million he had lost to Marcus’s scam was slowly being rebuilt.
Dexter smiled in relief. ’In no time, I should be able to recover.’
At that moment, Tessa’s expression suddenly shifted as her gaze turned serious.
"I heard about something happening today," she said casually. "In the city."
Dexter looked at her curious about what she was about to say.
"Harvest Homes was actually attacked by an angry customer," Tessa continued in a light but casual tone.
"It wa said that someone actually sent an executive of Harvest Homes flying out of the building with one punch."
"It was even said that if the executive wasn’t an Ultra Realm expert, they probably would have died from falling twenty-four floors."
Dexter’s expression didn’t change much but he raise an eyebrow of surprise and spoke.
"Really? That’s insane."
Tessa nodded and continued.
"The news tried to get information from Harvest Homes but they denied everything and even refused to share any details about the incident. It was really strange."
"Don’t you think that’s weird?"
Dexter stared at Tessa as he thought in his mind.
’Why is she telling me this specifically?’
Harvest Homes wasn’t the only incident in the city today as Stargate City was a metropolis of millions and things happened every day. Crimes, accidents, hero interventions, monster sightings.
But Tessa had chosen to tell him about this specific incident out of everything that had happened in the city today.
Which meant one of two things. Either she was making conversation and this was the most interesting thing she had heard today. Or she knew something.

chapters.title: Chapter 215 | Want to Try Something...
paragraphs: Dexter’s face remained impassive.
"What is Harvest Homes?" he asked. His voice carried the perfect blend of ignorance and disinterest. "Some kind of store? And why would it be my business either way?"
Then he shrugged and changed the subject smoothly.
"How many containers did you bring this time?"
Tessa gazed at Dexter for what seem to be an uncomfortable about if time before she suddenly smiled and spoke.
"I brought one hundred this time," she said.
Dexter was stunned.
"One hundred?"

"One hundred," Tessa confirmed, hefting two large bags onto the gate post. "Customers have already pre-ordered twenty meals for tomorrow. So one hundred is the minimum to make enough sales for the day."
Dexter blinked.
One hundred portions was a bit much and required even more preparations.
Which meant waking up at 3 AM instead of 5.
He sighed.
"Alright then," he said, accepting the bags. "I guess I’ll have to wake up very early tomorrow morning."
Tessa grinned. Then her expression turned soft.
"So," she said. "Have you made your decision about the festival? It’s next tomorrow, you know."
Dexter looked at her and frowned. He had almost forgotten about the festival and wouldn’t have gone if the girls hadn’t decided to come.
"Alright. I’ll come."
The smile that broke across Tessa’s face was astonishing as dimples lit up in her cheeks, and radiated outward with enough warmth to melt the sun itself.
"Perfect!" she squealed. "I can’t wait to introduce you to the other neighbors!"
Dexter held up a warning finger.
"Don’t get any ideas."
Tessa placed both hands over her heart with exaggerated innocence. "Of course not. I’m a very good girl."
Dexter snorted. "Good night, Tessa.
"Good night, Dexter!"
She chuckled and then turned back and Dexter watched as she skipped down the sidewalk as she waved at him.
Dexter closed the gate and then locked it as he back inside.
Mira was still in the parlor, cultivating and even when he walked past her, she didn’t say anything like she always did.

He didn’t say anything as he entered the kitchen and placed the bags of containers on the counter, organized them neatly, and confirmed that he had sufficient ingredients in his spatial storage to produce one hundred portions of Grade One Enchanted Meal.

Then he walked to his room, closed the door, and sat cross-legged on his bed as he began cultivating the mana hurricane around his house was starting to erupt when suddenly a ding rang out in his mind.
’Finally! The system notification.’
He was a bit excited about it because with more power, he could oppress his enemies which he silent increased after today and maybe when the Ashford family might come after him this time.
’[Ding!]
The notification materialized in his mind as a golden text hovered in the darkness behind his closed eyelids.
He was about to read it when he heard footsteps drectly in front of his door.
Dexter’s Enhanced Hearing focused and he isolated the heartbeat. Then he realized that heartbeat was familiar but also not familiar.
He knew Lyra’s heartbeat as he heard it every day as he knew it the way he knew his own pulse. Intimately.

This heartbeat was close to Lyra’s and had the same base rhythm and the same general pattern. But there were subtle differences that even confused Dexter. It was faster than usual.m this time, faster than when Lyra had always been nervous to asked for extra meals.
It was Lyra’s heartbeat and also not quite.

Dexter’s hand moved toward his spatial storage. His fingers twitched, ready to summon the Void Star Saber at a moment’s notice but then the scent reached him and he immediately knew who it was. At that split second, the door suddenly opened.
A tall, dark-haired woman stepped into the room. As she stepped into the room, she turnd and then closed the door behind her.
Then she suddenly turned around and to Dexter’s confirmation, it was Lyra.
Dexter smiled as he projected his thoughts to her.
"Is something the matter? Do you need something?"
Lyra nodded, then she shook her head and then nodded again.
Dexter was confused but then he smile as he fliped his hand and a chip oppress in his hand.
Lyra quickly end forward as she snatched it in her hands.
She at on his bed and started to eat it but then she passed as she stared at Dexter.
"Do you want more or do you need something?"
"I..." Lyra’s telepathic voice stuttered. The tremor was back. Stronger than before. "I want to try something."
Dexter blinked. "What do you want to try?"
Lyra’s blush deepened and she looked down at the chips in her lap in embarrassment as her fingers tightened around the bag, crinkling the plastic.
Then she shook her head.
"No, nothing, forget it."
She reached for another chip and began eating again but even faster this time.
Dexter watched her for a moment then he flipped his hand and a Celestial Pastry appeared as he held it out toward her.
Lyra saw the pastry and her eyes widened as she looked at the pastry then at Dexter, then at the pastry again.
And with speed even shockjng to Dexter, she snatched it from his hand with the speed of a striking cobra.
Then she looked at him with a deep blush spreading from her cheeks to her ears to the visible skin above the collar of her shirt.
"I wanted to try this," she said.
She placed the chips on the bed beside her. Both hands free as she straightened her posture and drew in a breath.
"You’ve been so good to me," she said. Her telepathic voice was barely above a whisper. "And I feel I should do something for you."
In in that split second, she leaned forward.

Dexter’s mind processed the approaching motion. He expected her lips to touch his cheek. The same gesture she had performed that morning in the kitchen, when the chips and pastries had overwhelmed her gratitude and her body had acted before her brain could intervene.

A cheek kiss. That was what he was preparing for. A brief, warm, slightly awkward press of lips against skin that would leave him flustered and her blushing and both of them pretending it hadn’t happened.
Her lips didn’t touch his cheek.
They touched his lips.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
His entire body went into shock like what was actually happening was an hallucination instead as his heart skipped two solid beats!

That was what he was preparing for.
A brief, warm, slightly awkward press of lips against skin that would leave him flustered and her blushing and both of them pretending it hadn’t happened.
Her lips didn’t touch his cheek.
They touched his lips.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
His entire body went into shock like what was actually happening was an hallucination instead as his heart skipped two solid beats!

chapters.title: Chapter 216 | Who Are You!?
paragraphs: The warmth started in his chest, spreading outward through his neck, across his face and unto his lips, which were still pressed against Lyra’s, lips.
Without his instruction. Hus hands rose from the bed as it found her cheeks.
It was warm and softer than he had expected from the bed and found the side of Lyra’s face.
’Is this okay?’
Dexter suddenly asked but at that moment, Lyra leaned into his hand as she pressed her cheek against his palm.
’Yes.’
The moment she said this, the kiss went even deeper as the two lips entangled even further than the French kiss.
Lyra’s fingers slid through his hair as she gradually pulled him even closer, consuming his lips like a predator.
In that split second, something sparked in the back of Dexter’s mind. But before it could register itself, the warm sensation form the kiss overwhelmed Dexter’s mind.
Even when the sensation worked through his body, Dexter almsot didn’t feel it. Who in their right mind would ignore a top beauty kiss!?
His hand rose and unconsciously found Lyra’s waist as he pulled her closer.

In that split second, Lyra moved forward, even closer to Dexter as she suddenly shifted her body and then landed on Dexter’s lap as her legs folded on either side of his crossed knees. Her weight settled onto his lap and her arms wrapped around his neck.
In that moment, she kissed him deeper.
And in that split second, the spark in the back of his mind flared again.
’Is something wrong?’
The thought was vague but immediately vanished as he thought about it.

Then the Tranquility Band on his wrist suddenly activated as a wave of cool, soothing energy radiated from the band into Dexter’s wrist, traveling up his arm and into his brain like ice water being splashed into his brain.
In that split second, the fog lifted and his brain started to work and everything connected in that split second.
The kiss was real, the body, the lips and everything else law but the person behind them...
"Bang!"
Dexter’s activated Flame Burst Step and his body blurred, as he flashed away from the bed and glared at the figure on the bed.
Lyra still sat on the bed where he had left her and her face was of pure genuine confusion.
"What?" she said.
The telepathic voice trembled. "What happened? Why?"
She was incredibly confused and her eyes started to turn teary and she was very hurt.
Just now, she had just shared an incredible kiss with Dexter a few seconds ago and now Dexter had actually recoiled away as though it worst thing he had ever felt.
She looked genuinely hurt. And when Dexter saw this, his heart pounded.
But Dexter’s clarity had not faded and he glared at Lyra as he suddenly spoke.
"You are not Lyra, are you?"
Lyra blinked in confusion as she stared at him.

"What do you mean by that?"Her telepathic voice continued to sound so sweet it was almost identical. "We just kissed and now you’re denying me? Is it because of Mira and Selene? You can tell me if that’s the case."
"Don’t bring them into this," Dexter immediately snapped. "You are not Lyra. Who are you?"
His voice resonated through the entire room as he stared at Lyra indifferently.
Lyra’s face which was confused suddenly turned even more pitiful at Dexter’s words.
But even after seeing this, Dexter still stared at her coldly.
The room turned silent for a almost a minute and then strangely, Lyra’s lips suddenly lifted up until it formed an amused smirk on her face.
Sha gently stood up from the bed touched the corner of her mouth with one finger as she said in a thoughtful tone.
"That’s quite strange."she said."
The voice was cold and the telepathic voice had changed. It wasn’t as sweet as it had always sounded. Even when Lyra was mad, she didn’t sound like that!
"I behaved eaacvrly like she would. But you still noticed. But don’t you think it was a little too late?" she continued.
"You already kissed me."
She tilted her head.
"Or should I say, you just sexually assaulted Lyra? You kissed her without her permission in the first place"
Dexter’s blood ran cold and his face turned extremely cold as his saber instantly materialized in his hand.
The dark blade hummed as it drank the light around it as he pointed the blade at the strange Lyra.
"If you don’t speak this instant, I will make you speak."
Lyra looked at the blade and then she looked at him and suddenly laughed.
The sweet laugh echoed in Dexter’s mind and it was even colder than before.
"What are you going to do?"she asked. "Kill me?"
She tilted her head again as her smirk widened.
"Kill her?"
"Come," she said, spreading her arms wide."Try it if you dare."
Dexter’s grip on the saber tightened. His knuckles went white. He had never expected this circumstance to happen and didn’t even think it was possible in real life.
But he didn’t move because that strange Lyra was right.
He couldn’t kill her because the body standing in front of him was Lyra’s body. The incredibly cute and sweet girl and if he struck, it would directly affect Lyra!
The entity wearing Lyra’s body knew this and she chuckled seeing the struggle on Dexter’s face.
Suddenly, Dexter’s face relaxed and he shook his head with a small smile on hhs face.
"There are other things I can do apart from killing," he said.
The entity raised an eyebrow.
"Oh?" The telepathic voice carried amusement. "What other things? You just kissed me with your tongue, so what other things can you do to me? Besides kissing me again, I mean, I wouldn’t object."
Dexter’s jaw tightened, the saber hummed in his grip as the Ancient Flame Demon Bloodline stirred. In that split second, massive heat radiated from his skin rapidly as the air around him shimmered.
But the entity didn’t flinch.

chapters.title: Chapter 217 | Aurelyx
paragraphs: Dexter continued staring at Lyra with a frosty look on his face.
"Tch...boring."
Lyra clicked her tongue and rolled her eyes and then smirked.
"You can call me Aurelyx.
Dexter stared at her as his heart squeezed tightly. It was even more serious than he feared, it was a whole other personality and it even has a name.
Dexter’s aura started to leak out of his body as killing intent flashed in his mind.
"What the fuck are you doing in Lyra’s body?"
Aurelyx laughed and it sounded sinister and sweet at the same time in Dexter’s mind.
"Lyra?" she repeated. "Lyra’s body?"
She tilted her head.
"What makes you think this is Lyra’s body and not my body?"
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
Then he grinned coldly.
"Do you think you can manipulate me?" he said. "If it wasn’t Lyra’s body, you would be called Lyra. You would be the one with the name, and she would be the one who had to invent one for herself."
He held her gaze.
"But she is called Lyra. And you had to name yourself Aurelyx. You named yourself because you’re the addition."
Aurelyx’s eyes flashed coldly.
Then she smiled.

"Now I get why Lyra likes you," she said. "I assumed she liked you because you give her food. That’s what I thought. Chips and pastries and six-bowl stews. Simple transactional affection. Feed the hungry girl and she follows you home."
She paused.
"But it’s different, isn’t it? She likes you because you see things. You notice what other people don’t. You pay attention."
Her eyes held his.
"That’s dangerous. For someone like me."
Dexter didn’t acknowledge the compliment. He didn’t acknowledge the threat. He simply stood there, saber still in his hand but lowered to his side, and spoke.
"What do you want?"
Aurelyx shrugged. Lyra’s shoulders. Lyra’s movement. But the casualness was exaggerated. Performed. The shrug of someone who was very deliberately trying to appear relaxed.
"I don’t want anything."
"Then what do you mean by kissing me?"

The question was blunt. Uncomfortable. The kind of question that most people would circle around with diplomatic language and careful phrasing. Dexter didn’t bother. He wanted a straight answer and he was going to get one.
Aurelyx’s expression didn’t change.
"Why can’t I just kiss you because I like you?"
Dexter’s grin faded as his expression hardened.
"State your true intentions," he said. "Do you really believe I can do nothing to restrain you? Do you truly believe I have no means of dealing with you?"

The threat was not explicit. It didn’t need to be. The Void Star Saber humming at his side was explicit enough. The Ancient Flame Demon Bloodline radiating heat from his skin was explicit enough. The fact that he had just fought an Ultra Realm expert to a standstill earlier that afternoon was explicit enough.
Aurelyx gazed into his eyes.
She was searching. Reading. Analyzing the micro-expressions and the mana fluctuations and the subtle, almost imperceptible signals that told her whether the man in front of her was bluffing or not.

She had been watching him for weeks. Through Lyra’s eyes. Through Lyra’s ears. Through Lyra’s brain. She had observed the way he moved, the way he fought, the way he made decisions. She had catalogued his abilities, his resources, his patterns.

She knew about the Seventh-Tier cultivation technique he had given the girls. A technique that shouldn’t exist. That was beyond anything any family in the city possessed. That had no business being in the hands of a disowned bastard with an F-Rank mana affinity.
She knew about the Type-3 weapons he had placed in their room. Weapons that had since been swapped for something even more powerful, though she hadn’t yet determined what.
She knew he had means. Connections. Resources. A background that didn’t match his public profile.
She also knew that he was serious. Right now, in this moment, he was not playing. He was not negotiating. He was demanding.
She smiled.
"You’re quite boring, you know that?" she said.
Dexter didn’t respond.

"Others would have taken advantage of this," she continued. Her voice carried a trace of genuine bewilderment, as though she was describing behavior she had encountered in others and found incomprehensible. "Others would have taken advantage of this opportunity. A beautiful woman enters their room at night. Locks the door. Sits on their bed. Kisses them."
She spread her hands.
"But you? You’re behaving like a cute, innocent virgin boy. Others would have slept with me by now. But you..."
She frowned.
"Annoying."
Dexter’s expression didn’t waver.
"Speak," he said coldly.
Aurelyx stared at him for a long moment. Then she sighed.
"Fine," she said. "I was teasing you. That’s all."
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
"You just wanted to tease me. So you decided to kiss a stranger instead."
"That’s a lie, isn’t it?" he added.
Aurelyx rolled her eyes.
"Fine," she said again. "It’s about your heavenly physique."
Dexter’s heart skipped a beat.
But his face didn’t change.
"What heavenly physique?" he said in a puzzled tone.
"I have no idea what you are talking about."
Aurelyx sneered.
"Now you are denying," she said. "You should learn to lie better."
Dexter’s expression remained blank. "I truly have no idea what you are talking about."
Aurelyx rolled her eyes again. Harder this time. More exasperated.
"Fine," she said for the third time. The response of someone who was accustomed to getting their way through persistence and was running out of patience with a man who refused to play along.
"If you won’t admit you have a heavenly physique, then I won’t tell you what I plan to do."
She turned away.
The movement was abrupt. Final. The kind of turn that signaled the end of a conversation rather than a pause in one. She walked to the door, unlocked it, and pulled it open.

Dexter stood in the center of the room, watching her go. His mind was still processing. Still analyzing. Still trying to determine how much she actually knew and how much she was guessing and whether the gap between the two was wide enough to be safe.
She stepped through the doorway. Paused.
Without turning back, she spoke one final time.
"Good night, Dexter."

chapters.title: Chapter 218 | Selene...
paragraphs: The door closed behind her and Dexter stood alone in his room.
He stared at the closed door, then he punched the air in anger.
"What the fuck," he muttered to the empty room.
He sat down on his bed and pressed his palms against his face.
The first question was the most fundamental. When had the switch happened? When Lyra entered his room, was she Lyra? Or was she already Aurelyx?
He replayed the sequence.
The first one had seemed like Lyra. The shyness. The hesitation. The nervous energy.
But the heartbeat had been slightly wrong but even then, the chips.
’Was she Aurelyx from the beginning? Or did they switch midway?’
The chips. The way her eyes had lit up. The way she had flashed across the room. The way she had eaten with content, rhythmic precision. The "thank you" that was soft and warm and genuine.
That had felt like Lyra. Completely, absolutely Lyra.

But then the crunching had stopped. The gaze had changed. The kiss had happened. And the voice that followed the kiss, the voice that asked "You don’t like it?", had carried a tremor that could have been either Lyra’s genuine nervousness or Aurelyx’s imitation of Lyra’s genuine nervousness.
’Did they switch during the kiss? Was Lyra the one who initiated it, and Aurelyx the one who took over when it deepened?’
’Or was Aurelyx there from the start, performing Lyra’s nervousness with enough accuracy to fool me?’
He didn’t know.
And that was the part that was driving him insane.
Was it Lyra? The sweet, shy, chip-loving girl who had kissed his cheek and then run away? Or was it Aurelyx? The Shadow Queen?
The uncertainty was maddening.
And then there was the other thing. The thing that Aurelyx had said before she left.
’Your heavenly physique.’
Dexter’s hands tightened into fists.
How did she know? What did she know? How much had she observed during her time in control of Lyra’s body?
’Think. Think. Think. The only way she can know about the physique is if she can sense it or she can actually read my inner most thoughts unlike Lyra who can read just the surface.’
He didn’t know that either.
Dexter lay back on his bed and stared at the ceiling.

Everything was starting to make sense now. The strange behaviors. The cold voice in the bedroom. The diary entry. The single-portion meals. The "Are you testing me?" reaction to the chips. All of it was starting to make sense.
It had been Aurelyx every time.
Two people and one body. One who remembered everything and one who remembered nothing.
And Dexter was caught between them.

He thought about what to do. The options were limited. He could confront Lyra directly, tell her about Aurelyx, and hope that the knowledge would help rather than harm. But he didn’t know if telling Lyra might trigger her or cause even more harm than good.
Or it might help and give Lyra the awareness she needed to fight back.
He didn’t know which but he knew one thing.
Between Aurelyx and Lyra, he had already chosen Lyra and not the Shadow Queen.
His Lyra.
Dexter would find a way to erase Aurelyx. To remove the secondary personality from Lyra’s body and give Lyra full, permanent, unchallenged control over her own mind and her own life.
He didn’t know how yet ans didn’t have the tools yet or knowledgeyet but he would find them.
Whatever it took and however long it took.
’For now, I can only keep an eye on her.’

The thought was unsatisfying. But it was the only strategy available to him at the moment. Charging into Lyra’s room and demanding answers from Aurelyx would accomplish nothing except potentially destabilizing a situation that was already balanced on a knife’s edge.
He was still pondering when the door opened.
"Click."
Dexter’s expression changed instantly.
The killing intent erupted from his body before his conscious mind could intervene.
For a split second, he thought Aurelyx had returned.
His hand shot toward his spatial storage as the Void Star Saber’s hilt materialized against his palm and his muscles coiled as his mana surged.
The door opened fully.
Dexter froze.
It wasn’t Aurelyx nor was it Lyra.
It was Selene.

She stood in the doorway, her silver-white hair falling over her shoulders, her pale face tilted slightly forward, her sightless eyes aimed roughly in his direction. She wore a simple white sleeping gown that reached her upper thighs, and her bare feet made almost no sound on the wooden floor.
At the same moment she appeared, the temperature in the room plummeted.
An icy chill seeped through the doorway like fog rolling across a frozen lake.
Selene had sensed Dexter’s killing intent and her face turned cold.
’Assassin.’
Without hesitation, her own killing intent exploded.
’BOOM!’
A violent, chilling aura erupted from Selene’s body.

The frost on the doorframe exploded outward, coating the walls, the ceiling, the floor. The window behind Dexter developed a thick layer of ice that blocked the moonlight. The air temperature dropped below freezing in an instant, cold enough to make breath painful, cold enough to freeze moisture on contact.
The killing intent was staggering.
It didn’t roar or crash or thunder like Dexter’s flame-forged aggression. It was silent as it consumed Dexter’s own.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
’What the...’
He hadn’t expected Selene to respond with a counter-surge that made his own killing intent feel like a campfire compared to a blizzard.
For a brief moment, the two killing intents collided and the atmosphere in the room became suffocating. Fire and ice.
Even crippled and blind and chronically ill. The killing intent she radiated was enough to make Dexter’s survival instincts scream.
He was caught off guard.
Not by the power. By the speed. By the instant, reflexive response of a woman who should have been helpless but whose body still remembered how to kill.
Dexter immediately withdrew his killing intent.

Selene’s killing intent held for another moment, then it gradually, it faded.

sentences.text: The door closed behind her and Dexter stood alone in his room.
He stared at the closed door, then he punched the air in anger.
"What the fuck," he muttered to the empty room.
He sat down on his bed and pressed his palms against his face.
The first question was the most fundamental.
When had the switch happened?
When Lyra entered his room, was she Lyra?
Or was she already Aurelyx?
He replayed the sequence.
The first one had seemed like Lyra.
The shyness.
The hesitation.
The nervous energy.
But the heartbeat had been slightly wrong but even then, the chips.
’Was she Aurelyx from the beginning?
Or did they switch midway?’
The chips.
The way her eyes had lit up.
The way she had flashed across the room.
The way she had eaten with content, rhythmic precision.
The "thank you" that was soft and warm and genuine.
That had felt like Lyra.
Completely, absolutely Lyra.
But then the crunching had stopped.
The gaze had changed.
The kiss had happened.

And the voice that followed the kiss, the voice that asked "You don’t like it?", had carried a tremor that could have been either Lyra’s genuine nervousness or Aurelyx’s imitation of Lyra’s genuine nervousness.
’Did they switch during the kiss?
Was Lyra the one who initiated it, and Aurelyx the one who took over when it deepened?’
’Or was Aurelyx there from the start, performing Lyra’s nervousness with enough accuracy to fool me?’
He didn’t know.
And that was the part that was driving him insane.
Was it Lyra?
The sweet, shy, chip-loving girl who had kissed his cheek and then run away?
Or was it Aurelyx?
The Shadow Queen?
The uncertainty was maddening.
And then there was the other thing.
The thing that Aurelyx had said before she left.
’Your heavenly physique.’
Dexter’s hands tightened into fists.
How did she know?
What did she know?
How much had she observed during her time in control of Lyra’s body?
’Think.
Think.
Think.
The only way she can know about the physique is if she can sense it or she can actually read my inner most thoughts unlike Lyra who can read just the surface.’
He didn’t know that either.
Dexter lay back on his bed and stared at the ceiling.
Everything was starting to make sense now.
The strange behaviors.
The cold voice in the bedroom.
The diary entry.
The single-portion meals.
The "Are you testing me?" reaction to the chips.
All of it was starting to make sense.
It had been Aurelyx every time.
Two people and one body.
One who remembered everything and one who remembered nothing.
And Dexter was caught between them.
He thought about what to do.
The options were limited.
He could confront Lyra directly, tell her about Aurelyx, and hope that the knowledge would help rather than harm.
But he didn’t know if telling Lyra might trigger her or cause even more harm than good.
Or it might help and give Lyra the awareness she needed to fight back.
He didn’t know which but he knew one thing.
Between Aurelyx and Lyra, he had already chosen Lyra and not the Shadow Queen.
His Lyra.
Dexter would find a way to erase Aurelyx.
To remove the secondary personality from Lyra’s body and give Lyra full, permanent, unchallenged control over her own mind and her own life.
He didn’t know how yet ans didn’t have the tools yet or knowledgeyet but he would find them.
Whatever it took and however long it took.
’For now, I can only keep an eye on her.’
The thought was unsatisfying.
But it was the only strategy available to him at the moment.
Charging into Lyra’s room and demanding answers from Aurelyx would accomplish nothing except potentially destabilizing a situation that was already balanced on a knife’s edge.
He was still pondering when the door opened.
"Click."
Dexter’s expression changed instantly.
The killing intent erupted from his body before his conscious mind could intervene.
For a split second, he thought Aurelyx had returned.
His hand shot toward his spatial storage as the Void Star Saber’s hilt materialized against his palm and his muscles coiled as his mana surged.
The door opened fully.
Dexter froze.
It wasn’t Aurelyx nor was it Lyra.
It was Selene.
She stood in the doorway, her silver-white hair falling over her shoulders, her pale face tilted slightly forward, her sightless eyes aimed roughly in his direction.
She wore a simple white sleeping gown that reached her upper thighs, and her bare feet made almost no sound on the wooden floor.
At the same moment she appeared, the temperature in the room plummeted.
An icy chill seeped through the doorway like fog rolling across a frozen lake.
Selene had sensed Dexter’s killing intent and her face turned cold.
’Assassin.’
Without hesitation, her own killing intent exploded.
’BOOM!’
A violent, chilling aura erupted from Selene’s body.
The frost on the doorframe exploded outward, coating the walls, the ceiling, the floor.
The window behind Dexter developed a thick layer of ice that blocked the moonlight.
The air temperature dropped below freezing in an instant, cold enough to make breath painful, cold enough to freeze moisture on contact.
The killing intent was staggering.
It didn’t roar or crash or thunder like Dexter’s flame-forged aggression.
It was silent as it consumed Dexter’s own.
Dexter’s eyes widened.
’What the...’
He hadn’t expected Selene to respond with a counter-surge that made his own killing intent feel like a campfire compared to a blizzard.
For a brief moment, the two killing intents collided and the atmosphere in the room became suffocating.
Fire and ice.
Even crippled and blind and chronically ill.
The killing intent she radiated was enough to make Dexter’s survival instincts scream.
He was caught off guard.
Not by the power.
By the speed.
By the instant, reflexive response of a woman who should have been helpless but whose body still remembered how to kill.
Dexter immediately withdrew his killing intent.
"Wait," he said.
His voice was calm.
Firm.
Designed to cut through the confusion without escalating it.
"There isn’t an assassin."
Selene’s killing intent held for another moment, then it gradually, it faded.

chapters.title: Chapter 219 | Selene... II
paragraphs: The frost stopped spreading and the temperature began to climb as the oppressive weight in the air dissipated, replaced by the normal, comfortable atmosphere maintained by the Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact.
Selene tilted her head toward Dexter’s direction.
"Then why were you releasing killing intent?"
Dexter fell silent.
How was he supposed to explain that he had spent the past several hours worrying about the possibility of Aurelyx returning?
He sighed.
"It’s a long story."
Selene frowned slightly. The expression was subtle, visible only in the slight tightening of the skin around her pale eyes and the barely perceptible downward pull of her lips.
"A long story?"
"Yeah."
He looked at her. She was standing in the doorway, her white sleeping gown slightly rumpled, her silver hair disheveled.
Dexter hesitated for a moment.
Then he spoke.
"What do you know about Aurelyx?"
The effect was immediate.

Selene’s eyes flashed and as harp, sudden flash of recognition that triggered her Echolocation into a burst of rapid, intense pulses, as though her body had involuntarily sharpened its senses in response to a name that carried weight.
Her brows furrowed.
"Where did you hear that name?"
Dexter blinked.
The reaction was not what he had expected.
Selene knew the name.
Dexter’s mind recalibrated instantly.
"I heard it randomly," he said carefully. "When I was speaking with the heroes at the meeting today. Someone mentioned it in passing."

It was a lie. He knew it was a lie. Selene probably knew it was a lie. But the truth, that Aurelyx had appeared in his bedroom and kissed him and claimed to be a separate personality living inside Lyra, was not a truth he was prepared to share. Not yet. Not without understanding more.
Selene’s expression became solemn.
She stood in the doorway for a long moment, her body perfectly still, her head tilted slightly downward.
Then she spoke.
"Aurelyx is said to be the number one assassin in this city."
The words landed in the room like stones.
Dexter stared at her.

"No one knows who she is," Selene continued in a quiet voice as thought she didn’t want anyone else to hear. "No one knows who he or she is. No one has seen their face or one knows where they live or who they work for."
She paused.
"But it is said that Aurelyx is the number one assassin in the entire city. Possibly in the country and any mission accepted has a 100 percent success rate and have never failed."
Dexter’s mind went blank.
The number one assassin in the entire city.
Aurelyx which was living inside Lyra was actually that person.
The number one assassin in the entire city is a split personality living inside my wife?
That didn’t make sense.

Aurelyx was a secondary consciousness likely due to the incident. An alternate personality that surfaced and retreated within Lyra’s body. She wasn’t a separate physical person and couldn’t operate independently to execute assassinations without Lyra’s body being present.
Unless...
Unless the switching happened frequently enough, and she was actually the main one personality.
The possibility was horrifying but entirely plausible.

"Moreover," Selene continued, "the name has circulated through the upper echelons of the Hero Association. The top brass are aware of her existence. They have a file on her, although it’s apparently mostly empty and the one they have is about her kills."
She paused.
"Anyone who knows that name should probably distance themselves from anyone associated with it."
Dexter’s face didn’t change. But inside, his mind was racing like a horse through a desert.
The number one assassin in the city was lyra.

Aurelyx isn’t just a personality fragment. She’s a functional, operational, professional assassin who has been conducting missions from inside Lyra’s body for years. Probably since before the dungeon incident.
It wasn’t Lyra they were afraid of, it was Aurelyx.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed.
"You said Aurelyx has never failed a mission," he said.
"Yes."
"Do you know anything else about her?"
Selene shook her head.
"Not much," she said. "Nobody knows her true identity. Nobody knows her appearance. Nobody knows where she lives or who she works for."
"Then how does the Hero Association know about her?"
Selene shook her head slowly. "They don’t know her. They only know the results.
"The results?"
"Every target she accepts dies."

"Regardless of how heavily protected the target is," Selene continued. "Regardless of their cultivation level. Regardless of their security detail or their defensive formations or their relic equipment. She always finds a way."
She paused.
"Always."
Dexter fell silent.
Aurylex was something else entirely. He thought about the shadow corruption.

The system had reported Lyra’s shadow corruption at zero percent. But Aurelyx had said she was the Shadow Queen. What if the shadow corruption hadn’t been cleansed? What if it had been absorbed? Integrated? Converted from a corrupting influence into a power source by a consciousness that knew how to wield it?

What if Aurelyx was, in her own right, an extraordinarily powerful entity who had been operating from inside Lyra’s body for years, conducting assassinations, accumulating power, and building a reputation as the most dangerous killer in the city?
All while Lyra slept.
Dexter’s gaze darkened.
Selene noticed the shift in his expression. Through her Echolocation, she could detect the subtle changes in his body.
"Is something wrong?" she asked.
Dexter immediately shook his head.
"Nothing is wrong."
He forced a smile which made Selene blink.
She didn’t believe him but since Dexter didn’t want to talk about it, she couldn’t force him.
"All right," she said. Her voice carried a trace of reluctance. "I should take my leave."
She turned around and left.
Dexter watched her begin to leave as her hand found the doorframe.
"Wait," Dexter said.
Selene froze at the door and her hand remained on the frame with her body half-turned toward the hallway, one foot already across the threshold.
She froze.
Then, in a voice so soft voice, she murmured.
"We can wait until you’re in a good mood."

chapters.title: Chapter 220 | Rely On Me!
paragraphs: Sha felt that she might be a burden to Dexter and immediately wanted to leave.
This made Dexter’s chest tighten and he spoke immediately.
"No, I’m quite alright."
He paused as he continued in an honest tone.
"And even if I’m in a bad mood, I will always want to help you."
Selene’s body trembled slightly as though she heard singling she almost couldn’t believe.
Selene didn’t respond immediately and five seconds passed.
’Did I say too much?’
Just when Dexter was about to speak and assure her; Selene suddenly nodded her head.
"Okay," Then she turned back into the room with her head was lowered. Her silver hair fell forward, screening her face as she walked to the bed slowly.
She reached the edge of the bed and then under dexter’s gaze, she sat down.
Then after a while, she crossed her legs beneath her, placed her hands on her knees with palms upward and then closed her eyes.
She began cultivating.

Dexter watched her settle and the tension in her posture gradually eased. He immediately exploded with his heavenly flames, letting the intense heat wash through her entire body and even the entire room.
Suddenly, ao thing sparked in Dexter’s mind and he felt bolder.
"Come closer to the bed," he said. "So your back can rest against the headboard."
He leisurely patted the space directly beside him.
Selene’s body froze as her white eyes opened andwidened.
She blinked rapidly, obviously startled by Dexter’swords.
Through her Echolocation, she could perceive him him and the space he was pointing to. The space that was directly next to his body.
He was asking her to sit next to him.
Selene blinked again and her ears turned pink. Dexter wasn’t asking and was telling her as though it was a casual thing she could do.
She was about to shake her head when to Dexter’s shock, she nodded her head slowly as the blush crept from her ears down her neck,
She suddenly leaned and then placed her hand on the bed as she bent down like a cute cat and then cat-crawled forward.
Seeing the arc of her back made Dexter’s heart race like a position in an engine!
That move was so damn captivating!
Selene moved across the bed on all fours, her silver hair swinging beneath her, until she reached the space beside him and then she settled.
Her back found the headboards her knees crossed beneath her as her shoulder came to rest against his.
The contact was electric.

The warmth that had been reaching her in diluted waves across the bed now flowed directly into her body through the point of contact. The heat seeped through her sleeping gown, through her skin, through the damaged meridians beneath, and into the cold that lived in her bones.
And she exhaled.
They sat together. Shoulder to shoulder. Backs against the headboard. Cultivating in silence.

The mana flowed. The Star Nodes absorbed. The cold and the heat coexisted in the small bedroom, finding equilibrium in the narrow space between two bodies that were, in their own quiet way, learning to share space.
Minutes passed.
Then Selene spoke.
"You’re still thinking about her, aren’t you?"
Dexter froze.

The question came from nowhere. Or rather, it came from the particular nowhere that existed between two people sitting close enough to feel each other’s heartbeats. The space where observations formed without conscious intent and words escaped without permission.
"About who?" Dexter asked. His voice was carefully neutral.
"Aurelyx."
Dexter stared at her profile. Her silver hair. Her pale skin. Her closed eyes. The faint, barely visible smile on her lips.
"You aren’t very good at hiding things," Selene said.
Dexter sighed.
"You’re becoming quite perceptive," he said.

"I’ve always been perceptive." Selene’s lips curved slightly. The smile was small. Quiet. The smile of someone who had just delivered a compliment to themselves and was slightly amused by it. "After all, I can’t see. I have to rely on everything else."
Her head tilted toward him.
"Your heart rate changes when you’re thinking about something that bothers you. It becomes slightly irregular. Not enough for most people to notice. But I notice."
She paused.
"Your breathing changes too. It becomes more controlled. More deliberate. As though you’re trying to regulate your thoughts by regulating your lungs.
Another pause.
"And your body temperature fluctuates. When you’re calm, the heat from your bloodline is steady. Even. When you’re disturbed, it pulses. Like a heartbeat within a heartbeat."
Dexter looked at her.

She had been studying him. Not visually. Not through observation of facial expressions or body language. Through the tools that her blindness had forced her to develop. Sound. Vibration. Temperature. The invisible, constant data stream that her Echolocation and her enhanced senses provided.
She couldn’t see his face.
But she could read him better than anyone else in the house.
Dexter’s expression softened.
"Then rely on me," he said.
The words were simple. Three words. Subject, verb, object. The most basic sentence structure in the English language.
But they carried weight.
Not the weight of a promise. Not the weight of an obligation. The weight of an offering. A man opening a door and standing aside, making room for someone to enter if they chose to.
Selene’s smile disappeared.

She became completely still. Not the stillness of cultivation. The stillness of a person who had just heard something that required recalibration. Something that didn’t fit into the existing framework of her understanding and needed to be processed before she could respond.
For several seconds, neither of them spoke.
The room was quiet. The mana hummed. The Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact released its gentle, clean scent into the air. The moonlight, filtered through the window, cast pale silver patterns on the floor.
Then Selene lowered her head slightly.
"Okay," she said.
Her voice was so soft that Dexter almost didn’t hear it. The word existed on the threshold of audibility, barely disturbing the air, more felt than heard.
But he heard it.
He smiled.
"Good."
The room became quiet once again. The cultivation resumed. The mana flowed. The warmth spread.

chapters.title: Chapter 221 | Where Are You Going?
paragraphs: The two of them stayed together through the night.
Not speaking nor moving, just existing in the same space, shoulder to shoulder, warmth flowing into cold.
Dexter had stayed awake through all of it.

He had felt the weight of her head settling against him. Felt her arms, which had been resting on her knees, slowly unfold and find his waist and felt as her fingers curl into the fabric of his shirt, gripping it loosely, the way a child grips a blanket in sleep.
He didn’t move.
For the second night in a row, he sat perfectly still for hours, his body stiff and his legs numb and his mana reserves slowly depleting from the sustained output of the Abyssal Flame.
Morning came slowly and Dexter’s eyes snapped open.
The first thing he registered was weight, a warm, solid weight pressed against his chest and wrapped around his waist. He looked down.
Selene was sleeping on him.
Her head rested against his chest, just below his collarbone, her silver-white hair spilling across his shirt in a cascade of moonlight-colored silk.
Her arms were wrapped around his waist, both of them, her fingers interlaced at the small of his back and her breathing was slow.

The Eternal Winter Ice, which typically made her sleep restless and broken, had been suppressed throughout the night by the steady warmth of his Heavenly Flame, and the result was the another peaceful sleep.
A faint, barely audible sound escaped within her lips. She wasn’t snoring but it sounded like a cat’s purr.
Dexter looked down at her sleeping face and she was extremely beautiful to him. If a man was to wake up to such beauty, then they are lucky for a hundred lifetimes.
"Cute," he muttered uncontrollably before he could stop himself.
So not to startle her awake, he wanted to turn off the alarm for today and also chevked the time.
He needed to start cooking.
One hundred portions of Grade One Enchanted Meal. That was the order Tessa had placed yesterday.
Which meant he needs to start cooking them soon.
Dexter began the careful, painstaking process of extracting himself from Selene’s embrace without waking her.

His withdrew his arms first and then shifted his torso. He leaned forward slowly, creating space between his chest and her head. This gave her room to settle onto the pillow rather than onto the empty space.
Suddenly, Selene’s arms tightened making Dexter freeze.
’This girl.’
He chuckled as her face pressed even harder against his chest and a small sound of protest.
"Mmm~"
Dexter held still and waited for her grip to stabilize. Then patiently, he extracted his other arm and his body. A process which took 5 minutes.
Eventually, he was free as he slid off the bed.

He turned back to the bed. Selene had settled into the space he had vacated, her face now pressed into his pillow instead of his chest. Her arms, finding nothing to hold, had curled around the pillow he had used as backrest and were gripping it.
Dexter reached for the duvet at the foot of the bed, tucking the edges around her shoulders.
She looked very peaceful with a tiny smile at the corner of her lips.
Dexter watched her for a moment, then inhaled deeply to calm his rising self and he turned to leave.
Suddenly-
A hand gripped his arm. Dexter stopped and looked back.
Selene’s hand had wrapped around his wrist.
Her eyes were half open as through barely conscious.
"Where... are you going?" she murmured in a sluggish and groggy voice.
Dexter looked at her and smiled as he realized she was sleep talking.

He bent down beside her and his face came close to hers. Then gently, he reached out and started to stroke her hair. Running his fingers through the cool, silky strands, pushing them back from her face, smoothing them against the pillow.
"Sleep," he whispered.
Selene’s eyes, which had been half open fluttered and then she eventually slept.
Her grip on his arm loosened as her fingers relaxed and her hand slipped away, falling back onto the mattress beside her face, the fingers curling slightly inward as they released their hold.
She was asleep again.
Dexter straightened up. He watched her for one more moment. Then he turned and left the room, closing the door behind him with a soft click.
He walked to the kitchen and began.
The process of making one hundred portions of Grade One Enchanted Meal was, by now, a familiar routine.
He started the rice first. While the rice cooked, he prepped the vegetables.
The Arcane Nutrition Insight guided his combinations.

He cooked through the early morning hours. The kitchen filled with the familiar, comforting aromas of seasoned rice and seared chicken. The pots bubbled. The oil sizzled. The knife board rattled with the rhythmic percussion of chopping.
By 5:30 AM, the first fifty portions were done. Packed. Sealed. Stacked.
By 6:30 AM, the second fifty were finished.
Dexter placed them all in his spatial storage, organized and counted, and turned his attention to the girls’ breakfast.
This was different.
For the girls, he didn’t hold back.
He pulled out the ingredients that no amount of money could buy at a market. Diamond Rice, Transcendent-Class beast meat, Star Essence Serum, Millennium Blood Ginseng, Void Spirit Lotus, etc.
The Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot came out as the heavenly Flame ignited. His Great Grandmaster Foodsmith techniques activated fully.
[Ding! Congratulations! You have successfully created Celestial Phoenix Nectar Bowl (Grade 5)]

[Effect: Accelerates meridian repair by 40%. Stimulates nerve regeneration. Boosts mana regeneration for 8 hours. Induces deep cellular healing. Strengthens bloodline integration. Increases cultivation speed by 300% for 6 hours.]

The Transcendent-Class meat had pushed the meal two grades higher than the Celestial Dawn Nectar Bowl from two days ago. The effects were extraordinary. Targeted. Designed specifically for the girls’ conditions.
Dexter plated four bowls. The food glowed as thin wisps of steam rose in spirals that seemed to form patterns, shapes that might have been characters from a language older than civilization.
He carried the bowls to the dining table. Set them down. Then turned back toward the kitchen to wash the pots.
And saw Lyra.

She was standing at the edge of the kitchen doorway. Her dark hair was wet, freshly washed, hanging in damp strands that dripped onto the shoulders of her clean shirt. Her AI glasses sat on her nose. Her dark eyes were fixed on the food with the particular, luminous intensity that Dexter had come to recognize as her default setting.
A small line of drool hung from the corner of her mouth.
Dexter shook his head.
"Good morning, Lyra."
Lyra blinked. Her eyes, which had been locked on the glowing bowls of Grade Five food, slowly moved to his face. The drool remained. She didn’t seem to be aware of it.

She had just bathed. Her hair was wet. Droplets of water clung to her jaw and ran down her neck, disappearing beneath the collar of her shirt. The scent of soap mixed with the aroma of the food, creating a combination that was simultaneously domestic and appetizing.
Dexter walked toward her. He raised his hand.
Lyra saw the hand coming. Her eyes tracked it. She could have moved, the old Lyra would have, but she didn’t.
Dexter’s hand found her head. His fingers sank into her wet hair and he rubbed gently, his palm moving across her scalp, his fingers spreading the moisture evenly through the strands.

chapters.title: Chapter 222 | What Bad Things Did You Do To Selene
paragraphs: Lyra’s eyes widened slightly but then it softened as she leaned into his hand, almost imperceptibly, the way a cat leans into a stroke.
Dexter smiled.
"Hope you slept well," he said as he transmitted the thought telepathically and she nodded, her melodious voice sounded in his mind.
"I slept well."
Dexter nodded. "Good. Sit down, I’ll plate your food."
He walked to the dining table and Lyra followed, her bare feet padding softly on the floor behind him as she sat in her usual chair.
Lyra’s spoon was in her hand before the bowl even touched the table.
’Foodie.’
Dexter chuckled at the foodie and was about to begin serving his own portion when Lyra’s voice entered his mind.
"What’s Aurelyx?"
Dexter’s body froze. But that reaction lasted less than half a second before he blinked his eyes and spoke.
"Where did you get that name?"
Lyra shrugged as she picked up her spoon and aimed it at the bowl with the eager, expectant gaze.
"When you saw me just now, you muttered the name Aurelyx in your mind." She said casually.
Dexter stared at her.
’I muttered it?’
The moment he had turned around and seen Lyra standing at the doorway with wet hair and drool on her chin. The thought that had crossed his mind in that instant.
Aurelyx.
He had thought the name externally on refelx. Moreover, he was a bit sleep deprived too which was why Lyra had been able to pick it up.
Dexter shrugged, keeping his expression carefully neutral.
"It’s just a random name that popped into my head."
Lyra looked at his face for a moment, she was about to follow up with another question when Dexter placed the bowl of Grade 5 Celestial Phoenix Nectar Bowl directly in front of her.
The aroma hit her and the question she was about to ask was instantly forgotten.
Her eyes widened as her nostrils flared and the spoon, which had been hovering in the air, descended toward the bowl with lightning speed as she ate.
Dexter watched her take the first bite as her eyes closed and her expression shifted from eager to stunned to blissful.
He sighed in relief.
At that moment, Mira arrived.
Her Spectral Arms pushed her through the hallway and into the dining room and she parked herself at the table, her crimson eyes scanning the food as her nose inhaled deeply the scent.
"Good morning."
She said unconsciously as she started eating her meal.
Dexter blinked his eyes and replied. "Morning."
Mira didn’t seem to hear as she descended on the food too.
Dexter was about to start eating when he noticed something, Selene wasn’t here.
Dexter immediately stood up and left the dining room and walked to the girls’ bedroom.
Selene should have finished bathing by now. She should have emerged, found her way to the dining table, and begun eating as that was the routine.
But whe he checked the girls bedroom, it was empty.
Dexter stood in the doorway and blinked.
"Don’t tell me she’s still in my room."
He walked across the hall, opened his bedroom door.
Selene was still in his bed.

She hadn’t moved and was exactly where he had left her, curled up beneath the duvet he had draped over her, her silver-white hair spread across his pillow, her arms wrapped around it too as she slept soundly.
Dexter stood in the doorway and stared.
Then he smiled softly. He could wake her but it would be useless.
He watched her for a moment, then he turned and walked back to the dining room.
Mira’s eyes tracked him as he returned.
Her eyes stared at the doorway, then stared at Dexter, then at the doorway again, then at Dexter.
She didn’t say anything as she continued eating for a few minutes. Suddenly she spoke.
"What did you do to Selene?"
The question landed on the table like a grenade as Dexter’s spoon froze halfway to his mouth.
Lyra also froze and her dark eyes, which had been exclusively focused on her bowl, widened and shifted to Dexter’s face.
The food had been so engrossing that Lyra had not noticed Selene’s absence until Mira spoke.
Dexter’s expression changed slightly but then, he dropped his spoke and then glared at Mira.
"What do you mean by what did I do to Selene?"
Mira’s lips curled upward into a smirk.
"You know exactly what I mean."
Dexter pursed his lips.. "You’re acting as if I’m some kind of villain."
"Of course you’re not a villain," Mira said in a honey sweet tone. "I’m pretty sure you want to do bad things, though."
Lyra’s ears turned pink and red at the same time !
Mira continued, completely unfazed by the destruction she was inflicting on Lyra’s composure.
"Who knows what you’ve done to Selene? Maybe she’s tired from all the bad things you did to her."
Dexter stared at her.

"I woke up this morning," Mira continued. "and Selene was not in the bedroom. She was not in the living room and she was not in the backyard. Which means she was either in the bathroom or in your bed."
She paused.
"She wasn’t in the bathroom, which means She was sleeping on your bed."
"Which means you definitely did bad things to her. So what bad things did you do to Selene?"
Dexter sat in his chair and stared at the woman in the wheelchair.
He wanted to argue but he knew it would be of no use.
So Dexter took a different approach.
He smiled and spoke.
"Are you jealous? Do you also want me to do bad things to you?"
Mira’s expression froze and her smirk vanished as she was stunned by dexters words.
Her neck turned red and she stuttered.
"Pervert," she spat. "I knew it. Pervert."
Dexter chuckled.

"Selene wasn’t comfortable sleeping with her illness. Her Eternal Winter Ice was acting up. So she came to my room and we cultivated together. My Heavenly Flame suppressed the cold. She fell asleep. That’s all."
Mira glared at him. Suspiciously.
Dexter met her gaze without flinching.
Eventually, Mira sniffed and then returned to her food.
