chapters.title: Chapter 223 | The Festival
paragraphs: The subject was closed.

Lyra exhaled slowly. The pink in her ears faded gradually, returning to a color that suggested her cardiovascular system had resumed normal operations. She picked up her spoon and dove back into her bowl with the relieved urgency of someone who had been caught in someone else’s crossfire and was grateful to still be alive.

They ate. The Grade Five meal was consumed in its entirety by all four of them. Mira cleaned her bowl. Lyra ate four portions. Dexter ate one. The remaining portions went into the refrigerator for later.
As the meal wound down, Dexter set his spoon down and looked at the three women.
"The festival is tomorrow," he said. "Are we all ready?"
Mira froze.

Her spoon, which had been en route to her mouth via her Spectral Arm, stopped in the air. Her crimson eyes, which had been focused on her bowl, shifted to Dexter’s face. A brief, flickering expression crossed her features. Something that might have been hesitation. Or uncertainty. Or the particular discomfort of a woman who had agreed to something days ago and was now reconsidering.
Lyra also paused. But only for a moment. The word "festival" registered, and with it the memory of Dexter’s earlier description. A neighborhood gathering. A picnic. Food. People. The outside world.
She resumed eating. The festival was tomorrow. That was a problem for tomorrow-Lyra.
Dexter noticed Mira’s reaction.
He noticed the way her jaw had tightened. The way her Spectral Arm had hesitated mid-motion. The way her crimson eyes had flickered with something that looked uncomfortably like doubt.

"We’re not in the mood to go anymore?" Dexter asked. The question was directed at Mira specifically. His eyes were on her face, reading the micro-expressions that she was trying and failing to suppress.
Mira shrugged. The shrug was too casual. Too deliberate. The shrug of someone who was trying to appear indifferent while feeling something very different. "Anything you want."
Dexter inhaled slowly through his nose. Exhaled through his mouth. Then glared at her.

"You were the main reason we wanted to go to this festival in the first place," he said. "You were the one who said you wanted to go outside. You were the one who said you wanted to see the outside world. And now you’re telling me you’re not in the mood?
Mira’s eyes flashed. "I didn’t say I don’t want to go. I didn’t say anything at all."
Dexter glared at her. "Your body language says otherwise. And if you don’t feel like going, that’s fine. But it’s three against one now. You don’t have a choice in the matter."
Mira glared back.

The two of them sat at the dining table, locked in a staring contest that carried the weight of three weeks of accumulated domestic tension, mutual stubbornness, and the particular, complicated dynamic of two people who cared about each other but would rather die than admit it directly.
Mira broke first.

Not by looking away. By shoving an enormous spoonful of rice into her mouth, causing her cheeks to bulge outward like a chipmunk hoarding for winter. She chewed. Slowly. Aggressively. While maintaining eye contact with Dexter the entire time.
The effect was simultaneously menacing and adorable.

Dexter held her gaze. He didn’t blink. He didn’t smile. He simply sat there and matched her stare with his own, the two of them locked in a battle of wills that had no stakes and no resolution and was being conducted over a table of empty bowls while one of them chewed with her mouth full and her Spectral Arms crossed behind her back in a posture of absolute defiance.
Lyra was not watching.
Lyra was eating.

Her focus was so completely, so thoroughly, so exclusively devoted to the Grade Five meal in front of her that the nuclear-level domestic dispute happening across the table was registering as background noise. She didn’t notice the staring contest. She didn’t notice the tension. She didn’t notice anything except the complex, layered flavors of Transcendent-Class beast meat and Diamond Rice dissolving on her tongue.
Dexter eventually broke the stare. Not because he lost. Because there was no winning a staring contest with a woman who was chewing angrily, and he had deliveries to make.
After breakfast, Dexter stood up and collected the plates.
"I need to run and deliver the meals to the bakery," he said. "I’ll be back in twenty minutes.
Lyra looked up from her bowl. She smiled and waved from the couch, her dark eyes warm behind her AI glasses. The telepathic connection carried her voice into his mind.
"Bye."
Dexter smiled and nodded at her.

He walked to where Mira was sitting. She had been wheeled to the living room by her Spectral Arms and was now positioned by the window. Her usual spot. Her crimson eyes were closed. Her expression was neutral. Carefully, deliberately neutral.
"I’m leaving," Dexter said.
He didn’t look at her. He said it to the air beside her, his voice directed at the general vicinity of her wheelchair rather than at her face. The verbal equivalent of a note left on a counter.
Mira snorted. A small, sharp, carefully modulated snort.
"Farewell."
The word was clipped. Final. Delivered with the precise, measured politeness of a woman who was not going to say anything more than the absolute minimum required by basic social convention.
Dexter snorted back. A small, sharp, equally modulated snort.
He walked to the front door. Opened it. Stepped outside. Closed it behind him.
The morning air was cool. Fresh. The street was quiet. The bakery was a five-minute walk. He didn’t need the SUV. The containers were in his spatial storage. He could carry them without effort.
He walked.

The neighborhood was beginning to stir. A few early risers were out on their porches, drinking coffee, reading tablets. A jogger passed him on the sidewalk, nodding politely. Somewhere down the street, a dog barked twice and fell silent.
Dexter walked and thought.
He thought about the festival tomorrow, about taking three women to a public gathering in a neighborhood where everyone knew their faces and their stories.

sentences.text: The subject was closed.
Lyra exhaled slowly.
The pink in her ears faded gradually, returning to a color that suggested her cardiovascular system had resumed normal operations.
She picked up her spoon and dove back into her bowl with the relieved urgency of someone who had been caught in someone else’s crossfire and was grateful to still be alive.
They ate.
The Grade Five meal was consumed in its entirety by all four of them.
Mira cleaned her bowl.
Lyra ate four portions.
Dexter ate one.
The remaining portions went into the refrigerator for later.
As the meal wound down, Dexter set his spoon down and looked at the three women.
"The festival is tomorrow," he said.
"Are we all ready?"
Mira froze.
Her spoon, which had been en route to her mouth via her Spectral Arm, stopped in the air.
Her crimson eyes, which had been focused on her bowl, shifted to Dexter’s face.
A brief, flickering expression crossed her features.
Something that might have been hesitation.
Or uncertainty.
Or the particular discomfort of a woman who had agreed to something days ago and was now reconsidering.
Lyra also paused.
But only for a moment.
The word "festival" registered, and with it the memory of Dexter’s earlier description.
A neighborhood gathering.
A picnic.
Food.
People.
The outside world.
She resumed eating.
The festival was tomorrow.
That was a problem for tomorrow-Lyra.
Dexter noticed Mira’s reaction.
He noticed the way her jaw had tightened.
The way her Spectral Arm had hesitated mid-motion.
The way her crimson eyes had flickered with something that looked uncomfortably like doubt.
"We’re not in the mood to go anymore?" Dexter asked.
The question was directed at Mira specifically.
His eyes were on her face, reading the micro-expressions that she was trying and failing to suppress.
Mira shrugged.
The shrug was too casual.
Too deliberate.
The shrug of someone who was trying to appear indifferent while feeling something very different.
"Anything you want."
Dexter inhaled slowly through his nose.
Exhaled through his mouth.
Then glared at her.
"You were the main reason we wanted to go to this festival in the first place," he said.
"You were the one who said you wanted to go outside.
You were the one who said you wanted to see the outside world.
And now you’re telling me you’re not in the mood?
Mira’s eyes flashed.
"I didn’t say I don’t want to go.
I didn’t say anything at all."
Dexter glared at her.
"Your body language says otherwise.
And if you don’t feel like going, that’s fine.
But it’s three against one now.
You don’t have a choice in the matter."
Mira glared back.

The two of them sat at the dining table, locked in a staring contest that carried the weight of three weeks of accumulated domestic tension, mutual stubbornness, and the particular, complicated dynamic of two people who cared about each other but would rather die than admit it directly.
Mira broke first.
Not by looking away.
By shoving an enormous spoonful of rice into her mouth, causing her cheeks to bulge outward like a chipmunk hoarding for winter.
She chewed.
Slowly.
Aggressively.
While maintaining eye contact with Dexter the entire time.
The effect was simultaneously menacing and adorable.
Dexter held her gaze.
He didn’t blink.
He didn’t smile.

He simply sat there and matched her stare with his own, the two of them locked in a battle of wills that had no stakes and no resolution and was being conducted over a table of empty bowls while one of them chewed with her mouth full and her Spectral Arms crossed behind her back in a posture of absolute defiance.
Lyra was not watching.
Lyra was eating.

Her focus was so completely, so thoroughly, so exclusively devoted to the Grade Five meal in front of her that the nuclear-level domestic dispute happening across the table was registering as background noise.
She didn’t notice the staring contest.
She didn’t notice the tension.
She didn’t notice anything except the complex, layered flavors of Transcendent-Class beast meat and Diamond Rice dissolving on her tongue.
Dexter eventually broke the stare.
Not because he lost.
Because there was no winning a staring contest with a woman who was chewing angrily, and he had deliveries to make.

"I need to run and deliver the meals to the bakery," he said.
"I’ll be back in twenty minutes.
Lyra looked up from her bowl.
She smiled and waved from the couch, her dark eyes warm behind her AI glasses.
The telepathic connection carried her voice into his mind.
"Bye."
Dexter smiled and nodded at her.
He walked to where Mira was sitting.
She had been wheeled to the living room by her Spectral Arms and was now positioned by the window.
Her usual spot.
Her crimson eyes were closed.
Her expression was neutral.
Carefully, deliberately neutral.
"I’m leaving," Dexter said.
He didn’t look at her.
He said it to the air beside her, his voice directed at the general vicinity of her wheelchair rather than at her face.
The verbal equivalent of a note left on a counter.

A small, sharp, carefully modulated snort.

paragraphs: Dexter exited the house and walked toward the bakery.
The morning was still early and the air was cool, carrying the faint scent of freshly baked bread that had been drifting from the bakery as Dexter neared there.
Just like yesterday, the place was already packed, but the moment Tessa spotted Dexter through the entrance, her eyes lit up.

She was behind the counter, wearing her white apron over her blue dress. Her curly red hair was tied back with a ribbon that was already coming loose, strands escaping in every direction. Flour dusted a but of her nose, she had probably been baking since four.
She headed toward him immediately, practically skipping the entire way. The customers in her path parted without complaint. M
"Good morning!" she greeted, arriving in front of him with a smile that could have powered the city’s grid. "You’re quite early today."
Dexter shrugged. "Yeah. I woke up early to prepare the orders."
He lifted the two bags in his hands. Each one contained fifty sealed containers of Grade One Comfort Chicken Rice.
Tessa’s eyes moved to the bags.
"Come over here," she said, gesturing toward the back of the bakery, leading him through the narrow hallway behind the counter, into the small storage room where the thermal shelves waited.
Dexter followed.
Tessa pointed toward the empty section of shelf that had been cleared for his meals. "Just put them here. I’ll sell them one by one today."
Dexter began stacking the one hundred containers neatly.
He stepped back.
"If that’s all, I’ll take my leave," he said, turning toward the exit.
"Wait!"
Dexter paused and turned back. Tessa was standing in the doorway of the storage room, her hands clasped behind her back.
"You’re coming to the festival tomorrow, right?"
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "I already told you I was coming, didn’t I?"
Tessa shrugged casually.
"You might have changed your mind. I’m just making sure you haven’t."
She smiled.
Dexter couldn’t help smiling back.
"No, I haven’t changed my mind. Or do you want me to change it?"
Tessa’s eyes widened and her head shook so rapidly that her curly hair bounced in every direction simultaneously.
"No, no, no! Of course not!"
Dexter chuckled.
"All right. If there’s nothing else, I really have to get going."
His expression became slightly more serious.
’Selene still hasn’t woken up.’
He wanted to be there when she did and she hadn’t eaten yet. The Grade Five meal was waiting in the refrigerator, but he wanted to feed her immediately she woke up.
He didn’t want her waking up and finding him gone. So he was in no mood to waste time.
"If there’s nothing else, I’ll head back."
Tessa hesitated.
Suddenly, her hand reached out and caught his sleeve.
Dexter looked at her with a puzzled look.
"Is something the matter?"
Tessa wanted to speak but then she hesitated again. After a while, she eventually spoke.
"The food you gave me..."
Dexter stopped as he looked at her hand on his sleeve. Then at her face.
"What about it?"
Tessa looked at him curiously.
"The food you gave me that time. Did it have any special effects?"
Dexter blinked.
"Yeah, all the meals I gave you have special effect."
Tessa immediately shook her head as her curly hair bounced as she spoke in a serious voice. "Now these ones. I meant the one you gave me to eat when I came to your home through the fence."
’The food I gave her.’
He rewound through his memory. The first meal he had ever given Tessa. Weeks ago. Before the bakery partnership.
It had been a small portion and was the remains of his wives bloodline meals
Those ingredients carried bloodline-awakening effects as a passive property. He hadn’t thought about it affecting Tessa.
And Tessa had eaten it.
Dexter studied her carefully.
’Did she awaken a bloodline?’

He looked her up and down. His Arcane Nutrition Insight, which provided passive information about ingredients and their effects, didn’t extend to reading other people’s cultivation status. He couldn’t detect bloodline activation through observation alone.
But he could look for signs.
Tessa’s skin was clear. Healthy. The complexion of a 17 year old who spent her days in a bakery and her evenings in a garden. Nothing unusual there.
Her energy was the same as always.
But...
There was something in her eyes. A faint, barely perceptible brightness that hadn’t been there before.
Dexter weighed his response carefully.
"Yeah," he said. "It contained some special effects."
Tessa’s expression became more attentive. She leaned forward slightly. The hand on his sleeve tightened.
Dexter continued. "There were recovery effects. A slight boost to cultivation. An improvement to one’s physique."
He paused.
"It also contained an effect capable of awakening a bloodline, but the amount you ate was very small."
He narrowed his eyes.
"Did something happen to you?"
The question was direct.
Tessa stared at him suspiciously for a moment.
Then she slowly shook her head.
"No. Nothing happened."
She smiled. The smile was light. Casual. Perfectly calibrated to convey that everything was fine and there was absolutely no reason for concern.
"I just wanted to make sure."
Dexter continued looking at her for several seconds.
Something about her answer felt wrong.
Tessa was a lot of things. She was energetic. She was entrepreneurial. She was perceptive. She was a better businesswoman at 17 than most adults were at forty.
But she was not a good liar.
Dexter considered pressing.
But he didn’t. Because it wasn’t his business anyways.
On his way back from the bakery, Dexter’s phone rang.
He checked the caller ID while walking. The name on the screen made him pause mid-stride.
Rachel.
He frowned slightly and his feelings was quite complicated about picking up the call.
He eventually answered.
"Hey, Dexter."
Rachel’s voice came through the speaker with the warm, polished cadence that he remembered from their first meeting at the hotel bar.
"It’s been a while," she said.

chapters.title: Chapter 225 | The Call...
paragraphs: Dexter blinked. "Hey, Rachel. It hasn’t been all that long, actually."
He could feel Rachel’s smile through the phone as she spoke.
"Which means you haven’t been thinking about me all this time. That is really sad."
Dexter didn’t respond to that. He had learned, through several interactions with Rachel, that engaging with her flirtatious comments was like feeding a stray cat.
"I’ve been really busy," he said instead.
Rachel went silent for a moment.
"How are your wives doing?" she asked sincerely. "I hope they are doing all right and hope they are healing quite nicely."
"They are doing quite fine, thank you," Dexter responded.
He paused and the phone was silent. Rachel was waiting.
Dexter sighed.
"What about you? Hope you’re doing all right."
He could feel Rachel’s excitement through the phone.
"Yes, I am doing quite all right. Thank you for asking."
Dexter shrugged, even though she couldn’t see it. "Yeah, anytime."
Then Rachel spoke again.
"We should try to get together sometime. Maybe for breakfast. Lunch. Dinner or something."
Dexter frowned slightly but he didn’t respond immediately.
Rachel sensed his hesitation. She immediately added, "You know, as friends. Just to catch up with each other. Maybe take a break from other stuff."
The word "friends" was emphasized.
"I’m always busy," Dexter said. "I don’t have much time for taking breaks and stuff."
Rachel remained silent for a while. The silence lasted long enough for Dexter to hear the faint sound of traffic on her end. She was outsid, walking or maybe in her car.
"It’s all right," she said. "I understand. Maybe another time then."
Dexter didn’t speak and the conversation felt like it was winding down.
Then Rachel said, "Oh, right, before I forget. What do you know about Harvest Homes?"
Dexter’s eyes flashed coldly.
"What happened?" he asked. "Why do you ask?"
"I read a report down here," Rachel said. "About a sudden incident at Harvest Homes. A breakout. An altercation. And your name was also in that report. So I had to ask."
Dexter’s jaw tightened.
’My name was on the report?’
"How?" he asked. "Who filed it?"

"Hero Association internal intelligence," Rachel replied. "They monitor significant incidents involving registered heroes. The Harvest Homes event flagged automatically because of the scale of the damage and the cultivation levels involved."
She paused.
"Your name was redacted, though. It wasn’t quite clear. Your involvement wasn’t explicitly stated. But you were one of the people connected to the incident."
Dexter thought about it then shook his head.
"It’s nothing," he said. "I was just nearby Harvest Homes when that happened. Coincidence."
Rachel didn’t respond immediately. The silence on her end was evaluative.
"All right," she said. The tone was neutral. Neither believing nor disbelieving.
Then she continued.
"Oh, before I forget. Aurora."
Dexter blinked. "What about Aurora?"
"I heard you met with her. At the restaurant. Yesterday."
"Yeah," Dexter said. "She was there. At the restaurant. When I met with the squad."
"Aurora told me," Rachel said. "She told me you two are quite connected. Are you?"
Dexter frowned. "What do you mean, connected? She approached me after the meeting. She had a proposition. That’s all."
Rachel’s voice carried a trace of amusement. "A proposition? That sounds interesting. What kind of proposition?"
"Business," Dexter said flatly. "Nothing else."
"Mm-hmm," Rachel said. The sound was noncommittal. The verbal equivalent of a raised eyebrow.
Then he continued. "She told me you two are quite connected. She said you know each other now. Are you best friends? Or something?"
"No," Rachel said, answering her own question before Dexter could. "We are not family. And neither are we friends."
Dexter blinked. He was confused. If they weren’t family and they weren’t friends, what else could they be? Colleagues? Acquaintances? Professional contacts?
Then he could feel Rachel smirking through the phone.
"We were involved," she said.
Dexter’s stride stopped.
He was standing on the sidewalk, three houses from his bungalow, his phone pressed against his ear, his brain processing two words that had just rearranged his understanding of two women he knew.
"Involved?" he repeated.
"With each other," Rachel clarified. "For a while. Just casually. Nothing too serious."
She paused.
"She’s more busy now. And I also like someone else. So the fling had to eventually cut off."
Dexter was stunned.
Rachel. Who had kissed him at the hotel bar and Aurora, the S-Rank hero of this generation.
These two women had been involved with each other.
Romantically and casually too!
"Fling?" Dexter said. The word came out as a question, but it wasn’t really a question. It was a verbal placeholder. A sound produced by a brain that needed a few more seconds to process.
"Yeah," Rachel confirmed. Her voice was relaxed as she spoke.
"I’m not just straight, you know?," she said. "I am also bi."
Dexter felt something spark in his mind as his body trembled slightly.
Rachel was bisexual, which meant she was attracted to both men and women.
"Yeah, I’m also bi. That means I can be with a man or a woman. And I’m also comfortable sharing my man..."
The sentence trailed off deliberately and Dexter’s brain completed the sentence.

His brain completed it in multiple ways. Several of which were extremely inappropriate. All of which were immediately suppressed by the disciplined, practiced, iron-fisted mental filter that he had spent twenty years developing in the Ashford estate!
But the spark remained.

The implication hung in the air between the phone and his ear. Rachel was comfortable sharing. Sharing. A word that, in the context she had established, carried a very specific, very clear, very loaded meaning.
Dexter swallowed.
"Rachel," he said. His voice was controlled. Steady. The voice of a man who was absolutely not going to engage with the implication. "Is there a specific reason you’re telling me this?"

"Because I wanted to be honest with you," Rachel said. Her tone had shifted. The teasing edge was still there, but beneath it was something more genuine. More sincere. "I didn’t want you to find out from someone else and think I was hiding something."
She paused.

"I am also bi."
Dexter felt something spark in his mind as his body trembled slightly.
Rachel was bisexual, which meant she was attracted to both men and women.
"Yeah, I’m also bi.
That means I can be with a man or a woman.
And I’m also comfortable sharing my man..."
The sentence trailed off deliberately and Dexter’s brain completed the sentence.
His brain completed it in multiple ways.
Several of which were extremely inappropriate.
All of which were immediately suppressed by the disciplined, practiced, iron-fisted mental filter that he had spent twenty years developing in the Ashford estate!
But the spark remained.
The implication hung in the air between the phone and his ear.
Rachel was comfortable sharing.
Sharing.
A word that, in the context she had established, carried a very specific, very clear, very loaded meaning.
Dexter swallowed.
"Rachel," he said.
His voice was controlled.
Steady.
The voice of a man who was absolutely not going to engage with the implication.
"Is there a specific reason you’re telling me this?"
"Because I wanted to be honest with you," Rachel said.
Her tone had shifted.
The teasing edge was still there, but beneath it was something more genuine.
More sincere.
"I didn’t want you to find out from someone else and think I was hiding something."
She paused.

chapters.title: Chapter 226 | Suspicious Individuals
paragraphs: "Aurora and I were involved. It’s over now. But we still talk and share information. Which is how she knew about you, and which is how I know she met with you."
Another pause.

"I like you, Dexter. I’ve made that pretty clear. I’m not going to pretend I don’t. But I also respect that you have three wives and that your situation is complicated. I’m not trying to insert myself into your household."
Her voice softened.
"I just want you to know that if you ever need anything, whether it’s a friend, a contact, a business partner, or... something more. I’m available. In whatever capacity you need me."
Dexter stood on the sidewalk. Even after what she said, he remained silent for a while and then spoke.
"I’ll keep that in mind," he said.
Rachel laughed softly. "That’s all I ask."
"Okay," she said. "I called mainly cause I wasworried when I saw your name along with the file on Harvest Homes. That’s why I called."
"Thank you for being worried," Dexter said. "I’ll talk to you later, yeah?"
"Okay, talk to you later." Rachel paused. "And don’t forget. You promised me we’d go out sometime."
Dexter immediately replied. "I didn’t promise you anything. But if I have time, I’ll let you know."
Rachel seemed to smile happily at that.
"Bye, Dexter."
"Bye."
The call ended.
Dexter pocketed his phone and resumed walking. His mind was still processing the conversation. Rachel was bisexual and had been involved with Aurora.
’She’s truly a temptress.’
He could even hear other people screaming ’pass the remote.’ In his mind.
He shook his head and continued to move. He was halfway down the block when he saw them.
Two figures walked past him, heading in opposite directions towards the bakery.
They were dressed completely in black. Black shirts. Black pants. Black boots. Black hoods pulled up over their heads, obscuring their faces.
Dexter frowned as they passed.
His Enhanced Hearing, always partially active, registered their heartbeats as they walked by and his mana affinity immediately recognized their realms.
Peak Superhuman Realm.
Both of them.

Dexter’s frown deepened. He turned his head slightly, tracking their movement as they continued past him without acknowledgment. They didn’t look at him, glance in his direction, or register his existence. They simply walked, their hoods low, their pace unhurried, their trajectory aimed precisely at the bakery ahead.
’What are two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators doing in this neighborhood?’

This was not the mid-district. This was not the commercial center. This was the outer ring, where families lived on modest incomes and the most dangerous thing on the street was the occasional stray dog.

Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators did not wander through outer-ring neighborhoods without a reason. They were too valuable. Too well-employed. Too busy taking high-paying dungeon contracts and Association missions to waste time walking through streets where the most exciting event of the day was the bakery opening at dawn.
’But the bakery just started selling Enchanted Meals. Maybe they came to buy.’

The thought was reasonable. His meals had been selling well. The reputation was spreading. Word of mouth in a city like Stargate City traveled fast, especially when the product was genuinely effective. Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators might have heard about the Grade One meals and come to try them.
’That’s probably it. Nothing suspicious. Just customers.’
Dexter smiled at his own paranoia.
’My meals are going viral. Two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators came to buy my food. That’s nice.’
He was about to continue home when his Enhanced Hearing caught something.
A scream.
Short. Sharp. Cut off almost as soon as it began. Not the scream of a crowd or a performance or a child playing. The scream of a single voice. Female. Young. Coming from the direction of the bakery.
Dexter’s expression changed.

His body moved before his brain finished processing. The decision to act was not conscious. It was reflexive. The particular, instant, full-body response of a man who had spent weeks fighting monsters and assassins and whose nervous system had been rewired to treat sudden sounds as immediate threats.
He flashed toward the bakery.

Not walked. Not jogged. Flashed. Using a suppressed version of Flame Burst Step that was calibrated for short-distance, civilian-adjacent movement. Fast enough to cover two blocks in seconds. Slow enough to avoid creating a sonic boom that would shatter every window on the street.
He reached the bakery in under ten seconds.

The front of the shop was still crowded. Customers milled around the display cases. The staff behind the counter were serving. Everything looked normal. Everything sounded normal. The ambient noise of a busy bakery in the middle of its morning rush.
But Tessa was not behind the counter.
Dexter’s eyes swept the room. Left. Right. Behind the pastry display. Near the ovens. In the hallway.
No Tessa.

The staff at the counter noticed him. They recognized him. He had been here twice before. They knew he was connected to the owner. They paid him no special attention as he moved through the shop with the focused, purposeful stride of a man who knew exactly where he was going.
He entered the narrow hallway. Passed the ovens. Passed the flour-dusted prep stations. Reached the storage room.
Empty.
The thermal shelves were there. His meals were there. But Tessa was not.

Dexter’s hearing expanded. He pushed the range outward, filtering through the layers of ambient sound. The hum of the refrigerators. The click of the ovens. The murmur of customers in the front. The traffic outside.
And beneath all of it, coming from further back. From behind the bakery. From the backyard.
Movement. Bodies. The sounds of physical contact. The particular, dense, heavy sounds of a fight.
Dexter didn’t hesitate.
He burst through the back door.

The backyard of the bakery was a small, enclosed space. A concrete patio. A few empty crates. A dumpster. A clothesline where aprons were hung to dry. Not large. Not designed for combat. The kind of space where a baker stepped out for fresh air between batches.

chapters.title: Chapter 227 | Dangerous Tessa
paragraphs: Dexter burst through the door and stopped.
The scene that greeted him was not what he expected.
Two bodies lay on the concrete.

Both of them were the figures in black. The two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators who had walked past him on the street moments ago. They were on the ground. Motionless. One was face down. The other was on his back, eyes open, staring at the sky with the blank, unfocused gaze of a person whose consciousness had been violently and comprehensively removed.
Their hoods had fallen back, revealing two faces that Dexter didn’t recognize. Both male too and they were unconscious!
And standing over them, crouched between the two fallen bodies, one hand on the first man’s chest and the other rummaging through the second man’s pockets, was Tessa.
She was searching them calmly as her fingers moved through the man’s pockets with experience and excitement.
The back door slammed against the wall as Dexter burst through.
Tessa looked up.
Her green eyes met his.
"Oh. Dexter. Hi." She blinked. "You’re still here? I thought you’d left already."
Dexter stood in the doorway and his eyes moved from Tessa to the two unconscious bodies on the ground.
He walked forward slowly, clearly stunne by what he was seeing. It wasn’t a while before the question registered in his mind.
"No," Dexter said. "I was about to leave when I saw the two suspicious people coming into your bakery. I was worried."
He looked at the bodies again.
"But it seems I was worried for nothing. Who are these guys?"
Tessa shrugged. The gesture was casual. Easy. The shrug of a sixteen-year-old girl who had been asked about something she considered trivial.
"I have no idea. They probably came to rob the store. Which is why they are here. So I had to retaliate."
Dexter stared at her.
Then he stared at the bodies.
Then he stared at her again.
"Tessa. These two are Peak Superhuman Realm."
"I know.
"Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators don’t rob ordinary bakeries."

Tessa blinked. Her green eyes widened. The expression was cute. Innocent. The particular, artless innocence of a girl who had been presented with a logical objection and was choosing to address it with an answer that was technically plausible but practically absurd.
"Maybe they really needed money desperately," she said. "You know. Addicts. Addicts do stupid things just to get a fix."
Dexter looked at her.

He looked at the two bodies on the ground. Both were well-built. Well-fed. Well-equipped. Their clothing was high-quality. Their boots were reinforced. Neither showed signs of malnourishment, desperation, or the physical deterioration that accompanied substance addiction.
These were not addicts.
These were professionals.
And they had been taken down by a sixteen-year-old girl in an apron.
"Tessa," Dexter said carefully. "You can defeat Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators?"
In his mind, the calculations were running.

Two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators. If Dexter fought them simultaneously, going all out, using his bloodline, his techniques, his Type-5 weapon, he would win. But it would take time. At least a minute.
But Tessa had dealt with both of them in under thirty seconds. Less. From the time he had heard the scream to the time he had burst through the back door, approximately fifteen seconds had elapsed.
Fifteen seconds.
For a 17-year-old girl who was supposedly an ordinary baker’s daughter.
’Who exactly is this girl?’

Tessa looked at him, her green eyes were bright. Carrying that same, enigmatic quality that he had noticed the first day they met. The quality that said ’I am more than I appear’ without actually saying it.
"Aw, Dexter." She tilted her head. "Were you really worried about me? I knew you cared about me."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Obviously, I was trying to make sure you weren’t getting kidnapped or something. But obviously I was worried for no reason."
He looked at the bodies one more time. Then at Tessa. Then at the bodies.
"Should we call the cops?"
Tessa immediately shook her head.
"No. Me and my dad will handle it."

She straightened up from her crouch. Brushed dust from her apron. Adjusted the loose ribbon in her hair. The transition from combatant to baker’s daughter was seamless. Instant. As though the fight had been a minor inconvenience, like spilling flour or dropping a tray, and had already been filed under "handled" in her mind.
Then she smiled at Dexter. The warm, bright, dimpled smile that he had come to associate with all things Tessa.
"Do you want to try some of our pastries? I made a special batch this time. Maybe you can give them to your wives if you don’t want to eat them yourself."
Dexter stared at her.

He stared at her for a long time. Long enough that Tessa’s smile began to carry a trace of something beneath its surface. Not discomfort. Not guilt. Just the quiet awareness of being evaluated by someone who was paying very close attention.

’She took down two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators in fifteen seconds. She’s searching their pockets instead of calling the police. She’s offering me pastries. She’s 17. Her father is a baker. Grandma Lucy can disperse Ultra-Rank auras with a tap of her finger. Her house was untouched during the monster outbreak.’
’Nothing about this neighborhood is what it seems.’
Dexter shook his head.
"There’s no need for that. I’ll take my leave."

He pointed toward the street. Then sighed. The sigh was not from frustration. It was from the particular, accumulated exhaustion of a man who had been discovering secrets all week and had just found another one.
He walked toward the back gate that led to the street. His stride was measured. Unhurried. The stride of a man who was choosing to leave rather than being driven away.
Tessa’s voice followed him.
"Bye, Dexter!"
He raised a hand without looking back. "Take care of yourself."
"I will!"
Her cheerful voice rang through the backyard, following him as Tessa waved enthusiastically at him.

Dexter reached the street. He paused. Turned back. Looked at the bakery. The facade was the same as always. Warm. Inviting. The smell of fresh bread drifting from the open door. Customers coming and going. The display cases full. The morning rush in full swing.
Everything looked normal.
Everything was not normal.

’Two Peak Superhuman Realm cultivators came to the bakery. They were dealt with by a sixteen-year-old girl in under fifteen seconds. She didn’t call the police. She didn’t seem scared. She didn’t seem surprised. She searched their pockets with the practiced ease of someone who had done it before.’
’And she offered me pastries afterward.’
Dexter shook his head.
He turned and walked home.

chapters.title: Chapter 228 | Sorry, I Shouldn’t Have
paragraphs: Dexter reached his bungalow in two minutes.
He opened the gate, walked up the path, and pushed open the front door.
"I’m home."
The living room greeted him with its usual quiet and the Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact hummed softly on its shelf.

He looked to the left and saw Mira in her wheelchair by the window with her eyes closed. Cultivating. Her crimson hair caught the sunlight and burned like copper wire as her Spectral Arms were folded behind her back, motionless.
The moment he came in, one of her eyes snapped open as she stared at him but the moment she saw him looking at her, she immediately closed it and pretended she hadn’t noticed him.
Dexter laughted quietly. ’Mira...’
He looked toward the living room couch.
Lyra was cross-legged with her eyes closed. The Primordial Beast Egg rested in her lap as she cultivated.
Since she couldn’t hear and her eyes were closed, she had no way of knowing that Dexter had entered the house.
Dexter wanted to extend his thoughts but he chose not to disturb her as she looked really peaceful.
He also noticed, with a pang of guilt, that he hadn’t brought anything for her. Now that he thought about it, he would have accepted the pastries Tessa wanted to give him.
’Next time. I’ll bring pastries next time.’
He shook his head and walked toward the hallway.
The person he kinda wanted to see most at this moment was Selene.
He checked the girls’ room first. Opened the door. Looked inside but there was no one there.
Dexter was a strangely a bit relieved about this.
He closed the door and walked across the hall to his own room.
He opened the door and to bi surprise, Selene was there.

She lay in his bed exactly where he’d left her that morning, sleeping. The duvet he’d draped over her was still there, and her silver-white hair, spread across his pillow in a chaotic tangled cascade, was wrapped around the fabric like a child’s favourite toy.
"Rustle."
She suddenly shifted in her sleep and pulled the duvet higher, covering her shoulders and tucked beneath her chin as she curled into it and slept much like a baby.
Dexter’s lips curled upwards.
He walked to the edge of the bed and looked down at her and she looked like a sleeping angel.
Suddenly, an instinct surged into his mind to reach out and strike her hair.
Without warning, his right arm lifted upward and his fingers spread as he was about to strike her hair!
His fingers were three inches from her head when she turned, he face rotated on the pillow and her eyes fluttered open.

Pale eyes disorientedly opened to the world as her Echolocation talent activated reflexively. A pulse went out. It bounced off the walls, the ceiling, the furniture, and the object hovering three inches from her head.
She saw the arm, Suspended in the air above her hair, in the precise, unmistakable posture of a person who had been about to stroke someone’s head and had been caught in the act.
Selene blinked.
She was still drowsy and her brain was still booting up. But the image, rendered through her Echolocation was clear enough.
She glanced at the arm then Dexter and back at the arm.
Dexter causally retracted his hand like he wasn’t doing anything wrong.
He looked down at her. His expression was neutral as he spoke.
"You’re awake,"

Selene blinked again. Her pale eyes, still foggy with sleep, processed the information. His voice. His presence. The arm that had been reaching for her and was now, very casually, resting at his side.
She nodded.
"Mm-hmm."
Dexter smiled. The warm, gentle smile he reserved for her.
"Good morning. You must be hungry. Should I bring your food here, or do you want to eat at the dining table?
Selene blinked.

"Yeah?" she said. The word came out as a question. Not because she was asking what he had said. Because she was asking what she wanted. The particular, uncertain "yeah" of a person who had just been woken from the best sleep of their life and whose brain was still negotiating the transition between dreams and decisions.
Dexter shrugged. "I don’t mind. You can eat here if you want."
He gestured at the bed. At the warm, comfortable, Dexter-scented bed that she had been sleeping in. The bed that, according to the pillow she had been clutching all night, smelled like him.
Selene was about to respond. About to say something. Maybe yes. Maybe no. Maybe something in between.
Then her brows furrowed.
Her Echolocation pulsed again. Stronger this time. More focused. The pulse swept the room, bouncing off every surface, returning with a three-dimensional map of her surroundings.
The bed was not her bed. The room was not her room. The pillow was not her pillow. The walls were the wrong distance apart. The window was in the wrong position. The door was on the wrong side.
This was Dexter’s room.
The realization hit her with the force of a small, private explosion.
She scrambled out of the bed.
The motion was sudden and quick.

The duvet flew, the pillow slid, her feet hit the floor as she stood beside the bed, her white sleeping gown rumpled and her silver hair in complete disarray, her face flushed a shade of pink that spread from her cheeks to her ears to the visible skin above her collar.
"Sorry," she said.

The word came out fast. Breathy. The apology of a woman who had woken up in her husband’s bed, realized where she was, and was now experiencing the particular, full-body embarrassment that came from knowing she had been sleeping there all night without permission.
"Sorry. I should have... I didn’t mean to..."
Dexter scratched the back of his head.
"It’s all right," he said. "I told you it’s all right. You can stay whenever and for as long as you wish."

He opened the gate, walked up the path, and pushed open the front door.
"I’m home."
The living room greeted him with its usual quiet and the Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact hummed softly on its shelf.
He looked to the left and saw Mira in her wheelchair by the window with her eyes closed.
Cultivating.

The moment he came in, one of her eyes snapped open as she stared at him but the moment she saw him looking at her, she immediately closed it and pretended she hadn’t noticed him.
Dexter laughted quietly. ’Mira...’

Lyra was cross-legged with her eyes closed.
The Primordial Beast Egg rested in her lap as she cultivated.

Dexter wanted to extend his thoughts but he chose not to disturb her as she looked really peaceful.
He also noticed, with a pang of guilt, that he hadn’t brought anything for her.
Now that he thought about it, he would have accepted the pastries Tessa wanted to give him.
’Next time.
I’ll bring pastries next time.’
He shook his head and walked toward the hallway.
The person he kinda wanted to see most at this moment was Selene.
He checked the girls’ room first.
Opened the door.
Looked inside but there was no one there.
Dexter was a strangely a bit relieved about this.
He closed the door and walked across the hall to his own room.
He opened the door and to bi surprise, Selene was there.
She lay in his bed exactly where he’d left her that morning, sleeping.
The duvet he’d draped over her was still there, and her silver-white hair, spread across his pillow in a chaotic tangled cascade, was wrapped around the fabric like a child’s favourite toy.
"Rustle."
She suddenly shifted in her sleep and pulled the duvet higher, covering her shoulders and tucked beneath her chin as she curled into it and slept much like a baby.
Dexter’s lips curled upwards.
He walked to the edge of the bed and looked down at her and she looked like a sleeping angel.
Suddenly, an instinct surged into his mind to reach out and strike her hair.
Without warning, his right arm lifted upward and his fingers spread as he was about to strike her hair!

Pale eyes disorientedly opened to the world as her Echolocation talent activated reflexively.
A pulse went out.

The warm, gentle smile he reserved for her.

chapters.title: Chapter 229 | Reverse
paragraphs: Selene shook her head firmly.
"Even so, its still inappropriate for me to sleep in your bed. And not give you the chance to sleep."
Dexter blinked.
"No, it’s all right," he said. "I also slept."
Selene’s head snapped up as her pale eyes, sightless started at Dexter, stunned.
"You slept?"
Dexter shrugged casually.
"Yeah. I also slept, you slept, so we slept together."
The words left his mouth and silence filled the entire room.
In that split second, Selene’s pale neck flushed read and she wa slightly flustered.
"You..." she stammered. "We... you..."
Dexter’s brain caught up with his mouth.
Approximately one second too late.
He chuckled and quickly clarified things.
"I’m just joking," he said. "We only cultivated together. We cultivated. You fell asleep. I put you to bed. Then I went to the kitchen to make the meals. Then I went outside to deliver them."
He paused. Regrouped.
"We didn’t sleep together."

The clarification was explicit. Unambiguous. Delivered with the deliberate, precise enunciation of a man who was acutely aware that the wrong word or wrong inflection at this moment could result in a frost seizure in his bedroom.
Selene stared at him.

Her pale eyes, still red, still wide, still carrying the particular, stunned expression of a woman whose brain was processing information at approximately three times its normal speed, held his face for a long moment.
Then she exhaled.
"Oh."
The word was soft. Relief. Clear, unmistakable relief. The exhalation of a body that had been bracing for one outcome and received another.

But Dexter, watching her through his Enhanced Hearing, detected something else in that exhale. A trace of something that wasn’t relief. Something that existed in the same frequency as relief but carried a different emotional signature.
Disappointment?
He wasn’t sure. The signal was too faint. Too brief. Too quickly buried beneath the larger, more dominant emotion of embarrassment to be reliably identified.
But it was there.
Or at least, he thought it was there.

Selene straightened her posture. She smoothed her sleeping gown with both hands. She pushed her disheveled hair back from her face. The process of reassembling her composure was visible, like watching someone build a wall brick by brick.

"I want to go freshen up," she said. Her voice was controlled again. Measured. The voice of a woman who had decided that the previous thirty seconds had not happened and was now proceeding with her day as though they hadn’t.
Dexter nodded.
"All right. I’ll have your food prepared at the dining table."
Selene walked out of the room.

She didn’t rush. She didn’t flee. She walked with the careful, measured grace that she always used, her bare feet finding the floor through memory and vibration. But her ears were pink. And the pink didn’t fade until she was well down the hallway.
Dexter stood alone in his bedroom. He stared at the closed door. Then at the rumpled bed. Then at the pillow that Selene had been holding.
The pillow still had the impression of her face in it.
He shook his head.
’She was disappointed. She was actually disappointed that we didn’t sleep together.’

’No. I’m reading too much into it. She was just embarrassed. The disappointment was relief that was misread by my Enhanced Hearing because I was overanalyzing micro-expressions in a woman who can’t make normal facial expressions because she’s blind and communicates through Echolocation and probably doesn’t even know what her face is doing half the time.’
’Or she was disappointed.’
’One of those two.’
He rubbed his face with both hands.
’I need to stop analyzing everything. I’m turning into a one-man surveillance system.’
He walked to the dining room.
He began plating the food. The Grade Five Celestial Phoenix Nectar Bowl for each of the girls. The Harmony Congee alongside it. The Star-Shaped Leaf tea in four cups.
He placed Mira’s bowl at her spot. Then Selene’s. Then Lyra’s. Then his own.
As he was setting Selene’s portion on the table, he felt something.
A gaze.
Not a sound. Not a vibration. Not a telepathic ping. A gaze. The particular, weighty, unmistakable sensation of being watched by someone who was waiting for you to notice them.
He turned around.

Lyra was sitting on the couch in the living room. Her dark eyes were open. The Primordial Beast Egg was still in her lap, but her cultivation had clearly been interrupted by the smell of food wafting from the kitchen.
She was staring at him.

Not at the food. At him. Through the living room, across the hallway, and into the dining room. Her dark eyes, behind the AI glasses, were locked onto his face with an expression that was simultaneously expectant and innocent.
The expression of a woman who wanted something to eat and was waiting for permission.
Dexter chuckled.
He projected his thoughts toward her through their telepathic connection.
"Do you want to eat?"

Lyra’s face immediately brightened. The transformation was instant. The serene, meditative composure of a cultivator dissolved, replaced by the eager, luminous enthusiasm of a woman who had been offered food.
She nodded. Rapidly. Her dark hair bounced. Her eyes sparkled.
"Can I eat too?" she asked as her telepathic voice carried the particular, hopeful quality of a child asking if it was time for dessert.
Dexter smiled. "Of course."
Lyra’s face broke into a full smile, glowing like the sun itself.
She stood from the couch, egg in arm, and walked toward the dining room with excitement in her eyes.
Mira, who had been sitting in her wheelchair by the window with her eyes closed in what was supposed to be cultivation but was clearly eavesdropping!
She looked at Dexter then at Lyra but her expression was one of indifference as though she wasn’t interested in what theh were talking about.
Dexter saw her expression and he smirked.
"You’re free not to eat with us if you don’t want to," he said casually but was clearly using reverse psychology on her.
Mira’s eye narrowed.
"I wasn’t eating," she said.

chapters.title: Chapter 230 | Do You Girls Want Massages?
paragraphs: Dexter shrugged. "So you don’t want to eat?"
"I didn’t say that either."
Dexter chuckled from the kitchen. He shook his head at the non-answer.
"Understood," he said. "I’ll set a plate down for you anyway."
He placed Mira’s bowl at her spot at the table. Then went to collect the tea.
By the time he returned, Mira’s food wasn’t at the dining table any longer she had taken it to the living room and was eating currently with her free arm.
Dexter said nothing.
He sat down at his own spot.
Lyra was already eating. Her spoon moved in a blur. The Grade Five meal disappeared from her bowl with speed.
Dexter blinked his eyes at the girl then at her chest and then shook his head with a small smile.

Selene emerged from the bathroom, her hair damp but her face clean. She’d swapped her sleeping gown for a simple white blouse and dark skirt, looking fresh and rested. The pink in her cheeks had faded to a natural healthy tone, slightly deeper than usual, Dexter noted.
She saw Dexter and lowered her head as she sat at the table. Found her bowl and picked up her spoon.
The three of them ate in silence and when Lyra asked for more, Dexter served her seconds without comment.
Selene ate slowly, tasting the food first and her eyes widened slightly as she spok.
"This is different," she said quietly.
Dexter looked at her. "It’s a new recipe."
Selene tilted her head.
"It’s really good," she said. "It feels... warm. Inside. Not temperature warm. Something else."
She took another spoonful.
"I’m glad you liked it." he said.
Then Dexter set his spoon down as he looked at Lyra, then at Selene.
"I want to ask you both something," he said.
Lyra’s spoon paused mid-air. Selene’s head tilted toward him.

"The massage technique I use on Mira is different." Dexter continued. "The 108 Body Massage Sutra. It stimulates healing at a cellular level. Increases nerve regeneration. Improves blood circulation. Accelerates the body’s natural recovery processes by alot."
He paused. Chose his words carefully.

"If I apply the same technique to both of you, your healing rates would increase significantly. Selene, your frost condition might stabilize faster. The countdown to your next crisis could be extended further. Lyra, your overall recovery would accelerate."
He looked at them.
"Do you want me to give you massages?"
The question landed on the table like a stone in still water.
Lyra’s spoon clattered against the rim of her bowl.

Her dark eyes went wide. Her cheeks flushed. The pink started at her neck and climbed upward with the relentless, unstoppable progression of a woman whose circulatory system had decided to publicly broadcast her emotional state.
She was shy.
Not the mild, social shyness that characterized her usual interactions. The deep, full-body, can’t-make-eye-contact shyness of a woman who had just been asked if she wanted a man’s hands on her body.

Her mouth opened and closed but no sound escaped. This was because her vocal cords were damaged and the telepathic connection was experiencing technical difficulties. The volume of simultaneous emotional signals was overwhelming her brain’s transmission capacity.
She sat in her chair, her spoon in her hand, her face the color of a ripe tomato, and stared at her bowl as though it contained the answers to every question ever asked by humanity.
Selene was different.

Her initial reaction was similar. A faint flush appeared on her pale cheeks. Her fingers tightened slightly around her spoon. Her head, which had been tilted toward Dexter, tilted further, angling downward in the particular, self-conscious dip of a woman who was processing an unexpected proposition.
But she recovered faster.
Her Echolocation pulsed once. Twice. Mapping the room. Confirming the distance between herself and Dexter. Establishing the spatial parameters of the request.
Then she nodded.

"If it might work," she said. Her voice was quiet. Careful. The voice of a woman who was weighing the practical benefits against the personal implications and arriving at a conclusion that prioritized healing over discomfort. "Then there is no harm in trying."
Dexter looked at her. She was still looking at the table. Her cheeks were still pink. But her posture had settled. Her breathing was steady. She had made a decision and was committing to it.
He turned to Lyra.

Lyra was still staring at her bowl. Her face was still crimson. Her spoon was still frozen in the air. The telepathic silence continued, suggesting that her brain was still running the emotional equivalent of a system reboot.
Dexter waited.
Five seconds passed.
Ten seconds.

Lyra’s spoon descended to the bowl. She set it down. Her hands moved to her lap, where they clasped together tightly. Her dark eyes, still wide, still carrying the particular, luminous intensity of a woman whose entire nervous system was processing a significant emotional event, lifted from the bowl and found Dexter’s face.
She nodded.
One small, barely perceptible dip of her chin.

The nod was accompanied by a telepathic transmission. A single word. Fragile. Trembling. Spoken with the cautious, tentative delivery of someone who was agreeing to something they wanted but were terrified of wanting.
"Okay."
Dexter smiled.
"Good," he said. His voice was warm. Gentle. Carefully calibrated to convey reassurance without pressure. "Whenever you are ready, come meet me. No rush. Anytime."
He paused.
"Lyra, you don’t have to be nervous. It’s a medical procedure. I’ve been doing it on Mira for two weeks. It’s completely professional."

The word "professional" was, in retrospect, possibly not the most reassuring word he could have chosen. Because Lyra’s face immediately went from pink to a shade of red that suggested her circulatory system had abandoned all pretense of normal function.
She stood up.
The motion was abrupt. Sudden. The particular, explosive evacuation of a chair that occurred when a woman’s fight-or-flight response had been triggered and the flight option had won by default.
She grabbed the Primordial Beast Egg from beside her bowl. Clutched it against her chest. Her dark eyes met Dexter’s for one brief, mortified second.
Then she fled.
Her bare feet slapped against the hallway floor. The bedroom door opened. Closed. The faint sound of her body landing on the mattress was followed by silence.
Dexter stared at the empty chair.
He looked at Selene.

Selene was still at the table. Her pale eyes were aimed at her empty bowl. Her expression was composed. Serene. The expression of a woman who had just watched her sister-wife flee the room in embarrassment and was choosing to process the moment with dignity.
Then, very faintly, the corner of her lip twitched.

It was not a smile. It was not a smirk. It was the particular, barely perceptible micro-expression that appeared on Selene’s face when she found something amusing but was too refined to acknowledge it openly.
Dexter caught it.
He caught it because he had spent three weeks studying her face. Learning the topography of her expressions. Mapping the subtle, almost invisible movements that constituted her emotional vocabulary.
She was amused.
’She’s laughing at Lyra. Internally. Without moving a single facial muscle.’
’And probably at me too.’
Dexter shook his head.
"I’ll be in my room when you’re ready," he said to Selene. "Take your time."
Selene nodded slowly.
Dexter collected the dishes and carried them to the kitchen. He washed them in silence. The water ran. The soap foamed. The sponge moved in circles.
He thought about what he had just done.
He had offered to massage two women who were not Mira. The same offer that, twenty-four hours ago, had triggered a spike of jealousy so intense that the temperature in the room had visibly increased.
Mira was at the window.
She had heard.
Mira continued eating.
She said nothing but the silence was louder than any comment could have been.
Dexter dried the dishes. Placed them on the rack. Turned off the kitchen light.
He walked past Mira on his way to the hallway.
"Ready for your massage in an hour," he said.

It was not a question. It was a schedule. Delivered with the calm, matter-of-fact authority of a man who was not going to ask permission because asking permission would open the door to refusal, and refusal was not on the agenda today.
Mira’s Spectral Arms folded behind her back.
Tighter than usual.
"I didn’t say I wanted one," she said.
Dexter stopped walking.
He turned. Her rigid posture, folded Spectral Arms and crimson eyes fixed on the window with a determined gaze suggested she was desperately trying to focus on something other than him.
"You didn’t say you didn’t want one either," he replied.
Mira’s jaw tightened.
"I’ll be in your room in an hour," Dexter said. "If you’re not there, I’ll come find you."
He turned and walked down the hallway.
Behind him, the temperature in the living room increased by two degrees.
Dexter smiled.
’I’m going to pay for that later.’
’But it was worth it.’

Her cheeks flushed.
The pink started at her neck and climbed upward with the relentless, unstoppable progression of a woman whose circulatory system had decided to publicly broadcast her emotional state.
She was shy.
Not the mild, social shyness that characterized her usual interactions.
The deep, full-body, can’t-make-eye-contact shyness of a woman who had just been asked if she wanted a man’s hands on her body.
Her mouth opened and closed but no sound escaped.
This was because her vocal cords were damaged and the telepathic connection was experiencing technical difficulties.
The volume of simultaneous emotional signals was overwhelming her brain’s transmission capacity.
She sat in her chair, her spoon in her hand, her face the color of a ripe tomato, and stared at her bowl as though it contained the answers to every question ever asked by humanity.
Selene was different.
Her initial reaction was similar.
A faint flush appeared on her pale cheeks.
Her fingers tightened slightly around her spoon.
Her head, which had been tilted toward Dexter, tilted further, angling downward in the particular, self-conscious dip of a woman who was processing an unexpected proposition.
But she recovered faster.
Her Echolocation pulsed once.
Twice.
Mapping the room.
Confirming the distance between herself and Dexter.
Establishing the spatial parameters of the request.
Then she nodded.
"If it might work," she said.
Her voice was quiet.
Careful.
The voice of a woman who was weighing the practical benefits against the personal implications and arriving at a conclusion that prioritized healing over discomfort.
"Then there is no harm in trying."
Dexter looked at her.
She was still looking at the table.
Her cheeks were still pink.
But her posture had settled.
Her breathing was steady.
She had made a decision and was committing to it.
He turned to Lyra.
Lyra was still staring at her bowl.
Her face was still crimson.
Her spoon was still frozen in the air.
The telepathic silence continued, suggesting that her brain was still running the emotional equivalent of a system reboot.
Dexter waited.
Five seconds passed.
Ten seconds.
Lyra’s spoon descended to the bowl.
She set it down.
Her hands moved to her lap, where they clasped together tightly.

Her dark eyes, still wide, still carrying the particular, luminous intensity of a woman whose entire nervous system was processing a significant emotional event, lifted from the bowl and found Dexter’s face.
She nodded.
One small, barely perceptible dip of her chin.
The nod was accompanied by a telepathic transmission.
A single word.
Fragile.
Trembling.
Spoken with the cautious, tentative delivery of someone who was agreeing to something they wanted but were terrified of wanting.
"Okay."
Dexter smiled.
"Good," he said.
His voice was warm.
Gentle.
Carefully calibrated to convey reassurance without pressure.
"Whenever you are ready, come meet me.
No rush.
Anytime."
He paused.
"Lyra, you don’t have to be nervous.
It’s a medical procedure.
I’ve been doing it on Mira for two weeks.
It’s completely professional."
The word "professional" was, in retrospect, possibly not the most reassuring word he could have chosen.
Because Lyra’s face immediately went from pink to a shade of red that suggested her circulatory system had abandoned all pretense of normal function.
She stood up.
The motion was abrupt.
Sudden.
The particular, explosive evacuation of a chair that occurred when a woman’s fight-or-flight response had been triggered and the flight option had won by default.
She grabbed the Primordial Beast Egg from beside her bowl.
Clutched it against her chest.
Her dark eyes met Dexter’s for one brief, mortified second.
Then she fled.
Her bare feet slapped against the hallway floor.
The bedroom door opened.
Closed.
The faint sound of her body landing on the mattress was followed by silence.
Dexter stared at the empty chair.
He looked at Selene.
Selene was still at the table.
Her pale eyes were aimed at her empty bowl.
Her expression was composed.
Serene.
The expression of a woman who had just watched her sister-wife flee the room in embarrassment and was choosing to process the moment with dignity.
Then, very faintly, the corner of her lip twitched.
It was not a smile.
It was not a smirk.
It was the particular, barely perceptible micro-expression that appeared on Selene’s face when she found something amusing but was too refined to acknowledge it openly.
Dexter caught it.
He caught it because he had spent three weeks studying her face.
Learning the topography of her expressions.
Mapping the subtle, almost invisible movements that constituted her emotional vocabulary.
She was amused.
’She’s laughing at Lyra.
Internally.
Without moving a single facial muscle.’
’And probably at me too.’
Dexter shook his head.
"I’ll be in my room when you’re ready," he said to Selene.
"Take your time."
Selene nodded slowly.
Dexter collected the dishes and carried them to the kitchen.
He washed them in silence.
The water ran.
The soap foamed.
The sponge moved in circles.
He thought about what he had just done.
He had offered to massage two women who were not Mira.
The same offer that, twenty-four hours ago, had triggered a spike of jealousy so intense that the temperature in the room had visibly increased.
Mira was at the window.
She had heard.
Mira continued eating.
She said nothing but the silence was louder than any comment could have been.
Dexter dried the dishes.
Placed them on the rack.
Turned off the kitchen light.
He walked past Mira on his way to the hallway.
"Ready for your massage in an hour," he said.
It was not a question.
It was a schedule.
Delivered with the calm, matter-of-fact authority of a man who was not going to ask permission because asking permission would open the door to refusal, and refusal was not on the agenda today.
Mira’s Spectral Arms folded behind her back.
Tighter than usual.
"I didn’t say I wanted one," she said.
Dexter stopped walking.
He turned.
Her rigid posture, folded Spectral Arms and crimson eyes fixed on the window with a determined gaze suggested she was desperately trying to focus on something other than him.
"You didn’t say you didn’t want one either," he replied.
Mira’s jaw tightened.
"I’ll be in your room in an hour," Dexter said.
"If you’re not there, I’ll come find you."
He turned and walked down the hallway.
Behind him, the temperature in the living room increased by two degrees.
Dexter smiled.
’I’m going to pay for that later.’
’But it was worth it.’

chapters.title: Chapter 231 | Rewards...
paragraphs: Dexter went to his room and sat on the bed.
He had been so consumed by yesterday and also this morning’s events, that he had completely forgotten about the system reward.
"System, open reward."
Golden text materialized in the air before him and Dexter’s mind went blank.
He blinked his eyes and cleaned his eyes to see if what he was seeing was true.
’What the heck? Just two rewards?’
Dexter scratched the back of his head clearly stunned and confused.
For the past several days, the system had been generous with its rewards. Each day brought a cascade of returns that had transformed him from his previous weakling status to his new found strength.
But today, the system had only given him two rewards instead of the usual ten plus.
He looked at the first reward.
’Sigh! Let’s just check why I got.’
[Reward 1: Lifespan Extension — Ten Additional Years]
Dexter stared at the notification as he pursed his lips.

Ten years was not insignificant. In the cultivation world, where breakthroughs between major realms could take decades and where the most powerful experts lived for centuries, ten years was nice but for a twenty-year-old man it wasn’t all that valuable.
Then he looked at the second.
[Reward 2: Dual Avatar Fruit]
[Grade: 8 ]

[Description: A legendary fruit born from the convergence of life energy and dimensional mana. When consumed, the fruit grants the user the ability to create a second physical body that is completely independent from the first.]’’
[Effects:]
[• The second body is a perfect physical replica of the user’s primary body]
[• The second body possesses its own independent mana reserves, cultivation base, and talent]
[• The second body can operate independently, at any distance, without affecting the primary body]
[• Damage to one body does not transfer to the other]
[• The user’s consciousness can shift between bodies at will]
[• Both bodies share the same soul, creating an unbreakable telepathic link between them]
Dexter’s hand trembled slightly. An actual grade 8 fruit? Dexter had never expected the system would give him a grade 8 fruit this early!
The Avatar Fruit could create a second body. A complete, independent, fully functional second body. With its own mana. Its own cultivation. Its own talent.
His mind went immediately to Aurelyx.
’If I give this fruit to Aurelyx, she could separate from Lyra’s body. She could have her own physical form. No more two consciousnesses fighting for control of one body.’
’Lyra would be free. Aurelyx would be free. Both of them, in their own bodies, living their own lives.’

The thought was intoxicating as this was the solution to the problem that had been consuming him since the night Aurelyx had appeared in his bedroom and kissed him and revealed herself as the Shadow Queen.
And now the solution was sitting in his hand. In the form of a fruit.
But.
Dexter’s excitement cooled.
’But I don’t know Aurelyx’s intentions.’
From what he could tell, Aurelyx was not a good person.
Giving her an independent body meant giving her freedom. Freedom to move, to act, to kill, without the limitation of having to surface from inside another person’s consciousness.
An Aurelyx with her own body was an Aurelyx unleashed.
’And I don’t know her true strength.’
This was the critical unknown. When Aurelyx was inside Lyra’s body, she was constrained by Lyra’s physical condition. Whatever power Aurelyx possessed, it was filtered through a broken vessel.
But if Aurelyx had her own body, a body created by the Avatar Fruit, a body with its own independent mana reserves and cultivation base, she would be at full power. Whatever that power was.
’The number one assassin in the city. At full power. With her own body. Answering to no one.’
’That might be worse than the current situation.’
Dexter closed his eyes.
He couldn’t give her the fruit. Not yet. Not without more information. He needed to understand Aurelyx first.
He needed to observe.
He needed to learn how the switching worked. When it happened. Why it happened. What triggered Aurelyx’s emergence and what caused her retreat.
He didn’t know any of this. And until he did, the Avatar Fruit would stay in his spatial storage.
Dexter placed the fruit in his spatial storage. The golden text faded. The system interface closed.
He sat on his bed for a moment, staring at the wall.
’I was expecting more rewards. I was hoping for a cultivation boost. Something that would push me past the Superhuman Realm and into Ultra.’

The disappointment was manageable. The system’s rewards were not predictable. They came in waves. Some days brought a flood. Others brought a trickle. The system didn’t operate on a schedule. It operated on investment. On the significance of his actions. On the depth of his care.

The past two days had been extraordinary in terms of events but perhaps less extraordinary in terms of investment. The kiss with Aurelyx had been detected by the system, but it had been attributed to Lyra.

Perhaps the past two days had been too chaotic by external events, the Harvest Homes fight, the squad meeting, Aurora’s proposition, Rachel’s call, Tessa’s secret, for the system to register the kind of deep, focused investment that triggered major rewards.
Dexter closed his eyes and began cultivating.

He cultivated for an hour. The mana flowed. His body strengthened. His mind settled. The cultivation was productive, even without a system boost. His SS-Rank mana affinity made absorption effortless. Every breath drew in energy. Every heartbeat distributed it through his system.
The alarm on his phone rang.
Dexter opened his eyes. Checked the time. One hour had passed. It was time for Mira’s massage.
He stood up. Walked to the door. Opened it. Stepped into the hallway.
Opposite his room was the girls’ bedroom. The door was closed.

He had expected it to remain closed. He had expected Mira to ignore his instruction. To stay at the window. To refuse to come. To maintain the sulk that had been her default state since the massage discussion the previous evening.

chapters.title: Chapter 232 | I Will Seduce You In A Month
paragraphs: Mira was stubborn, proud and also territorial. She did not respond well to being told what to do and did not appreciate having her exclusive ritual shared with other women.
Dexter had told her, one hour, my room, and had walked away without waiting for a response. As usual, Mira would never obey him.
He walked to the girls’ bedroom, opened the door and was stunned.
Mira was actually in the room!
She was in her wheelchair, parked directly beside the bed, waiting for him with her eyes closed.
Dexter blinked and then he smiled softly.
’She had actually listened to me.’
Maybe it’s because she hed heard him promised the other two girls massages but whatever the reason was, it was a good thing.
Dexter obviously wanted to tease her but paused and eventually decided not to say anything.
He walked to the wheelchair, stood behind it and placed his hands on the handles.
"I’m going to carry you now," he said softly.
Mira didn’t open her eyes but she let out a ’hmph’ sound and turned her face away.
Dexter smile widened at her cute act of anger.
He lifted her from the wheelchair and carried her, then placed her on the bed.
Afterwhich, he began removing her clothing.
This morning, he had dressed her in the outfit she preferred. A white cropped top, black leather skirt and a black choker.
He removed the cropped top first and watched as the fabric slid over her head, revealing the white sports bra beneath.
Then he removed the skirt, unzipped it carefully, sliding the leather down over her hips and supple legs.
Mira lay on the bed in her sports bra and briefs. Her crimson hair on the pillow and her eyes closed.
Dexter then wore the Shockwave Glove as mana-threads tightened around his knuckles and activated it with mana.
He applied the Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil to his hands, set the glove to its lowest vibration setting and began.

Her Shoulders first. His oiled fingers pressed into the dense muscle where her neck met her shoulders as the shockwave Glove hummed and the Massage Sutra guided his movements through the precise, prescribed pattern.
Mira’s body was familiar to him now. Every pressure point, meridian pathway. He knew where she was tense, she was sore, the nerve damage was deepest and where the healing was furthest along.
Mira’s right arm lay on the mattress beside her body. It was no longer completely motionless. The fingers twitched occasionally.
He worked down her spine. Vertebra by vertebra.
Dexter increased the intensity slightly. The glove hummed louder as the vibration reached the deep tissue layers along her lumbar region.
A sound escaped Mira’s lips.
Dexter paused for a bit and then continued. After a while, he spoke.
"Mira,"
"What?"
"The marks on your back.
Her eyes opened.
"What about them?"
"Have they changed?"
Her expression changed slightly.
"They’re bigger," she said quietly.
Dexter nodded.
The bloodline was progressing and the marks were growing.
"How much bigger?"
Dexter fingers measured the length. From the top of her shoulder blade to the bottom of the mark.
"Two inches," he said. "They were ten inches yesterday. They’re twelve now."
Two inches of growth in twenty-four hours.
At this rate, the bloodline would fully manifest within a month. Possibly less.

Mira said nothing. She simply nodded as he worked her legs, thighs, calves and feet. The muscles there were still atrophied, but the Massage Sutra was stimulating blood flow and nerve activity. With continued treatment, the legs would eventually respond.
He finished, cleaned the oil from her skin, dressed her, carried her to her wheelchair.
Mira sat in her chair. Her crimson eyes opened. She looked at nothing in particular.
"Thank you," she said.
"You’re welcome," Dexter replied.
He wheeled her to the living room. Positioned her by the window which is her favorite spot.
But instead of walking away, he had walked back to her and then knelt down to her level.
His dark eyes looking directly into her closed eyes.
Mira had just closed her eyes when she settled into her spot. But she felt his gaze.
She opened her eyes and saw him kneeling there, right in front of her.
She frowned.
"What do you want this time?"
Dexter smiled.
"Can’t I just look at my wife?" he said. "Can’t I stare at my wife without wanting anything?"
Mira sneered.
"Pervert," she said. "Liar."
But her face flushed slightly as she closed her eyes and ignored him. .
Pretended to concentrate. Resumed the mask of cultivation.
Thirty seconds passed.
But Dexter’s gaze was still on her.
She opened her eyes and immediately glared at him.
"It seems you don’t have any work to do, right?"
Dexter shrugged casually.
"Yeah. I have nothing else to do."
Mira glared harder at him.
"Are you trying to seduce me?"
The word "seduce" came out dripping with mocking skepticism.
Dexter smirked.
"You’ve been the one seducing me since the beginning."
Mira’s eyes widened by a fraction.
"Is it working?" Dexter continued.
Mira rolled her eyes eloquently.
"Is that how you seduce?" she said with contempt.
Dexter shrugged again.
"Show me how to seduce a woman. Tell me how I can seduce you."
Mira glanced at his face then his feet and then back to his face.
"You don’t have the talent,"
Dexter was stunned but then he chuckled with confidence.
"Are you trying to challenge me?"
Mira scoffed.
"Challenge?" she repeated. "Even if I give you one hundred years, there is no way you will be able to seduce a woman, not to talk of me."
Dexter glared at her.
"What do you mean by that?"
Mira sneered.
"I meant exactly what I said and you know exactly what I mean."
Dexter stood up.
He pointed at her. "You!"
"Okay," he said. "Challenge accepted."
Mira was confused as she blinked her eyes.
"What challenge?"
Dexter smiled.
"You just said I can’t seduce you, even if I have one hundred years. I said challenge accepted. Give me a month. I will seduce you in a month."
