chapters.title: Chapter 233 | Challenge Accepted
paragraphs: Mira frowned in confusion as she blinked and looked at him.
"What challenge?"
Dexter flexed the muscles in his neck and replied with a smile.
"You just said I can’t seduce you, even if I have one hundred years. I said challenge accepted. But will do it in ten span of a month."
Mira laughed as thought it was the most funny thing she had ever heard.
Her smile was so dazzling that even after seeing all of Mira, he was still incredibly stunned by that astonishing smile.
Her laughter manage to subside as she spoke.
"You seduce me in a month? Impossible."
Dexter who had been initially stunned came to at her words. His eyes narrowed as he glared at her.
"Are you trying to call me ugly?"
Mira shook her head slightly, a small smile on her face as she replied.
"That’s not it."
She paused as she pondered whether she should say what was in her mind but decided to anyways.
"At first I never truly looked at you and thought you were quite alright," she said. "But now, I realize you are actually handsome. Maybe even more than you previously were.
Dexter’s eyebrows rose and he smirked as a bit of arrogance within his mind.
"But even with that," Mira continued, recovering her composure and reassembling her sneer, "there is no way you can successfully seduce me in a month."
She crossed her Spectral Arms. The mana limbs folded across her chest as she challenged him.
Dexter raised eyebrow dropped and his eyes narrowed.
’Shes quite confident, isn’t she?’
He glanced at her for a while, thought for a bit and then spoke.
"Hm... to you, what counts as successful seduction?"
He paused as a mischievous glint appeared in his eyes.
"Kissing or sex?"
Mira’s crimson eyes blazed and she immediately hissed at him. "Who the hell is going to have sex with you!?"
Dexter chuckled as he quickly held up both hands.
"Hey, it’s an appropriate question. I’m just asking, what counts as seduction? Kissing, making out or sex?"
Mira glared at him as her eyes literally almost burned with flames and she said through gritted teeth.
"Kissing," she said.
Dexter nodded. "Okay. So I have thirty days to kiss you. That’s the challenge."
Mira immediately nodded. The nod was accompanied by an arrogant smirk.
Dexter chuckled. "Okay. What are the stakes?"
Mira blinked and was slightly caught off guard by the challenge.
She frowned.
"I have nothing to offer you," She said quietly.
Dexter looked at her then nodded his head.
"Okay," he said. "How about we double the promise you owe me?"
Mira’s eyes widened.
"Instead of you doing one single thing for me," Dexter continued, "let’s make it two. Two favors instead of one. If I win."
Mira stared at him as she thought more deeply about it.

Dexter could not seduce her in thirty days. The man could barely touch her without his heart going haywire. Although he touched her regularly, she could tell he was always on the brink of breaking and also shy.
This man was not going to seduce anyone in thirty days.
"Okay, fine," Mira said confidently. "What about me? What would you give me if you fail?"
Dexter blinked as his eyes shifted and he smirked.
"Anything you want."
Mira raised an eyebrow. "Anything?"
"Anything. And also, along with a surprise, I will do everything in my power to make you walk," he said.
The words landed in the living room like a thunderclap.
Mira eyes went wide as she stared at Dexter.
The ability to stand without help.
Dexter was offering that.
If he failed, he would dedicate everything he had to making her walk.
She stared at him. For a long, silent moment. Her crimson eyes moved across his face. Reading. Searching. Looking for the angle.
She didn’t find one.
Or was he planning to win?
She couldn’t tell.
And that, she realized with a discomfort that settled into her chest like a warm stone, was what made it dangerous.

Because if Dexter actually tried, if he actually applied himself to the challenge with the same focused, relentless, patient determination that he applied to everything else, if he brought that level of commitment to the task of seducing her...
She might lose.
Mira looked at Dexter.
Dexter looked at Mira.
The living room was quiet.
"Deal," Mira said.
Dexter smiled.
The kind that started at his mouth and reached his eyes and stayed there.
"Deal," he said.
He stood up. Extended his hand.
Mira looked at the hand. Then at his face. Then at the hand again.
Her right arm, the functioning one, the one that had moved for the first time three days ago, the one that had grabbed his wrist in a moment of unconscious need, reached out.
Her fingers found his.
The handshake was brief. Firm. The clasp of two people sealing an agreement that would, in thirty days, change everything between them.
Dexter’s hand was warm. Mira’s was cool.
They held for one second. Two.
Then released.
Dexter turned and walked toward the kitchen.
"Thirty days, Mira," he said over his shoulder. "Starting now."
Mira sat in her wheelchair. Her crimson eyes watched him go. Her right hand, the one that had just held his, rested in her lap. The fingers were still curled slightly. Holding the ghost of his grip.
She closed her eyes.
Her heart was beating faster than it should have been.
Faster than it had been in years.
’Thirty days.’
’Impossible.’
’Absolutely impossible.’
’So why is my heart doing that?’
"BAM BAM BAM!"
The knock was heavy.
Not the light, rhythmic tap of Tessa’s morning visits.
Bam. Bam. Bam.
Dexter blinked.
He wasn’t expecting anyone. Tessa had already come and gone this morning. Rachel had called. The bakery delivery was done. The squad meeting was yesterday. The festival was tomorrow.
There was no one on his schedule.

His Enhanced Hearing activated automatically, expanding outward through the walls and gate to scan the space beyond. He filtered the ambient noise. Traffic. Wind. The distant bark of a dog three houses down.
Then he found the heartbeats.
Not one.
Five.
All carrying the steady, controlled rhythm of people who were calm and purposeful and had arrived with intention.
Dexter frowned.
’Police? Hero Association?’

The thought sent a cold spike through his chest. Harvest Homes. The fight. The destroyed office. The four-meter transformation. The old man sent flying through a wall. The building damaged. The cameras. The witnesses.
’If they’ve traced it back to me...’
His mind spiraled.

chapters.title: Chapter 234 | The Intruders
paragraphs: ’Run. Take the girls. Take the SUV and disappear.’
The thought was extreme but the thought was also rational and also irrational.
’Stop. Think. Face it head-on.’
Dexter took a breath and exhaled.
He looked at Mira. She was in her wheelchair by the window, eyes closed, cultivating.
"I’m coming," he muttered.
He walked to the front door, opened the door and stepped onto the porch. Then walked to the gate.
He saw them.
And he stopped.
Five people stood outside his gate.
They wore dark tailored and expensive suit.
Four men stood side by side, two on each side. They were all tall broad-shouldered and carried themselves with the rigid practised posture of professional security personnel.
And in the center, flanked by the four suited men, stood a single figure.
An old man.

Perhaps sixty or older, his age was difficult to discern. His silver hair, neatly combed, framed his white temples. His face was lined but not wrinkled, bearing the deep permanent creases of a man who had maintained a specific expression for decades. This expression had ultimately frozen into his face by default.
He wore a dark grey suit. Slightly lighter than the others. A white handkerchief in the breast pocket. A monocle in his left eye.
Behind them, parked at the curb, was a limousine.
Dexter recognized the old man immediately.
The butler.

Not just any butler. The Ashford family butler. The man who had stood at the gate of the Ashford estate on the day Dexter was disowned and had delivered, with the flat, emotionless face the terms of his exile.
Ten thousand credits. The key to the bungalow and the deed to the house.
"The family has nothing more to do with you."
Those had been his words the day Dexter’s life had ended and begun simultaneously.
And now the man was standing at his gate.
Dexter’s face hardened.
The warmth from the conversation with Mira, all of it evaporated and turned cold chilling.
He walked to the gate. Stopped behind it. Looked through the iron bars at the five suited figures.
"What the fuck do you want?"
The words were incredibly cold and chilling and even the surprising atmosphere seem to freeze at his cold words.
The butler, however, didn’t react.

Not a twitch. Not a blink. Not a single facial muscle moving in response to the profanity. The man’s expression remained exactly as it had been. Neutral. Composed. The professional blankness of someone who had been verbally abused by better than Dexter and had long since stopped registering it.

"That is no way for a gentleman to speak," the butler said. His voice was measured. Precise. Each syllable articulated with the careful, deliberate enunciation of a man who had been trained in diction and had never relaxed his standards.
"Good day to you, Dexter. I hope I met you in good health."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"And I hope you die in the next five minutes. What the hell do you want?"

The butler’s expression didn’t change. The monocle caught the morning light and threw a small, sharp reflection across the gate. His gloved hands, white and pristine, remained clasped in front of his body.
He reached into his jacket.

One of the suited men on his left moved. A subtle, barely perceptible shift in posture that brought his hand closer to his jacket’s interior. A defensive reflex. The movement of a bodyguard responding to a potential threat.
The butler raised one hand. A small, calming gesture. The bodyguard relaxed.

The butler produced nothing from his own jacket. Instead, he turned slightly toward the bodyguard on his right. This man held a silver tray. Polished. Reflective. The kind of tray that was used in formal settings to present items that were too important to be handed directly and too small to be carried openly.
On the tray sat a letter.

It was white. Cream-colored, to be precise. Heavy stock. The kind of paper that was used for official correspondence between families of significance. The Ashford family seal was embossed on the front in gold wax. A phoenix, wings spread, rising from flames. The symbol of the family that had risen to the top of Stargate City through wealth, power, and the systematic exploitation of everyone beneath them.

The butler took the letter from the tray. His white-gloved fingers held it by the edges, presenting it to Dexter through the gate bars with the formal, precise gesture of a man who had been presenting documents to people for decades and could perform the action in his sleep.
Dexter stared at the letter.
Then at the butler.
Then at the letter again.
He didn’t take it.
"What is it?" he asked.
"An invitation," the butler said.
"From whom?"
"From the Ashford family."
Dexter’s jaw tightened. The coldness in his chest spread. Through his shoulders. Down his arms. Into his fingertips, which were currently gripping the gate bars with enough force to dent the iron.
"I have nothing to do with the Ashford family," Dexter said. "Your boss made that clear days ago doesn’t that ring any bells?"
The butler’s expression remained unchanged.

"Circumstances have changed," he said. "The family has reconsidered certain positions. The letter contains the details of an invitation that the family believes you may find... advantageous to accept."
"Advantageous," Dexter repeated. The word tasted like ash.
He looked at the letter. At the gold seal. At the phoenix rising from flames.
’The Ashford family is inviting me after disowning me, scamming three families into marrying their daughters to a bastard.’
’And they sent the butler. The same butler who handed me ten thousand dollars and told me I was worthless.’
’Why?’
The question was the only thing that prevented Dexter from telling the butler to leave and slamming the gate. Not curiosity nor politeness.

The Ashford family did nothing without reason. Every action, every statement, every gesture was calculated. Designed. Optimized for maximum effect with minimum cost. They were chess players. Grandmasters. And they had just moved a piece onto his board.
Refusing to look at the move would be a mistake.

chapters.title: Chapter 235 | Fuck. Off
paragraphs: The butler continued to hold the letter like Dexter’s opinion didn’t matter.
"If you will accept the invitation and read it, you will know every detail regarding the event. Take it."
Dexter looked at the letter then he glared at the butler.
"Like I said, I have nothing to do with the Ashford family," he said coldly.
"I and the Ashford family are done. You said so yourself."
He held the butler’s gaze.
"It’s useless. I have nothing else to do with the family. Now, if there is nothing more, take your leave."
The butler’s face changed slightly as he stared at Dexter coldly.

"You should do well to know your place. If it wasn’t absolutely important for you to attend, do you think the family would extend an invitation to a bastard they alredy cast aside? This is your opportunity and you should be groveling on the ground for this opportunity graced to you by the Ashford family."
Killing intent exploded from Dexter’s gaze and the smell of blood spread through the entire neighborhood as his Asura body activated.
Dexter’s lips slowly curled upwards as he stared at the old man before him. "Fuck, Off."
The butler’s blood ran cold as the killing intent spread through his entire body like ice pricking his entire body.
Before he could say anything, the gate instablt slammed shut!
"Bang!!!"
It closed directly in the butler’s face!
The butler stood on the other side of the gate as his heart pounded slightly with fear.
He looked at the closed gate, gritted his teeth as he halted at the gate.
Inside his compound, Dexter inhaled deeply and then breathed out as he calmed his killing intent. It eas becoming even more explosive than before.
After a while, he then walked to the house and closed the door.
When he came to the door, he saw Mira turned to look at him, then she suddenly spoke.
"The Ashford family butler," With her strength, she obviously can hear from far distances.
Dexter looked at her then nodded slowly. "Yeah."
Mira’s brows furrowed slightly in worry.
"What do they want?
Dexter shrugged as he flexed his fingers.
"They came to drop an invitation letter. I have no idea what it’s about, and I don’t wish to know. I have nothing to do with the Ashford family. So I really don’t care."
Mira blinked as she stared ad his face closely.
Then she asked something unexpected.
"Are you okay?"
The same three words that Selene had asked the night before, when she had sensed his killing intent. But the tone was different. Selene’s version had been cautious.
Mira’s version was something else. Without pretence or sarcasm.
Dexter was taken aback.
Dexter looked at her as saw hee gaze was soft, then he smiled.
"Yeah," he said. "I’m okay."
Mira stared at his face for a long, silent moment and when she found what she was looking for, She nodded.
Then she closed her eyes as mana swirled around her body as she resumed her cultivation.
Dexter watched her for a moment and something warm settled in his chest.
He then turned toward the hallway.
Had had only taken one step, when,
"Bam. Bam. Bam!!!"
The knock hit the gate like a hammer and was even heavier than before.
Dexter stopped. His face changed and his gaze hardened.
’If they don’t leave me alone, I will teach them a lesson.’
He stormed to the front door. Yanked it open. Walked to the gate.
He grabbed the gate handle. Pulled it open.
"Did I not tell you to leave?" he growled.

The words were loud. Hard. Directed outward through the opening gate with the full force of a man who had reached the limit of his tolerance and was prepared to enforce it with whatever means were necessary.
But the words died in his throat.
Because the butler was not there.

The limousine was gone. The five suited figures were gone. The silver tray, the white gloves, the monocle, the cream-colored letter with the gold phoenix seal. All gone. The street was empty of everything except the fading smell of expensive perfume and the residual impression of a vehicle that had been parked at the curb.
The butler had left.
What stood at Dexter’s gate instead was something else entirely.
Something he had forgotten about.
Something he had, if he was being honest, completely forgotten existed.
Kreg.
The name registered before the face did.
Kreg.
The thug. The gang leader. The man who had walked into his house three weeks ago with four cronies and had demanded protection money.
"We’ll be back next month."
That had been the promise. Next month. The monthly protection fee. The Red Fang Crew’s business model. Pay us, or we find other ways to collect.
Dexter had forgotten.
He had been so consumed by the system, that he had completely and utterly forgotten about the street thug who had robbed him in his own living room.
Kreg stood at the gate.

He was tall. Muscular. Built like a door, which was the description Dexter had applied to him the first time they had met. His white beard was the same. His leather jacket was the same. His gold tooth caught the morning light and threw a small, sharp glint across the gate bars.
He was not alone.

Behind him, arranged in the loose, informal formation of men who followed a leader because the leader was bigger than them, stood four figures. Dexter recognized them. The same four from weeks ago. The same four who had fanned out across his living room, hands in pockets, grinning with the confidence of men who believed they owned whatever street they were standing on.
Kreg looked down at Dexter and smiled arrogantly.
"Oh," Kreg said, his voice deep and rough, carrying the particular, amused cadence of a man who had just been shouted at and had found it funny. "You actually dared to shout at me?"
Dexter stared at him. Kreg still had the gold tooth, the leather jacket and there were four minions behind him.

sentences.text: The butler continued to hold the letter like Dexter’s opinion didn’t matter.
"If you will accept the invitation and read it, you will know every detail regarding the event.
Take it."
Dexter looked at the letter then he glared at the butler.
"Like I said, I have nothing to do with the Ashford family," he said coldly.
"I and the Ashford family are done.
You said so yourself."
He held the butler’s gaze.
"It’s useless.
I have nothing else to do with the family.
Now, if there is nothing more, take your leave."
The butler’s face changed slightly as he stared at Dexter coldly.
"You should do well to know your place.
If it wasn’t absolutely important for you to attend, do you think the family would extend an invitation to a bastard they alredy cast aside?
This is your opportunity and you should be groveling on the ground for this opportunity graced to you by the Ashford family."
Killing intent exploded from Dexter’s gaze and the smell of blood spread through the entire neighborhood as his Asura body activated.
Dexter’s lips slowly curled upwards as he stared at the old man before him.
"Fuck, Off."
The butler’s blood ran cold as the killing intent spread through his entire body like ice pricking his entire body.
Before he could say anything, the gate instablt slammed shut!
"Bang!!!"
It closed directly in the butler’s face!
The butler stood on the other side of the gate as his heart pounded slightly with fear.
He looked at the closed gate, gritted his teeth as he halted at the gate.
Inside his compound, Dexter inhaled deeply and then breathed out as he calmed his killing intent.
It eas becoming even more explosive than before.
After a while, he then walked to the house and closed the door.
When he came to the door, he saw Mira turned to look at him, then she suddenly spoke.
"The Ashford family butler," With her strength, she obviously can hear from far distances.
Dexter looked at her then nodded slowly.
"Yeah."
Mira’s brows furrowed slightly in worry.
"What do they want?
Dexter shrugged as he flexed his fingers.
"They came to drop an invitation letter.
I have no idea what it’s about, and I don’t wish to know.
I have nothing to do with the Ashford family.
So I really don’t care."
Mira blinked as she stared ad his face closely.
Then she asked something unexpected.
"Are you okay?"
The same three words that Selene had asked the night before, when she had sensed his killing intent.
But the tone was different.
Selene’s version had been cautious.
Mira’s version was something else.
Without pretence or sarcasm.
Dexter was taken aback.
Dexter looked at her as saw hee gaze was soft, then he smiled.
"Yeah," he said.
"I’m okay."
Mira stared at his face for a long, silent moment and when she found what she was looking for, She nodded.
Then she closed her eyes as mana swirled around her body as she resumed her cultivation.
Dexter watched her for a moment and something warm settled in his chest.
He then turned toward the hallway.
Had had only taken one step, when,
"Bam.
Bam.
Bam!!!"
The knock hit the gate like a hammer and was even heavier than before.
Dexter stopped.
His face changed and his gaze hardened.
’If they don’t leave me alone, I will teach them a lesson.’
He stormed to the front door.
Yanked it open.
Walked to the gate.
He grabbed the gate handle.
Pulled it open.
"Did I not tell you to leave?" he growled.
The words were loud.
Hard.
Directed outward through the opening gate with the full force of a man who had reached the limit of his tolerance and was prepared to enforce it with whatever means were necessary.
But the words died in his throat.
Because the butler was not there.
The limousine was gone.
The five suited figures were gone.
The silver tray, the white gloves, the monocle, the cream-colored letter with the gold phoenix seal.
All gone.
The street was empty of everything except the fading smell of expensive perfume and the residual impression of a vehicle that had been parked at the curb.
The butler had left.
What stood at Dexter’s gate instead was something else entirely.
Something he had forgotten about.
Something he had, if he was being honest, completely forgotten existed.
Kreg.
The name registered before the face did.
Kreg.
The thug.
The gang leader.
The man who had walked into his house three weeks ago with four cronies and had demanded protection money.
"We’ll be back next month."
That had been the promise.
Next month.
The monthly protection fee.
The Red Fang Crew’s business model.
Pay us, or we find other ways to collect.
Dexter had forgotten.
He had been so consumed by the system, that he had completely and utterly forgotten about the street thug who had robbed him in his own living room.
Kreg stood at the gate.
He was tall.
Muscular.
Built like a door, which was the description Dexter had applied to him the first time they had met.
His white beard was the same.
His leather jacket was the same.
His gold tooth caught the morning light and threw a small, sharp glint across the gate bars.
He was not alone.
Behind him, arranged in the loose, informal formation of men who followed a leader because the leader was bigger than them, stood four figures.
Dexter recognized them.
The same four from weeks ago.
The same four who had fanned out across his living room, hands in pockets, grinning with the confidence of men who believed they owned whatever street they were standing on.
Kreg looked down at Dexter and smiled arrogantly.
"Oh," Kreg said, his voice deep and rough, carrying the particular, amused cadence of a man who had just been shouted at and had found it funny.
"You actually dared to shout at me?"
Dexter stared at him.
Kreg still had the gold tooth, the leather jacket and there were four minions behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 236 | The Thug, Kreg!
paragraphs: Dexter blinked.
He hadn’t expected this.
He had almost forgotten about Kreg and the money and what he had said about his wives.
But here he was, standing at the gate with his four minions behind him and with the same arrogance too!
And Dexter was surprised.
Dexter was surprised by his own reaction.
Dexter had been planning to go find Kreg eventually when he had time.
But Kreg had come to him.
’Is this what they call a blessing in disguise?’
"Kreg," he said.
Kreg smiled confidently as the gold tooth glinted in his mouth.
"Oh, now you remember me," Kreg said. "Nice. I assume you haven’t forgotten about my protection fee."
Dexter blinked and was about to say signing when Kreg moved.
He didn’t wait for Dexter to speak as he pushed past Dexter. Kreg’s shoulder caught Dexter’s chest, shoving him sideways, intending to Knick him down but Dexter didn’t move a single inch.
Kreg was a bit stunned but he didn’t put that to his mind as he entered the compound.
His eyes moved across the property as he scanned the place.
The four lackeys followed him as they also pushed past Dexter with the same casual, dismissive physical contact.
They all swaggered into the compound like they owned it.
Dexter registered their cultivation levels as they passed.
Kreg. Eighth Stage Awakened.
The others. Seventh. Sixth. Sixth.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Three weeks ago, Kreg had been at Third Stage Awakened. The others at First and Second. Now they were Awakned. All of them. Advanced by multiple levels in less than a month.
That kind of advancement was not natural.That kind of jump required either an extraordinary external resource or an extraordinary external intervention.
’Someone is boosting them.’
That was the only reason.
But Dexter didn’t say anything as he didn’t care about this.
As Kreg entered, he didn’t pause as he spoke.
"Oh," Kreg said. "I see you’ve renovated. This is nice."

The words were casual. Appreciative in the particular, proprietary way that a landlord appreciates improvements to a property he intends to seize. The tone of a man who looked at someone else’s work and saw his own future.
He didn’t wait for a response. He opened the front door. Stepped inside.
Dexter’s front door. Dexter’s house. Opened and entered by a man who had not been invited and had not asked.
The four lackeys followed. They entered the living room with the same swaggering, take-ownership gait that their leader had used. Looking around. Evaluating. Claiming.
Dexter stood at the gate.
He watched them go.

His face was expressionless. Completely, absolutely, perfectly blank. The mask he had spent nineteen years perfecting in the Ashford estate. The mask that revealed nothing. Not anger. Not fear. Not the particular, cold, focused calculation that was running behind his eyes like a computer processing a targeting solution.
But a smile tugged at the corner of his lips.
Not a warm smile. Not a friendly smile. The particular, barely perceptible, almost invisible upward curve of a mouth that was anticipating something.
He walked through the gate. Closed it behind him. The latch clicked.
He walked up the path. Into his house. Through the front door.
Kreg was in the living room. Standing. Looking around. His eyes moving across the space with the slow, evaluating scan of a man who was mentally cataloguing everything he could take.
Then his eyes found Mira.

She was in her wheelchair by the window. Crimson hair. Pale skin. Closed eyes. Cultivating. Her Spectral Arms were folded behind her back, motionless. She was wearing the white cropped top and black skirt that Dexter had dressed her in that morning. She looked, despite the wheelchair and the paralysis and the three years of suffering, like what she was. A noblewoman. A warrior. A woman whose beauty had not been diminished by her condition but had been refined by it, sharpened to a point that was almost painful to look at.
Kreg’s smile widened.
The widening was specific. Targeted. The particular, predatory expansion of lips over teeth that occurred when a man saw something he wanted and had no intention of asking permission.
"Oh," Kreg said. His voice had dropped. Softened. The particular, intimate tone that bullies used when they were transitioning from general intimidation to specific acquisition.
The lackey who had whistled at Dexter’s wives three weeks ago, the same one, the one with the sharp eyes and the loose mouth, spoke.
"Ooh, boss. The girls are even prettier than before."

He walked toward the living room. His eyes were on Mira. Then on Lyra, who was on the couch with the Primordial Beast Egg, her AI glasses on, her dark eyes open, watching the men enter with an expression that was, through the barrier of her deafness, taking longer to process than it would for someone who could hear their words.
"Boss, the girls are even prettier than before," the lackey repeated. "If we wait any longer, other gangs might beat us to the chase."
He whistled. The sound was sharp. Loud. The particular, aggressive, proprietary whistle of a man who was making a claim and wanted everyone in the room to know it.
He walked toward the living room. Toward Mira. Toward Lyra. His eyes moving between them with the casual, evaluating hunger of someone browsing a display case.
Dexter watched.
He stood near the front door as a small smile tugged at his face.
He had closed the front door and locked it. Be had also don’t the same for the gate too.

He snapped his fingers and above the house, in the sky that had been blue and clear and ordinary, the air rippled. As the Type-5 House Protection Talisman, buried beneath the living room rug, responded to Dexter’s command.
The formation’s primary function was defense but it had several secondary function.
One of which was a ilencing.
Every sound within the dome, every voice, every scream, every impact, every crash, every cry, was contained, sealed within the boundary of the formation and prevented from traveling beyond it.
What happened inside would not be heard outside.

chapters.title: Chapter 237 | Kreg...
paragraphs: A young dark-haired woman stood in front of the Hero Association building, staring up at its magnificent structure. Though it wasn’t as large as the Hero Association headquarters, it was still impressive. Heroes came and went through the gate as she watched.
"Hey," the woman said. "I assume you’re Jasmine."
Jasmine nodded slowly. "And you’re...?"
The woman smiled. The smile was warm. Genuine. The kind that arrived without calculation and stayed without effort.
"Call me Rachel. I was assigned to show you around. Show you your office. Walk you through the branch’s operations."
She extended her hand.
"Welcome ."
Jasmine took the hand and shook her.
"Please come with me," Rachel said.
Jasmine nodded. She followed Rachel through the front entrance.
Dexter stood with his hands behind his back, looking at the five thugs in his home. His lips curled into an evil smirk as various thoughts flashed through his head.
At that moment, Kreg and the other four lackeys were still looking around the house. One had even gone to the living room, heading directly toward Mira.

However, Kreg seemed to notice something. Although arrogant, his survival instinct was extremely sharp. He knew whom to offend and whom not to offend. That was why, despite the number of strong people in the neighborhood, nobody had taught him a lesson. He had not offended the wrong people.
But now, he suddenly felt that something was wrong. He didn’t know exactly what, but he felt it.

One of his lackeys spoke. "Boss, what do you say? We can actually take one of the girls and sell her to one of the top three families. No matter how powerful the Vance, Frost, and Callaway families are, they can never compare to the top one, top two, or top three families. If we sell one of these premium girls to that royal blood, we’ll earn enough money to live out our lives. Enough money that our generations would inherit. We could even flee the country and enjoy the rest of our lives. What do you say, boss?"
Kreg did not answer. His brows furrowed as the wrongness persisted. He looked around the house, then turned toward Lyra.

Lyra sat on the couch in the living room, cross-legged, eyes closed in concentration. Mira’s eyes were also closed. Kreg looked at both women. It wasn’t their beauty that attracted him now. It was the fact that he couldn’t sense their strength at all.
But the danger he felt wasn’t coming from them. It came from another source. He looked around and frowned but could not see who or what it was.
"Boss, are you all right?" one lackey asked.
Kreg shook his head. "Must be my imagination." He waved the lackey off. "I’m all right." He turned back to Dexter and smiled.

"As you know, there was a monster outbreak a few weeks ago. If it wasn’t for us—the Red Fang gang—this entire street would have been wiped out. So our protection fee has increased by more than ten times. Previously, you gave me five thousand dollars, which was barely enough to do anything. But since you were the son of the Ashford family, we gave you face and didn’t say anything. This time, our protection fee has increased a lot. It has been months since the Ashford family even cared about you. They have never come here, which means you have been truly abandoned. Your wife has also been abandoned. Therefore, there is nobody else to protect you. Their reputation cannot protect you this time. So our fee has increased to five hundred thousand dollars. What do you say?"
Dexter blinked. Then he smiled widening and chuckled slightly.
Kreg raised an eyebrow, surprised that Dexter dared to chuckle.

Suddenly, one of the lackeys heading toward Mira froze. His face flashed with confusion. He tried to move, but pressure held him as if ten mountains had landed on him. His body was a statue; he could not move a single muscle. His eyes widened in horror. He opened his mouth to scream, but no sound came out. He tried to explode with energy, but his energy was restricted by multiple chains. He could not move at all.
The other three lackeys noticed nothing. They were staring at Dexter along with Kreg.
At that moment, Dexter spoke. "Oh, you’re laughing.
One lackey said, "No, boss. I think he has finally gone mad, actually daring to laugh at us. Should I teach him a lesson? Let me teach him a lesson."
The lackey stepped forward. It was the one Dexter had kicked in the nuts the first time, and he was still angry. He was about to crack his knuckles when Kreg raised a hand. The lackey froze.
"Wait," Kreg said. "Let him speak."
Dexter looked at the lackey, then at Kreg. "Five thousand dollars. Five hundred thousand dollars. From five thousand to five hundred thousand. Isn’t that a bit much? That is slightly too much."
Kreg shrugged. "Of course it’s much. We, the Red Fang gang, risked our lives to repel the monsters that invaded this district. That’s why it costs. I hope you understand where we are coming from."
Dexter slowly nodded. "Yeah, I understand where you’re coming from. So which one of you should I give the money to?"

Kreg’s eyes widened slightly. He had expected Dexter to negotiate, or to say he didn’t have that kind of money. But Dexter actually agreed. His brows furrowed, but then he spoke. "If you are trying to deceive us, I hope you know the consequences."
Dexter nodded. "Of course. I would never dare deceive anybody from the Red Fang gang."

Kreg laughed arrogantly, and his lackeys laughed with him. Dexter brought out his phone, opened his bank app, and told Kreg to give him his bank information. Kreg did. Dexter nodded and transferred the money. He showed his phone to Kreg.
Kreg chuckled. "Satisfied. Of course, of course. Haha. I never thought you had that kind of money at hand. Wonderful, wonderful."
The lackeys erupted in laughter and joy.

chapters.title: Chapter 238 | You’re Going To Die
paragraphs: Kreg chuckled. "Satisfied. Of course, of course. Haha. I never thought you had that kind of money at hand. Wonderful, wonderful."
The lackeys erupted in laughter.
Suddenly, Kreg ’s laugh paused as he noticed something wrong. He turned to the side and realized his lackey on Mira’s side was still there. "Victor? What are you still doing there? Victor!"
Victor didn’t answer. "Victor!"

Still no answer. One of the lackeys frowned and went toward Victor. When he reached him, he froze. Victor was literally crying—crying blood. His eyes were bloodshot, his body frozen, his mouth open in a soundless scream.
The lackey was stunned. Before he could turn to say something to Kreg, his body also froze as if it were a statue.
The other two lackeys and Kreg noticed something was wrong. They turned toward Mira’s side.
Dexter cracked his neck. "So we begin."
"I have waited so long for this moment. I didn’t expect you to deliver yourself to me."
Kreg frowned, noticing Dexter’s voice had changed. "What do you mean by that?"

Dexter tilted his head slowly. "Even if you kneel, beg, or scream, it’s useless. You wanted to cripple me, right? You humiliated me in front of my wife. Threatened my wife. And you dared to extort me twice. I just hope I get a return for the 5000 dollars I gave you."
Kreg frowned and his face hardened then exploded with his seventh-level awakened strength. "What the fuck are you talking about? Do you want to die?"
Dexter chuckled. "Die? The one to die would be you."
Kreg’s voice had barely fallen when Dexter disappeared.
"Bang!"

A fist slammed into Kreg’s stomach. His eyes bulged as the air was violently knocked from his lungs. His entire body folded inward, doubling over around the impact, before he was sent flying across the room like a ragdoll.
"BOOM!"
He crashed into the wall, leaving a spiderweb of cracks behind. Dust and plaster rained down around him as his body crumpled to the floor in a broken heap.
He gasped, wheezed, tried to breathe—but his lungs refused to cooperate. The air tasted like copper and chalk. His ribs screamed with every shallow, ragged gasp.
Before Kreg could recover, Dexter was already standing in front of him.
Kreg’s pupils contracted.
He hadn’t even seen Dexter move. One moment, Dexter was across the room. The next, he was there.
Dexter grinned as he grabbed him by the hair and slammed his head into the floor.
"BANG!"
The impact shook the room. The floorboards cracked beneath Kreg’s skull. Blood sprayed across the wood in a dark, wet arc. The coppery scent of it filled the air, thick and cloying.
"You’re an 7th-level awakened now," Dexter said calmly. "You probably thought that made you powerful."

Kreg coughed, blood dripping from the corner of his mouth. His vision swam. His thoughts scattered like startled birds. He tried to speak, tried to form words, but all that came out was a wet, pathetic gurgle. The sound of a man whose body was failing him faster than his mind could track.
Dexter lifted him again by the hair, forcing Kreg to look up at him. Forcing him to meet his eyes.
"Look at me. You really think you are strong but there’s always a mountain above a mountain..."
"BANG!"
He slammed him down again. The sound was sickening. Bone meeting wood. Flesh meeting force. The particular, wet, cracking resonance of a skull being introduced to a surface that would not yield.
"You’re nothing."
Kreg gritted his teeth.
"You cripple!"
He activated his talent as his arms covered in bone spikes as he punched hard at Dexter.
Dexter caught his fist effortlessly, mid-swing, as though he were catching a thrown ball as the spike cracked and shattered against his palm.
Dexter’s body was insane. Not to mention Awakened level 7, Superhuman level 7 could barely penetrate his skin.
Dexter held his fist and squeezing gently, letting Kreg feel the absolute futility of resistance.
Letting him feel the particular, crushing, inexorable pressure of a grip that could not be broken.
A sharp crack echoed through the room as Dexter twisted his arm.
Kreg screamed.
"AAAGH!"
The remaining lackeys finally understood. They had kicked a diamon stone.
"Run!"
One of them shouted and desperately tried to escape. He bolted toward the door, He reached the door—
Only for an invisible force to slam him backward.
BOOM!

He crashed into the floor. The impact drove the air from his lungs and left him gasping like a fish on dry land. Dexter didn’t even look at him. The formation had sealed the compound. Nobody was leaving. Not until Dexter decided they could. Not until he was finished.
"I’ll save you for last," Dexter faced Kreg as he spoke. "It’s always the sweetest."
He smiled as he turned away from Kreg.

He hadn’t used any pressure from his superhuman strength, yet Kreg was frozen in fear. The man who had walked into his home with confidence, with arrogance, with four men and a plan—that man was gone. What remained was a trembling shell.

Dexter licked his lips and turned toward another lackey—the man who had previously touched his wife the first time they came. The one who had put his hands on Mira’s shoulder while she sat helpless in her wheelchair. The one who had smiled while doing it.
"Bang!"
His chest caved in as blood spilled from his lips and he was sent flying. He hit the ground hard, rolled, and came to a stop against the base of the couch.
He tried to breathe. Blood bubbled between his lips with each shallow, labored gasp. The sound was wet and rhythmic, like a leaking valve.
Dexter slowly approached him. The man’s face turned extremely pale. The color of a corpse that hadn’t realized it was dead yet.
"Please..."
Dexter stopped in front of him. "You remember me?"
The man trembled. "I... I was wrong."
Dexter crouched down. "You were wrong?"

chapters.title: Chapter 239 | Killing The Thugs
paragraphs: "Please..."
Dexter stopped in front of him. "You remember me?"
The man trembled. "I... I was wrong."
Dexter crouched down. "Oh... you were wrong?"
His voice was frighteningly calm.
"You came into my home."
He grabbed the man’s collar, twisting the fabric in his fist.
"You robbed me."
He lifted him off the ground with one hand, holding him suspended like a puppet whose strings had been cut.
"You threatened my wife."
His eyes became cold, colder than the void between stars and merciless like a demon.
"Beat me up and you thought you could do it again?"
The man’s entire body trembled in fear and suddenly, his grey pants turned dark as his bladder let go, soaking his pants, and dripping on the floor.
He wanted to beg, find mercy from Dexter but found nothing.
Dexter looked down at the ground as the water stained his floor.
"Disgusting."
Dexter immediately threw him aside.
"BOOM!"
The man crashed through the coffee table, shattering it into splinters as he lay there, broken and bleeding, whimpering like a wounded animal.

Two were frozen by Mira’s pressure. Their bodies locked in place, eyes bleeding, mouths open in silent screams that would never be heard. The worst part is they were aware if everything but but utterly incapable of doing anything about it.
And only one was left.
Dexter looked at him with a dark smile as he took a step forward. Before his feet could touch the ground, he flashed and appeared before him.
"Crack!" "Crack!" "Crack!
The thug’s neck rotatated twisted three times around his head as the flesh of his neck bulged and looked obscene as he stood there for three seconds.
His face was pale with fear and even as he was dying, fear and horror could be seen in his face as he fell to the ground.
He didn’t die immediately but he lost all motor fiction as he lie there.
Dexter walked over to the one with the cracked chest.
The one who had suggested selling his wives.
"You’re the one who wanted to sell my wives aren’t you?"
Dexter smiled as he bent down, picking up the man’s arm.
"Crack!"
"Ahhh!!!"
The man screamed in pain and agony as Dexter broke his arms inch by inch.
The screams became even more high-pitched and piercing as Dexter finished twisting the entire right arm. He turned to the left arm and did the same. Making sure every inch of the nine was broken.
The man fainted and Dexter immediately woke him up with a slap.
"Now now, don’t sleep on me, we are now done."
Dexter did the same to his legs.
Breaking them inch by inch. Placing his legs on the man’s balls.
"Pop!" "Pop!"
Two popping sounds echoed through the entire place. And the man screamed even more as Dexter tortured him.
Until Mira said, "Noisy."
With a whoosh, flames erupted from her arm and landed in the man as shs burnt him with her flames, which made him scream even more horrifyingly than before.
The burning was slow, too. Deliberate. It consumed his clothing first. Then his skin. Then the tissue beneath. Layer by layer.
Dexter blinked. It seemed her flames could actually affect the soul. He watched the particular, faint, barely visible distortion that appeared around the man’s body as the flame consumed him.

When he was done burning, silence descended over the room. The particular, absolute, ringing quiet that followed the removal of all sound sources. What remained on the floor was not a body but an outline.
He then went to the two beside Mira and killed them too.
They collapsed without a sound.
Kreg was barely conscious. His arrogance was completely gone. His gold tooth was missing. His confidence was gone.
"What... are you?
Dexter walked toward him. "You don’t need to know."
Kreg tried to crawl backward. His hands scrabbled against the floor.
Dexter grabbed him by the throat and lifted him effortlessly. Kreg’s hands clawed at Dexter’s wrist. His legs kicked uselessly. His face changed color. From red to purple. From purple to blue.
"You should have stayed away from my family."
Kreg’s eyes widened. "Wait—"
Crack.
Dexter’s grip tightened. Kreg’s struggling stopped. His body went limp. The particular, quiet, definitive sound of a trachea being compressed past its structural limit.
Dexter released him, allowing the body to fall to the floor.
One by one, he finished off the remaining members of the Red Fang Gang. When the last of them stopped moving, Dexter stood silently in the middle of the room.
His expression was cold.

He looked around. At the bodies. At the ash outline. At the blood on the walls. At his living room—the space he had spent three weeks cleaning, repairing, painting, and protecting. At the Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact that still hummed on its shelf, doing its job regardless of what had happened in the room it was filtering.
He walked to the front door. Unlocked it. Opened it.
The morning air came in.
Dexter stood in the doorway, closed his eyes and breathed.
The five men who had entered his home were now dead. The Red Fang Crew was finished.
And Dexter Ashford was still standing.
After Dexter killed Kreg, he looked around.

Lyra was still on the chair, her eyes closed, still cultivating. It seemed she hadn’t noticed anything. Or perhaps she had noticed something and simply chosen to ignore it. Alternatively, she might have been cultivating so deeply that the violence in the living room had registered as nothing more than background noise.
Dexter watched her for a moment and the coldness in his gaze dissipated like smoke as he smiled at her.
’It’s time for clean up.’
Then he started to clean up.

He took the bodies of the remaining thugs—the ones Mira hadn’t incinerated, the ones who had died by his own hands—and stacked them in the backyard. Greg’s lifeless body went on top. Dexter carried them all as if they weighed nothing, his expression unchanged, his pace steady. The particular, casual ease of a man who had done this before and would likely do it again.

chapters.title: Chapter 240 | Where Do You Want Me?
paragraphs: ’It’s time for clean up.’
Then he started to clean up.

He took the bodies of the remaining thugs—the ones Mira hadn’t incinerated, the ones who had died by his own hands—and stacked them in the backyard. Kreg lifeless body went on top. Dexter carried them all as if they weighed nothing.
When he reached the backyard, Selene was cultivating on the swinging chair.
She turned to face him as he walked in.
She ’saw’ the corpses Dexter was dragging raised an eyebrow but didn’t say anything.
Dexter blinked, then offered a small, apologetic nod. "Sorry for the disturbance."
Selene shrugged. "It’s all right."
Dexter threw the corpses onto the center of the backyard. Then, activating his Heavenly Flame, a fireball materialized in front of him and landed in the corpses.
The corpses burned.

The smell that rose was not unpleasant. It was the particular, rich, smoky aroma of roasting meat—barbecue, almost, if one didn’t think too hard about the source. That was the main reason Dexter hadn’t burned them in the living room. The smell would have lingered and seeped into the furniture.
Here, in the open air, it would disperse.
And fortunately, the air purifier Mira had burned—the Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact—had already cleansed the interior. The smell wouldn’t reach the house.
When the flames died and nothing remained but ash, Dexter turned to go back inside.
Then Selene spoke.
She stopped herself.
Dexter, who was about to enter, paused. With his enhanced hearing, he had caught her speaking before she stopped herself.
He turned back toward her. "Do you need anything?"
Selene blinked. She remained silent for a while. The particular, internal, visibly conflicted silence of a woman who wanted to ask for something but didn’t want to impose.
Then she spoke.
"Was it your massage technique that healed Mira’s arm?"
Dexter blinked. Then he slowly nodded.

"Yes. It’s a massage technique—but not just the massage technique. The healing was due to many factors. The food I provide. The tea. The medicine. The massage. All of it, working together. But yes, the massage is one of the factors."
Selene nodded slowly. Then she opened her mouth to say something else.
Then closed it.

Dexter watched her. He knew how shy she was. Knew that she didn’t like to ask for things. Knew the particular, self-effacing, almost apologetic quality of a woman who had spent too long in the background and had never quite learned how to ask for what she wanted.
So he spoke first.
"If you want, I can try it on you."
Selene’s eyes widened slightly.
"Right now, since I’m not doing anything at the moment. It will only take ten to twenty minutes of your time."

Selene blinked. Her face flushed—the particular, pale, almost translucent blush of a woman whose complexion was so fair that any color at all stood out like a stain on white silk. It made her look, for a moment, almost human.
She slowly nodded. She didn’t look at him.
"Okay."
Dexter chuckled internally.
He turned and headed back into the house to prepare.
But first, Dexter needed to deal with the mess in the living room.

He started with the ashes—the particular, fine, grey-white residue of the body Mira had incinerated. The flames had burned so completely that nothing remained but a faint, almost invisible smudge on the carpet. He vacuumed it away, watching the particles disappear into the machine with the particular, clinical detachment of a man who had long since stopped being bothered by such things.
Then he addressed the wall.
The spiderweb of cracks where Kreg had slammed against it.
It took less than two minutes to clean the living room.
The wall would need to be repaired, of course. But he had materials left over from the window repair and he had purchased during the renovation. But he won’t fix it now.
Not when he had somewhere else to be.
His heartbeat had increased thinking about it but he tried to hide his excitement.
He was about to leave the living room when Mira spoke.
"Won’t you be in trouble?"
Dexter paused.
Mira’s voice was quiet.
"Since they’re dead," she continued, "there might be others who would look for them. It might cause trouble for you."
Dexter shrugged. "It doesn’t really matter."
Mira blinked at him.
"It can’t be big enough trouble," he said, "that we can’t handle when the time comes."
She looked at him for a moment. Then she nodded. "Okay.
Dexter smiled at her.
He was about to leave when he paused.
He looked down at Lyra.
She was still on the couch, cultivating.
Dexter smiled slightly.
He flipped his fingers. A pastry appeared on his left palm.He gently placed it on the couch beside Lyra.
when she woke, she would see it.
Dexter left.
He went to the room to prepare.

The bed was already made—the particular, clean, crisp, folded precision of sheets that had been smoothed to perfection. He placed the oils on the nightstand. The shockwave glove. The particular, soft, warm towels he had warmed in advance.
He arranged everything beside Selene bed, then waited.
Two minutes later, the door creaked.
The atmosphere in the room suddenly chilled.
Dexter raised his head.

The door creaked open, and a figure slowly entered. It was Selene. Her head was bowed. Her white hair—the particular, silver, almost luminous cascade of it—covered her entire face as she entered the room.
She moved with the particular, hesitant, almost reluctant grace of a woman who was not used to being seen. Not used to being the center of attention.
Dexter didn’t speak.
He simply waited.
Selin stepped fully into the room, and the door clicked shut behind her.
The silence stretched.
Then, slowly, she raised her head.
"Where do you want me?" she asked.
Her voice was quiet and shy as she spoke.
Dexter gestured to the bed. "Lie down. Face up. I’ll start with your shoulders."
Selene nodded as she slowly walked up to the bed.

He turned back toward her.
"Do you need anything?"
Selene blinked.
She remained silent for a while.
The particular, internal, visibly conflicted silence of a woman who wanted to ask for something but didn’t want to impose.
Then she spoke.
"Was it your massage technique that healed Mira’s arm?"
Dexter blinked.
Then he slowly nodded.
"Yes.
It’s a massage technique—but not just the massage technique.
The healing was due to many factors.
The food I provide.
The tea.
The medicine.
The massage.
All of it, working together.
But yes, the massage is one of the factors."
Selene nodded slowly.
Then she opened her mouth to say something else.
Then closed it.
Dexter watched her.
He knew how shy she was.
Knew that she didn’t like to ask for things.
Knew the particular, self-effacing, almost apologetic quality of a woman who had spent too long in the background and had never quite learned how to ask for what she wanted.
So he spoke first.
"If you want, I can try it on you."
Selene’s eyes widened slightly.
"Right now, since I’m not doing anything at the moment.
It will only take ten to twenty minutes of your time."
Selene blinked.
Her face flushed—the particular, pale, almost translucent blush of a woman whose complexion was so fair that any color at all stood out like a stain on white silk.
It made her look, for a moment, almost human.
She slowly nodded.
She didn’t look at him.
"Okay."
Dexter chuckled internally.
He turned and headed back into the house to prepare.
But first, Dexter needed to deal with the mess in the living room.
He started with the ashes—the particular, fine, grey-white residue of the body Mira had incinerated.
The flames had burned so completely that nothing remained but a faint, almost invisible smudge on the carpet.
He vacuumed it away, watching the particles disappear into the machine with the particular, clinical detachment of a man who had long since stopped being bothered by such things.
Then he addressed the wall.
The spiderweb of cracks where Kreg had slammed against it.
It took less than two minutes to clean the living room.
The wall would need to be repaired, of course.
But he had materials left over from the window repair and he had purchased during the renovation.
But he won’t fix it now.
Not when he had somewhere else to be.
His heartbeat had increased thinking about it but he tried to hide his excitement.
He was about to leave the living room when Mira spoke.
"Won’t you be in trouble?"
Dexter paused.
Mira’s voice was quiet.
"Since they’re dead," she continued, "there might be others who would look for them.
It might cause trouble for you."
Dexter shrugged.
"It doesn’t really matter."
Mira blinked at him.
"It can’t be big enough trouble," he said, "that we can’t handle when the time comes."
She looked at him for a moment.
Then she nodded.
"Okay.
Dexter smiled at her.
He was about to leave when he paused.
He looked down at Lyra.
She was still on the couch, cultivating.
Dexter smiled slightly.
He flipped his fingers.
A pastry appeared on his left palm.He gently placed it on the couch beside Lyra.
when she woke, she would see it.
Dexter left.
He went to the room to prepare.
The bed was already made—the particular, clean, crisp, folded precision of sheets that had been smoothed to perfection.
He placed the oils on the nightstand.
The shockwave glove.
The particular, soft, warm towels he had warmed in advance.
He arranged everything beside Selene bed, then waited.
Two minutes later, the door creaked.
The atmosphere in the room suddenly chilled.
Dexter raised his head.
The door creaked open, and a figure slowly entered.
It was Selene.
Her head was bowed.
Her white hair—the particular, silver, almost luminous cascade of it—covered her entire face as she entered the room.
She moved with the particular, hesitant, almost reluctant grace of a woman who was not used to being seen.
Not used to being the center of attention.
Dexter didn’t speak.
He simply waited.
Selin stepped fully into the room, and the door clicked shut behind her.
The silence stretched.
Then, slowly, she raised her head.
"Where do you want me?" she asked.
Her voice was quiet and shy as she spoke.
Dexter gestured to the bed.
"Lie down.
Face up.
I’ll start with your shoulders."
Selene nodded as she slowly walked up to the bed.

chapters.title: Chapter 241 | Massaging Selene
paragraphs: Dexter voice sounded even thicker and huskier than it should have been as he spoke.
"Lay down."

Selene was dressed in a cardigan over her body and a thick skirt. As she lay down on her bed, Dexter’s heartbeat immediately increased. He closed his eyes and managed to calm himself, his face remaining expressionless as he approached her.
"It’s a deep tissue massage," he explained. "Which is why j would need to remove most of your clothing."
At that moment, Selene glanced at him, her pale white eyes narrowing as if she were about to attack him.

Dexter immediately raised his hands. "Just like I said, it’s a deep tissue massage. The more clothing you wear, the less chance for the technique to work. Don’t worry. Although I’m not gay—I would never think of you girls that way."
Selene frowned, and Dexter felt the chill in the surrounding air increase drastically.
"Are we that unappealing to you?" she asked, her voice carrying a cold edge.
Dexter shook his head immediately. "No, it is actually quite the opposite."
Selene blinked, looking at him.

Dexter continued. "You girls are more appealing than anyone I have ever seen in my entire life. Apart from a single person. But I have a technique to suppress my thoughts and suppress myself. That’s why I said I would never think of you girls that way. This is purely professional."
He paused, letting his words settle.

"And you want to increase the healing to your body, don’t you? To do that, I have to do this massage. If you don’t let me do that, although you will heal, the healing might be even lesser than before."
Selene couldn’t see, but her pale white eyes glanced at him for a few seconds. Then she slowly nodded.
"Okay. I shall lie down on the bed."
Dexter smiled. "I will start to remove your clothes.
Selene’s face flushed red, but she slowly nodded and muttered a tiny "okay" that even with Dexter’s enhanced hearing, he could barely hear.
He successfully removed her cardigan. Then he removed the shirt she was wearing underneath, leaving the bra she wore. His fingers slowly went downward as he removed her skirt.
"I’m removing your skirt right now," he said.
Selene’s face flushed even redder, her entire body turning red. She didn’t say anything, but Dexter attributed it to her saying "okay." So he went down and removed her skirt.
Dexter’s eyes widened as he saw her entire pale skin.

Her skin was even paler than anything he had ever seen in his entire life. He had never expected somebody’s skin to be so white. He had never seen anybody’s skin, or even thought anybody’s skin could be so white, so crispy, and so clean.
Her skin was fucking crispy, clean, white, and fresh. It was like she was a newborn baby. There was no freckle on her skin.

Mira’s skin was fresh and had a few freckles on it, giving it its beauty. Selene’s skin was different entirely, having no freckles, not a single thing, not a single blemish on it. It was fucking white like milk.
Dexter’s heartbeat increased rapidly, even when he tried to distract himself by using his cultivation, by chanting his cultivation chant. The sight of that skin made his heartbeat increase rapidly.
However, he still managed to calm himself as he spoke.
"Turn around."
He spoke with a nonchalant tone, keeping his voice steady.
Selene looked at him for a while, then she turned her back on him, revealing her back.
As she turned her back on him, Dexter, who was using all his best to suppress the redness of his face because Selene was looking at him, suddenly blurted out.

The moment he blurted out, his entire face flushed red in an instant, as blood rushed through his entire face and skin. If Selene had been looking at him at this moment, she would have immediately known what he was thinking.
But she wasn’t looking. She was facing away, her silver hair cascading down her pale back, waiting.

Dexter took a deep breath, steadying himself. He reached for the oil, pouring a generous amount into his palms and warming it between his hands. The familiar scent of herbs filled the room, grounding him.
He placed his hands on her shoulders, and Selene flinched slightly at the contact. Her skin very cool to the touch, almost cold.
"Relax," he said softly. "This will feel strange at first, but it will help."

Dexter then began the technique, channeling his mana through his palms in slow, deliberate pulses. The shockwave glove on his hands hummed faintly, sending micro-vibrations through her muscles, breaking down tension and stimulating circulation.
Selene let out a small breath as he’d shoulders, which had been rigid, slowly began to loosen.

Dexter worked methodically, moving from her shoulders down her spine, then to her lower back. Each press, each pulse, each wave of warmth was measured and precise. He focused entirely on the technique—on the healing—pushing everything else from his mind.
Seconds passed, and then minutes passed in silence. The only sounds were the soft hum of the glove and the occasional whisper of breath.
At that moment, Dexter suddenly knew. If he didn’t do anything else to distract himself, he might actually be consumed by lust. Might actually lose control entirely.
So he suddenly spoke.
"Selene, I want to ask you a question."
Selene was silent for a while before she spoke. "Okay."
Dexter continued, distracting himself from the feeling. "Is this house okay to you, or should I get a different one separate from this place?"
Selene remained silent for a while before she spoke.

"Although this house is quite decent and the neighborhood is quite okay, our families know exactly where we are staying. The Calloway family, the Vance family, the Frost family, and the Ashford family all know exactly where we are staying. We are put at a disadvantage toward them, and we are at their mercy staying exactly here. While I know you have the deed to the house, it doesn’t matter to any of the top three families. They can do whatever they wish in this place. So while this particular neighborhood isn’t bad, it is quite practical to immediately change location, so we won’t be at the mercy of the top three families."
Dexter remained silent for a while as he thought. Selene’s thought was exactly his thought. That was what he had been thinking about when he wanted to get a new house.

chapters.title: Chapter 242 | Selene Bloodline Awakening
paragraphs: Dexter knew he was in trouble.

If he did not distract himself immediately, he was going to lose control. The warm, glowing skin under his hands was sending signals to his brain that his meditation techniques could barely filter out. If he did not engage his mind with something complex, something analytical, he would be consumed by the heat building in his chest.
He needed a distraction.
"Selene," Dexter said suddenly, his voice a bit too loud in the quiet room. "I want to ask you a question."
Selene was silent for a moment. The only sound was the soft hum of the Shockwave Glove against her skin. "Okay."
Dexter kept his hands moving along her shoulders, forcing his brain to focus on strategy. "Is this house okay for you? Or do you think we should get a different one? Somewhere else?"
Selene did not answer right away. He felt her shift slightly under his hands, her head tilting as she considered the question.

"Although this house is decent and the neighborhood is quiet, our families know exactly where we are staying. The Calloway family, the Vance family, the Frost family, and the Ashford family. They all know our exact location. We are at a disadvantage here. We are at their mercy."
She paused.

"Even though you have the deed to the house, it does not matter to the top three families. They can do whatever they wish to this place. They can send whoever they want. It is practical that we change locations immediately, so we are not at their mercy."
Dexter remained silent.

Her thoughts mirrored his own exactly. That was the exact reason he had gone to Harvest Homes. But then he remembered what had happened there. He had been scammed out of one million credits because the Ashford family controlled the city. They had put a word out, and the agency had robbed him.

He realized then that he could not just buy a new house under his own name. The Ashford family controlled Stargate City. If he tried to purchase property anywhere, they would know. They would interfere. The only way to get a new house was to use someone else’s name. Someone unconnected to him. But even that was a gamble.

As he thought about this, his eyes drifted down. The smooth, milky white skin of Selene’s back entered his vision. The information traveled straight to his brain, wiping out his strategic thoughts completely. His body grew hot. The heat rushed up his neck and threatened to flush his face again.

He immediately fled from that train of thought. He needed another topic. Something complex. Something that would force his brain to work overtime and ignore the beautiful woman lying half-naked on his bed.
"Did you dream?" Dexter asked suddenly.
Selene turned her head slightly toward him. "Did I dream about what?"
"Flying," Dexter said. He kept his hands moving down her spine. "Do you dream about flying? Or something else?
Selene was quiet. "No, not really. Why do you ask?"
Dexter frowned.

Mira had dreamed about flying. She dreamed about wings ripping out of her back. He had assumed that the bloodline awakening would manifest as wings for all three girls. But Selene was saying she didn’t dream about flying.
That meant two things. Either Selene’s bloodline was not manifesting yet, or the bloodline she was awakening did not involve wings. Each of them might get a different bloodline.
Dexter shook his head. "Nothing. Don’t worry about it."
"But I dreamt about something else," Selene said suddenly.
Dexter’s interest peaked. The strategic part of his brain engaged again, fighting back the biological distractions. "What did you dream about?"
"It isn’t about flying," Selene said. "It’s about control. No, not control." She paused, searching for the right word. "I dreamt that I could see."
Dexter’s hands stopped on her lower back. The hum of the glove continued, but his hands were frozen. "You dreamt you could see?"

"Yes," Selene said. Her voice was soft, carrying a weight of wonder and sadness. "The dream was very vivid. I dreamt I could see almost everybody in the world. Even those hidden in different dimensions. Even those hidden across the entire earth. I felt like a god staring down at everybody."
Dexter stared at the back of her head. His mind was racing. Seeing everyone. Hidden dimensions. God-like perception.
"Of course, even if the dream was realistic, I know it was just a dream," Selene added quietly.
Dexter did not respond.

His mind was no longer on the massage. It was no longer on her skin. It was on her face. He was looking at her face, or rather, the side of her face as she lay turned away from him. And suddenly, he noticed something he had noticed before but had dismissed.
Three distinct marks on her face.
They were very faded. So faded that he had thought it was an illusion the first time he saw them. But now, with the morning light hitting her face at the right angle, he could see them clearly.
One mark was on her forehead. Right in the center. Perfectly horizontal.
Another mark was underneath her left eye. A thin, curved line.
And the third mark was underneath her right eye. Identical to the left.
Three marks. Like closed eyes.

His brain connected the marks to her dream. Mira’s marks were on her shoulder blades. They were ten inches long and looked like scars from wings trying to rip through. They matched her dream of flying like a phoenix.
Selene’s marks were on her face. On her forehead and under her eyes. They matched her dream of seeing like a god.
The bloodline was manifesting differently for each of them.
Mira was getting wings. A Phoenix bloodline.
Selene was getting eyes. A Clairvoyance bloodline. Or something similar. A bloodline of sight.

The irony was not lost on Dexter. Selene was blind. She had been blind for three years. And the bloodline she was awakening was giving her marks around her eyes. A bloodline of vision for a woman who could not see.
Selene was becoming something else.
Something with eyes.
What was Lyra becoming?
The thought brought him back to Aurelyx. The Shadow Queen.
If Mira was getting wings, and Selene was getting eyes, what was Lyra getting? And more importantly, what was Aurelyx getting?
The Avatar Fruit sat in his spatial storage. Waiting. The potential solution to a problem that was growing more complex by the day.

chapters.title: Chapter 243 | Selene Massage
paragraphs: There were hundreds of thousands of known bloodlines in the world. The Bloodline Codex, maintained by the Hero Association, catalogued over three hundred thousand of them across every grade and type — and the Codex was still incomplete. Some bloodlines existed outside its pages. Some had never been recorded at all. Some were so rare, so ancient, or so powerful that no one had encountered them in living memory, and therefore no one had thought to write them down.
Without the system, identifying a bloodline from its early manifestation marks alone was impossible.
What Dexter could tell was that it was high-grade.
The higher the grade, the harder the manifestation. The longer the body took to integrate it. The more the body had to adapt before the bloodline could fully emerge.

That was why the girls hadn’t awakened yet. It seeded the bloodline into the body’s DNA, and then the body had to merge with it. Restructure itself at a cellular level to accommodate a new genetic framework.
With the system, the process would have been instantaneous. When the system had given Dexter his Flame Demon Bloodline, the integration had taken seconds.
But the girls didn’t have the system.
So the bloodline would only integrate with time.
And judging by the marks on Selene’s face and Mira’s back, that pace was accelerating.
The massage continued.

His hands moved down Selene’s spine. The Shockwave Glove hummed. The oil glistened. The 108 Body Massage Sutra guided his fingers through the precise, prescribed patterns that stimulated nerve regeneration and accelerated healing.
He noticed her skin again.
Every inch of Selene was silky and milky white and was cool to the touch. Not cold the way poor circulation is cold.
Dexter suddenly had an idea.
He activated his Heavenly Flame.
A thread — the thinnest, most precisely calibrated thread of heat his evolved bloodline could produce.
He channeled it through his hands, Into her skin.

The effect was immediate.

That cold was being touched by heat for the first time.

The sound hit Dexter like a freight train.
His hands froze and arousal spiked instantly.

His brain was willing. His body was not and his trousers immediately became tight.

None of it worked.

He was losing.

Her back was beautiful.

Something that made the situation considerably worse.
Selene was not flat.

paragraphs: "You’ve never been here, have you?" Dexter asked.
Lyra shook her head. Her telepathic voice echoed in his mind.
"No. This is the first time I’m seeing your room. It is quite nice. Spacious."
Dexter blinked. "Yeah. It is quite spacious. I would have let one of you girls come share the room with me, but it would be inappropriate. And I don’t think any of you would accept."
Lyra shrugged. The gesture was casual. Easy.
"It’s all right. The three of us are quite comfortable sleeping in one room."
Dexter nodded as he began preparing the bed. Spreading the blanket. Adjusting the pillow.
"Even though I feel like you girls need your own personal rooms," he said.
Lyra continued looking around. Her fingers touched the edge of his nightstand. Traced the grain of the wood.

"Yeah. We are women, so we definitely need privacy. However, since the three of us are cultivating the same technique, there is no secret between us. So there is not much need for privacy between ourselves."
She paused.
"But getting a new house would be much better."
Dexter nodded. He agreed completely but he would have been moving if not for the incident with the Harvest Home.
The bed was ready. Pillow positioned, oil, glove, towel, all in place.
He looked at Lyra.
"Remove your outer clothing," he said. "The massage works best on bare skin."
Lyra was caught off haired by Dexter’s bluntness and she was immediately shy.
Dexter opened his mouth to explain about deep tissue massage and mana transfer and pressure points and the importance of direct skin contact for optimal technique performance.
L

Before the first word of the explanation left his mouth, Lyra reached for the hem of her gown and pulled it off in one swift motion and then dropped it beside the bed without ceremony, revealing a dark bra and dark panties.
Dexter’s breath caught and he was stunned.
Lyra’s chest was massive that even her bra was struggling to fully hold them.
Selene’s chest wasn’t as massive but her back compensated for it. Mira hed both front and back. While not that large, it was a handful while Lyra had a massive front!
He immediately inhaled and calmed himself.
"Come," he said. His voice was steady. "Lie down on the bed."
Lyra blinked at him innocently and obviously as she nodded and walked to the bed. Lay down. Face down.
On the blanket. Her dark hair spread across the pillow. Her hands rested at her sides.
Dexter looked at her.
Even face down, Lyra’s chest was visible, spreading to the sides, visible from above as a curve of flesh that extended beyond the width of her ribcage.
Dexter inhaled deeply and fit his own peace of mind, he cut off the circulation to his lower body!
He started with her legs.
He placed his oiled hands on her right foot and began.
Her feet were clean. Incredibly clean. The particular, soft, smooth, well-maintained quality of skin that had been cared for despite three years of hardship.
Then Lyra spoke.
"Your bed smells nice and masculine."
The words arrived in his mind through the telepathic connection.
Dexter’s hands paused on her calf.
"Thank you," he said.
Then Lyra spoke again.
"Do you use perfume? Or is this your natural musky scent?"
Dexter blinked.
"No," he said. "I don’t use perfume."
Lyra raised her head. Turned it slightly to look back at him.
"That is really surprising," she said. Her telepathic voice carried genuine wonder. "Because your bed smells really good. I can’t quite place the smell. It is very exotic. And attractive."
The last word landed in Dexter’s mind with the particular, weighted, loaded quality of a term that was being used in a specific, biological, pheromone-related context.
Dexter knew what she was talking about.
His bloodline.
The Ancient Flame Demon Bloodline, evolved to its Ancient Grade, had been changing his body in ways that went beyond cultivation and combat ability.
His skin produced pheromones.
The particular, concentrated, enhanced, bloodline-amplified pheromones that an Demon Bloodline generated as a passive byproduct of its evolutionary advancement.
The pheromones were designed by the bloodline’s biological framework to attract.
The effect was not something Dexter could control.
Everyone who entered his room would smell it.

The particular, exotic, musky, impossible-to-identify but impossible-to-ignore scent that was not perfume and not cologne and not any commercially produced fragrance but was instead the chemical signature of his bloodline.
To women, the effect was particularly pronounced. The pheromones were designed to be attractive to females.

Not consciously. Not in a way that could be identified or resisted through awareness. The attraction operated at the level of instinct. At the level of biology. At the level where the body responded to chemical signals before the brain could evaluate them.
Lyra was responding.
Her body, pressed against his bed, surrounded by his scent, was processing the pheromones through her olfactory system.

The chemical signals were traveling through her nasal passages to her limbic system, where they were triggering responses that she was interpreting as "exotic" and "attractive" without understanding the biological mechanism behind the interpretation.
She didn’t know it was pheromones.
She just knew his bed smelled good.
Dexter knew it was pheromones.

And he knew that the pheromones, combined with the massage, combined with the physical intimacy of the situation, combined with the fact that Lyra was already predisposed to find him attractive, were creating a particular, volatile, potentially combustible combination of biological and emotional factors that he needed to manage very carefully.
"It’s just my natural scent," Dexter said. "Nothing special."
Lyra turned her head back into the pillow and then pressed her nose into it and inhaled deeply.
If was as though she didn’t mind he was inhaling his scent and just did it.
"It’s very nice," she murmured into the pillow. Her telepathic voice was drowsy and really relaxed. "Very masculine and also very warm. Are you sure you aren’t using any perfume?"
She asked suspiciously.
Dexter chuckled ass he continued his massage. "There’s no reason I’d lie to you Lyra."
