If you were to say something, Selin had a big front, Lyra had a big front, Selin had a big back. It was as if they were each compensating for the other. It was quite funny. And Mira was the perfect combination of the two of them, although her front and her back weren’t as big as Lyra’s front and Selin’s back. It was quite a handful also, and was above average.
Dexter continued to massage Lyra’s leg.
Then suddenly Lyra spoke. "I am feeling something."
Dexter was stunned. "What was that?"
Lyra frowned. Lyra, who was lying there on her front, suddenly spoke to Dexter’s mind. "I have no idea what it is, but I really like it. Continue."

Dexter was quite a bit stunned because he was directly massaging Lyra’s upper thigh. With the vibration of the shockwave glove, the vibration was definitely going through her pelvis area. For her to say she was feeling something—
Dexter at first thought she was feeling pain. "Is it painful?"
Lyra remained silent for a while before she said, "No. No, it’s not painful. It’s actually quite the opposite."
Dexter was stunned.
Quite the opposite? Which meant—
He thought for a bit, then his eyes widened slightly as he knew what she was talking about.
Lyra continued, "It is quite enjoyable. I like it. It’s quite enjoyable.
Dexter paused for a bit. He quickly knew what she was talking about.
Without hesitation, he went upwards. He continued massaging her pelvis area, but then he switched upwards to her upper back as he continued massaging her upper back.

If he continued to massage her pelvis, if he continued to massage her upper thighs and her pelvis area, it would count as taking advantage of her. He didn’t want to take advantage of her. If he wanted to do something with her, he would want it to be genuine. He didn’t want to take advantage of Lyra at all.
So he stopped massaging her upper thigh and went to her waist, massaging her waist.
As he did this, Lyra suddenly let out a slight groan of dissatisfaction.

chapters.title: Chapter 246 | Kissing Lyra
paragraphs: "Like I said, I’d really like to know how kissing feels," Lyra said, her finger still unconsciously stroking her lips.
Dexter looked at her. At the way her pale finger traced the soft curve of her mouth. At the innocent curiosity in her eyes. He shook his head to clear his mind of the thought.
"If you see someone you like," he said, "then you can try kissing them."
Lyra looked at him. She stayed silent for a while, but then her voice echoed in his mind.
"What if the person? What if I’m not sure if the person I like likes me back?"
Dexter was stunned. He gazed into Lyra’s eyes. She was looking directly at him. She was looking directly at him as she said this with all seriousness.

At first, he thought it was Arilex talking. He thought her second personality had surfaced. But he listened to her heartbeat—and he knew it was Lyra. From the heartbeat, it was Lyra who was speaking at this moment. It was truly Lyra.
He remained stunned for a while before he replied.
"Even if you are not sure the person might like you back, you still have to take the risk. You still have to take that risk. Because remaining silent won’t achieve much."
Lyra looked at Dexter for a while, then nodded her head. "You’re right. Remaining silent won’t achieve anything. Taking the risk would be much better."
She blinked her eyes and looked at him.

"But I haven’t kissed anyone before. If I kiss the person I like, but I don’t know how to kiss, and if I kiss the person I like and the person doesn’t like it—she doesn’t like the way I kiss—it might be bad."
Dexter blinked his eyes. He tilted his head and pondered.
"Not really. If the person truly likes you, regardless of whether you know how to kiss or not, they would like it as long as you kiss them."
Lyra blinked her eyes. "I’m not really sure about that."
Dexter didn’t say anything. He remained silent.
Then suddenly Lyra spoke.
"How about you teach me?"
Dexter’s hands, which were massaging Lyra’s body, froze. His mind went blank.
Teach her? What does she mean, teach her?
They were talking about kissing, and she was saying he should teach her how to kiss. Isn’t that basically both of them kissing?
He immediately focused. He used his enhanced hearing talent again and heard Lyra’s heartbeat. It was a bit faster this time. But it was still Lyra’s signature heartbeat—just slightly faster.
Dexter stared at Lyra for a while before he said, "How should I teach you how to kiss?"
Lyra smiled innocently. She looked at him innocently.
"Dummy. Of course you have to use your lips. I know you have a lot of experience in kissing. So of course you use your lips to teach me how to kiss."
Dexter was flabbergasted.

He had never expected such a situation to occur right at this exact moment. He didn’t know what to do. Of course he would like to kiss Lyra. But he didn’t want it to be like he was taking advantage of her.
So he asked, "Are you sure?
Lyra nodded her head. "Yes, I’m sure. I want you to teach me how to kiss."
Dexter inhaled and told her, "All right. You have to relax your body first."
Lyra nodded her head. "I am quite relaxed."
She leaned on the bed as she relaxed quite a bit. She relaxed very well on the bed.
She relaxed as she raised her eyes toward him, waiting patiently. Dexter looked at Lyra as his heartbeat increased slightly. His heartbeat increased slightly as he looked at her.
Then slowly his face edged toward her. Slowly his face edged toward her. Just when his face was ten inches away from her face, he spoke to Lyra.
"Do you prefer—"
Just when he was ten inches away from her face, Lyra suddenly spoke. "Should I close my eyes, or should I open them?"
Dexter paused. Dexter paused as he spoke. Dexter paused, then later he spoke.

"It depends on what you are feeling during the kiss. Your eyes may remain open, and once you are kissing, your eyes may close naturally. I’m not really sure. It depends on you. I’m not really sure, but it depends on each person’s preference."
Lyra blinked her eyes as she nodded her head and said, "Okay. Okay, let’s continue."
She gave him a small smile.

Dexter blinked and then he inhaled deeply as he exhaled slowly. As he held his breath, he inhaled deeply and held his breath as his face inched closer toward her. He edged closer and closer toward her—five inches, four inches, three inches, two inches—and then their lips met.
Dexter felt his spine jolt slightly as his lips met hers. Lyra’s lips were incredibly soft. Really, really nice. Her lips were incredibly soft and really, really nice.

As their lips met, Dexter’s eyes were still open. Lyra’s eyes immediately closed as their lips met. Dexter checked to see if she wasn’t uncomfortable, saying that she wasn’t uncomfortable. He parted his lips and then took her lower lip into his lips, squeezing her lower lip with both of his lips as he slightly suckled on it. It was really, really soft.
By the time he caught himself, he had kissed Lyra’s lips for about a full minute. At that time, it was even Lyra’s moan. Lyra’s unconscious soft moan that jolted him up.

Dexter’s eyes widened. He didn’t even realize his eyes had been closed throughout. His eyes widened as he looked down at Lyra and immediately removed his lips as he pulled back, a bit embarrassed and he cleared his throat.
Lyra’s eyes fluttered open. Her face was flushed, her breathing slightly uneven as she unconsciously licked her lips as she looked at him with an expression he couldn’t quite read.
"That’s..." she started, then paused. Her voice echoed in his mind like the sound of a thousand siren. "That’s what kissing feels like?"
Dexter blinked his eyes and nodded. "That’s a simple kiss."
Lyra touched her lips again, the same unconscious gesture from before. "It felt... nice. Warm. I liked it."
Dexter smiled slightly. "Good."
Lyra looked at him, then spoke again. "Can we do it again? I want to practice more."
Dexter blinked. His heartbeat, which had been relatively steady, suddenly quickened.
"Lyra..."
She looked at him innocently. "What? You said you would teach me. I need more practice to learn properly."
Dexter stared at her for a long moment. Then he sighed. ’This girl is really naughty.’
A small smile tugged at his lips as he thought.
"All right. One more time."
Lyra smiled brightly. She closed her eyes and tilted her head back, waiting.
Dexter looked at her. At her closed eyes. At her parted lips. At the gentle rise and fall of her chest beneath the dark fabric of her bra.
He leaned in again.

This time, the kiss was different. Slower. More deliberate. He pressed his lips to hers and held them there, letting the warmth build between them. Lyra made a small sound—a soft, contented hum that vibrated against his mouth.

He moved his lips gently, guiding her, teaching her without words. She followed his lead, her lips soft and pliant beneath his. When he pulled back slightly, she leaned forward, chasing the contact, and he had to suppress a smile.
"Easy," he whispered.
She opened her eyes, looking up at him with that same innocent curiosity. "Did I do something wrong?"
"No," he said. "You’re doing fine. Just... let it happen naturally."
She nodded and closed her eyes again.
He kissed her a third time. This time, he let his hand move to her cheek, cupping it gently. Her skin was warm beneath his palm. She leaned into his touch, a small sigh escaping her lips.
The kiss deepened. Not much—just enough to let her feel something more than simple pressure. He tilted his head slightly, changing the angle, and she followed, her lips parting just a fraction.
When he finally pulled back, they were both breathing a little harder.
Lyra’s eyes remained closed for a moment. Then they opened, and she looked at him with a soft, dazed expression.
"That was..." She paused, searching for words. "That was really nice."
Dexter nodded. "Good."
She touched her lips again. "I think I understand now. Why people like it so much."
Dexter smiled slightly. "I’m glad."
Lyra looked at him for a long moment. Then she spoke again, her voice quiet in his mind.
"Thank you, Dexter. For teaching me."
He nodded. "You’re welcome."
She settled back onto the bed, her body relaxing into the sheets. Her eyes were still on him, soft and warm.
"Can we do this again sometime?" she asked. "The massage, I mean. And... maybe the kissing too?"
Dexter blinked. His heartbeat, which had finally begun to settle, quickened again.
"We’ll see," he said.
Lyra smiled happily as she replied.
"Okay, i will hold you to that."
Dexter shook his head, a small chuckle escaping him. He continued the massage after that, working on her shoulders, her arms, her back. But the atmosphere in the room had shifted.

chapters.title: Chapter 247 | Repairing The House
paragraphs: By the time Dexter finished massaging Lyra, she had already fallen deeply asleep.
Dexter only noticed when he stopped working on her shoulders and received no response from her.
"Lyra?"
Nothing.
Her breathing had become slow and steady, and her face looked completely relaxed against his pillow.
Dexter stared at her for a moment.
"She actually fell asleep..."

A small smile appeared on his face as he picked up the towel beside the bowl of warm water. He carefully wiped away the remaining massage oil from her skin so she wouldn’t wake up feeling sticky or uncomfortable.
Once he was satisfied, he pulled the blanket over her but Dexter remained standing beside the bed.
His eyes wandered toward Lyra’s face before eventually settling on her lips. They were slightly parted, soft and pink, still faintly glistening from where she had licked them earlier.
For a brief moment, the memory of their earlier kiss returned. The warmth of her lips against his.
And along with it came the urge to kiss her again.
Dexter immediately pushed the thought aside.
Lyra was asleep.
Yes, she had given him permission earlier, but that had been different. She had been awake, curious and probably wanted to understand what kissing felt like.
That didn’t mean he could simply kiss her whenever he wanted.
Especially while she was sleeping.
That would be taking advantage of her. And despite everything, Dexter still had his principles. He had promised himself he would protect these girls, not exploit them.
Dexter shook his head.
"Forget it."
He turned toward the door.
Before leaving, however, he glanced back one final time.
Then Dexter quietly closed the door behind him.
The house had become unusually peaceful.
Selene was already sleeping in the girls’ shared room, while Lyra had taken over Dexter’s bedroom. The two of them were resting.
That left only one of his three wives awake.
Mira.
Dexter headed toward the living room.
Just as he expected, Mira was there.

She sat in her wheelchair opposite the window, occupying the same position where she usually cultivated. The sun streaming through the glass cast her in its orange glow that made her hair look like it was on fire.
Her eyes were closed, her breathing calm, and there was almost no movement from her body.
For a second, Dexter wondered if she had fallen asleep while cultivating.
But the moment he stepped farther into the room, Mira’s head tilted slightly toward him.
She had sensed his presence but her eyes never opened. After acknowledging him, she simply turned her head forward again and resumed her cultivation.
Dexter didn’t disturb her.
He quietly entered the living room and sat down on the couch.
For several moments, silence filled the house.
Then Dexter’s attention shifted toward the wall.
His expression immediately changed.
Two ugly holes remained there.

They were souvenirs from his earlier confrontation with Kreg and his thugs. When Dexter had punched Kreg and one of his men, both of them had been sent smashing through the wall. He had already swept away the broken pieces and debris afterward, but cleaning the floor hadn’t exactly solved the bigger problem.
Two enormous holes were still glaring at him.
Dexter stared at them.
The longer he looked, the uglier they seemed to become.
He sighed.
"I really did a number on this place."
His gaze briefly moved toward Mira.
She didn’t react.
Dexter looked back at the wall.
He couldn’t exactly leave the house like this. The girls deserved to live somewhere that didn’t remind them of violence every time they walked into the room. They had already endured enough.
Fortunately, when he had bought materials for renovating the house, he had purchased more than they eventually needed. Some of the leftover supplies were still sitting inside the storage room.
That should be enough.
Dexter stood.
Since everyone else was sleeping or cultivating, there wasn’t much else for him to do anyway.
He might as well fix the damage he had caused.

He entered the storage room and began searching through the remaining renovation materials. Boxes of drywall patches, joint compound, sandpaper, paint—everything he needed was still there, tucked away in the corner.
It didn’t take long before he found what he needed.
Dexter carried everything into the living room and placed the materials near the damaged wall.
Then he got to work.

He wasn’t a professional builder, but this wasn’t his first time doing basic repair work either. He knew enough to understand what needed to be done. He measured the holes, cut the patches to size, and fitted them into place.
Piece by piece, the holes began disappearing.
The quiet living room soon filled with the soft sounds of Dexter working. The scrape of the putty knife. The rustle of sandpaper. The occasional creak of the floorboards as he shifted his weight.
Mira remained near the window throughout the entire process.
She didn’t speak.
Dexter didn’t bother her either.

It created a strangely peaceful atmosphere. One person cultivated. The other repaired a wall he had accidentally destroyed by punching people through it. A perfectly normal night in Dexter’s increasingly abnormal life.
Time slipped past.
Roughly an hour later, Dexter finally stepped backward and examined his work.
The two holes were gone.

He wiped the sweat from his forehead with his arm before looking over the repaired sections carefully. The patches were smooth, the edges blended, and he had even managed to match the paint reasonably well.
It wasn’t perfect.
Anyone experienced in construction would probably notice the difference immediately. But considering what the wall had looked like an hour ago?
Dexter nodded with satisfaction.
"Good enough."
At least nobody could walk into the house and immediately ask why there were two human-sized holes in the living-room wall.

Dexter crouched and gathered the remaining materials. After returning everything useful to the storage room, he came back with a broom and cleaned the floor. By the time he finished, the living room looked considerably better and almost normal. What was left was the wall paper.
Dexter placed both hands on his waist and inspected his work.
"Nice."

"Lyra?"

chapters.title: Chapter 248 | You’re Blushing
paragraphs: "You’re quite good at this."
Dexter paused.
He had just finished inspecting the repaired section of the wall when Mira’s voice suddenly came from behind him.

Turning around, he saw that Mira had finally opened her eyes. She had turned her wheelchair slightly and was now studying the wall he had repaired. Her gaze moved across the smooth surface and there was a faint look of admiration in her eyes.
Dexter smiled. "Yeah. I’ve gotten a bit of practice over the years."
Mira looked from the wall to him.
"Practice?"

Dexter shrugged causally as he brushed some dust from his hands. "I was a servant at the Ashford Estate all my life. You learn to do a little bit of everything when you’re the person everyone calls whenever something needs fixing."
Mira slowly nodded.
For several seconds, she said nothing as her expression became thoughtful. Her eyes narrowed slightly as she studied hum.
"If you hadn’t mentioned it, I would’ve forgotten you were a servant with the Ashford family."
Dexter blinked before chuckling. "Why do you say that?"
"Isn’t it obvious?"
Mira turned her wheelchair completely toward him.
"The raw materials you somehow get your hands on. The techniques you possess. Those ridiculously high-grade meals you cook..."
She paused.
"Any one of those things would make you unusual. But all of them together?"
Her eyes narrowed slightly.
"We have established the fact thag you’re not ordinary."
Dexter remained silent.
Mira continued calmly. "And yet I’m supposed to believe that someone like you spent years living as a servant in the Ashford family despite being their firstborn?"
She tilted her head slightly, her dark eyes never leaving his face.
"Was being a servant only a cover?"
For once, Dexter didn’t immediately answer.
He looked at Mira for a but then the corner of Dexter’s mouth curled upward to an imperceptible smile.
"Does it really matter whether it was a cover or not?"
Mira stared at him.
Then she shrugged dismissively.
"You’re right."
"It doesn’t really matter."
She turned slightly toward the window, gazing outside.
"Besides, you wouldn’t tell me anyway."
Dexter’s smile faded a little.
He walked closer, the floorboards creaking softly beneath his feet. His presence seemed to fill the space around her, and yet he was careful not to crowd her.
"It’s not that I don’t want to tell you."
Mira glanced at him.
Dexter looked toward the window as he sighed.
"That part of my life is already the past."
"I’ve spent enough time thinking about what happened before. I’m trying to focus on what comes next."
Mira remained silent.
Then Dexter looked directly at her. His eyes met hers with an intensity that made her pause.
"And you three are my future."
Mira froze.
For several seconds, she simply stared at him.
She clearly hadn’t expected that answer.
A faint redness slowly appeared on her cheeks. It was subtle—just a hint of pink against her pale skin.
Mira immediately looked away.
"Okay, whatever."
Dexter stared at her.
Then his lips slowly curved into a grin.
"Are you blushing?"
Mira’s head snapped toward him. Her eyes flashed with something dangerous as she glared.
"Me?"
Dexter’s grin widened.
"Yes, you."
"Blush?"
Mira scoffed as though he had just accused her of committing some terrible crime. The sound was sharp, dismissive, and entirely unconvincing.
"Nothing could ever make me blush."
"Really?"
"Really."
Dexter took a step toward her.
Mira’s eyes immediately narrowed.
Dexter took another step.
She watched him suspiciously.
"What are you trying to do?"
Dexter stopped beside her wheelchair. He wore such an innocent expression that it immediately made Mira even more suspicious. The corners of his eyes crinkled slightly.
"Nothing."
"Dexter."
"Nothing much."
He leaned slightly closer. His voice dropped to a murmur.
"Just trying to seduce you."
Mira stared at him.
Then she sneered.
"Seduce me?"
A short laugh escaped her. It was sharp and full of disbelief.
"Ha! Have you already forgotten what I told you? You won’t succeed."
Dexter placed one hand against his chest as though her words had wounded him. He let out a dramatic sigh.
"Never say never."
"I just did."
"That doesn’t make it true."
"It does when I’m the one saying it."
Dexter chuckled.
Mira placed her hand underneath her jaw.
There was confidence written all over her face now as she stared at him like a winner.
Dexter noticed it.
And somehow, that only made him want to tease her more.
He stepped around the wheelchair until he stood directly in front of her. Mira followed him with her eyes, refusing to be the first to look away.
"Moreover," Dexter said, "we still have a month, right?"
The confidence on Mira’s face flickered for a second.
But Dexter caught it and his smile widened.
Mira immediately recovered.
"So?
"So..." Dexter crouched slightly until their eyes were closer to the same level. "That means I still have plenty of time."
"To embarrass yourself?"
"To make you fall for me."
Mira almost laughed.
"Your confidence is impressive."
"Thank you."
"That wasn’t a compliment."
"I’ve decided to accept it as one."
Mira rolled her eyes.
"You’re hopeless."
"And yet you’re doing it again."
Her hand immediately rose toward her cheeks.
The instant she realized what she had done, Mira froze.
Dexter’s grin became unbearable. It spread across his face like sunlight, warm and infuriating.
Mira slowly lowered her hand.
"You tricked me."
"I didn’t say you were actually blushing."
Mira’s eyes sharpened as she gritted her teeth and glared at him.
"Dexter!"
He burst out laughing.
Mira’s expression darkened, but there was a giant smile.
"You have three seconds to get away from me."
"Or what?"
"Three."
Dexter straightened.
"I’m curious now."
"Two."
"What’s going to happen at zero?"
Mira’s cultivation energy suddenly stirred around her. The air grew hottter, and a faint pressure began to press against the edges of the room.
Dexter’s smile disappeared.
"One."
"Goodbye, Mira."
He immediately turned around.
"Ha!" Mira laughed victiriously.
Dexter immediately stopped in hus teacks and he slowly looked over his shoulder.
Mira had the faintest victorious smile on her face. It was small, almost imperceptible, but it was there.
That did it.
Dexter turned back toward her.
Mira’s smile vanished.
"What?"
"You know," Dexter said, walking toward her again, "for someone who claims she can’t be seduced, you seem awfully interested in whether I’m giving up."
"I couldn’t care less."
"Then why are you smiling?"
"I wasn’t."
"You were."
"You’re imagining things."

chapters.title: Chapter 249 | Preparations
paragraphs: Dexter stopped beside her again. His presence was warm, familiar, and entirely too close.
For a few seconds, neither spoke. The playful atmosphere slowly settled into something quieter. Something more real.
Mira looked toward the repaired wall.
Then toward Dexter.
"Dexter."
"Hmm?"
The teasing light in her eyes faded and her expression became more serious.
"Do you really mean that?"
"Mean what?"
"What you said earlier."
Dexter knew exactly what she meant.
Still, he waited.
Mira hesitated like she didn’t want to ask but still, she continued.
"That we’re your future."
The teasing disappeared from Dexter’s face.
He looked at her properly.
"Yes."
Mira’s eyes narrowed as she stared deeply into his eyes and she immediately saw that he wasn’t joking and extremely serious too.
Mira’s eyes remained on him for a moment before she looked away.
"Idiot."
Dexter smiled.
"That sounded suspiciously affectionate."
"It wasn’t."
"Of course."
"And stop smiling."
"I’m not smiling."
"You clearly are."
Dexter’s smile only widened.
Mira sighed and turned her wheelchair back toward the window.
"You’re irritating."
"And I still have a month."
Mira closed her eyes again.
"You’ll need more than a month."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
That wasn’t the same as saying he would never succeed.
Interesting, very interesting, Dexter decided not to point that out, Dexter turned toward the repaired wall, then looked at Mira one final time.
Later that night, he was just done washing the plates when a knock came from the front gate.

Dexter’s eyes shifted toward the sound. He didn’t immediately move. Instead, he focused his enhanced hearing, letting the sounds of the night sharpen around him. The faint rustling of leaves. Distant voices from neighboring houses. The soft hum of insects in the cool air.
And finally, the steady heartbeat of the person standing outside his gate.
Dexter recognized it immediately.
"Tessa."

He got up and headed outside, his footsteps quiet against the floorboards. The house was still, everyone else asleep or cultivating. He opened the front door and walked to the gate, the night air cool against his skin.
When Dexter opened the gate, Tessa was standing there waiting for him. The moonlight caught her features, highlighting the smile that always seemed to hover at the corners of her lips.
"There you are."
"As if you haven’t been knocking for less than a minute," Dexter replied.

Tessa ignored that. As usual, she had come to settle the money from the meals Dexter had prepared and supplied to her father’s bakery. After accounting for her own agreed cut, she transferred Dexter’s share of the day’s earnings.
Dexter checked the transaction and nodded. Everything was correct.

Normally, they would also discuss how many meals he needed to prepare for the next day. Tonight, however, there was no need. Tomorrow was the neighborhood festival, and most businesses in the area would be closed, including Tessa’s father’s bakery.
For once, Dexter didn’t have a mountain of meals waiting to be cooked before sunrise.
"Alright, Tessa. Goodnight."
He was about to close the gate when Tessa suddenly stopped him.
"Wait."
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "What?"
"You’re preparing for tomorrow, right?"
Dexter gave her a strange look. "I already told you I’m coming."
"I know that."
"Then what preparations are you talking about?"
Tessa blinked. Then realization appeared on her face. "You seriously don’t know?"
"Know what?"
"About the food."
"What food?"
Tessa stared at him for several seconds. Then she sighed, the sound heavy with exaggerated patience. "You really don’t know."
Dexter folded his arms. "That’s why I’m asking."

Tessa stepped a little closer. The smell of bread and sugar clung to her clothes—the familiar scent of the bakery she worked at every day. "Everyone calls it a festival, but it’s actually more like a huge neighborhood picnic."
Dexter nodded slowly. "Okay..."
"Families come out, people sit together, talk, eat, and enjoy themselves. Most importantly, everyone brings food."
"That makes sense."
"I’m not finished."
Dexter gestured for her to continue.
"We exchange meals.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "Exchange?"
"Yeah. It’s a tradition around here. You cook something, someone else cooks something, then everyone shares. You give people some of your food and they’ll give you some of theirs."
Dexter finally understood. "So basically, I need to cook enough food to share."
"Exactly!"
Tessa smiled brightly. A small dimple appeared on her cheek, softening her features. It was a smile that made her look younger, more carefree.
"And I’ll be expecting yours tomorrow."
Dexter narrowed his eyes playfully. "Now I understand why you came all the way here to explain the tradition."
"What?"
"You just want free food."
Tessa placed a hand against her chest, feigning offense. "Free food? It’s a cultural exchange."
Dexter almost laughed. "Of course."
"A very important cultural exchange."
"Right."
Tessa pointed at him. "So make sure you save some for me. I want to taste more of your cooking."
Dexter smiled. "If you’re late, it won’t be my fault if everything finishes."
Tessa’s mouth immediately fell open. Then she pouted. "You’re trying to bully me."
"I’m warning you."
"That’s bullying."
Dexter chuckled and waved his hand. "Goodnight, Tessa."
Tessa continued pouting for another second before eventually smiling. "Goodnight, Dexter. See you tomorrow."
"See you tomorrow."
She waved before turning away. Dexter watched her leave, her figure growing smaller as she walked down the quiet street. Then he closed and locked the gate.
He returned inside.

The house was quiet again. Everyone had already eaten. Selene and Lyra had woken up earlier in the evening, and Lyra had returned to the girls’ room after eating. Mira had eaten as well. By now, everyone had retired for the night.
Dexter entered his bedroom and sat on the edge of his bed.
Tomorrow.
He leaned backward slightly and thought about it. Tomorrow would be the first time in quite a while that he was taking all three girls outside simply to enjoy themselves.
No fighting. No cultivation emergency. No business. No thugs smashing through walls.
At least, Dexter hoped so.
He wasn’t entirely sure whether he should be nervous about taking all three of his wives to a neighborhood festival at once. Still...
Dexter smiled.
He was looking forward to it. The girls had spent far too much time inside the house recently. A change of scenery would be good for them.
Especially Mira.

He opened the front door and walked to the gate, the night air cool against his skin.
When Dexter opened the gate, Tessa was standing there waiting for him.
The moonlight caught her features, highlighting the smile that always seemed to hover at the corners of her lips.
"There you are."
"As if you haven’t been knocking for less than a minute," Dexter replied.
Tessa ignored that.
As usual, she had come to settle the money from the meals Dexter had prepared and supplied to her father’s bakery.
After accounting for her own agreed cut, she transferred Dexter’s share of the day’s earnings.
Dexter checked the transaction and nodded.
Everything was correct.
Normally, they would also discuss how many meals he needed to prepare for the next day.
Tonight, however, there was no need.
Tomorrow was the neighborhood festival, and most businesses in the area would be closed, including Tessa’s father’s bakery.
For once, Dexter didn’t have a mountain of meals waiting to be cooked before sunrise.
"Alright, Tessa.
Goodnight."
He was about to close the gate when Tessa suddenly stopped him.
"Wait."
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"What?"
"You’re preparing for tomorrow, right?"
Dexter gave her a strange look.
"I already told you I’m coming."
"I know that."
"Then what preparations are you talking about?"
Tessa blinked.
Then realization appeared on her face.
"You seriously don’t know?"
"Know what?"
"About the food."
"What food?"
Tessa stared at him for several seconds.
Then she sighed, the sound heavy with exaggerated patience.
"You really don’t know."
Dexter folded his arms.
"That’s why I’m asking."
Tessa stepped a little closer.
The smell of bread and sugar clung to her clothes—the familiar scent of the bakery she worked at every day.
"Everyone calls it a festival, but it’s actually more like a huge neighborhood picnic."
Dexter nodded slowly.
"Okay..."
"Families come out, people sit together, talk, eat, and enjoy themselves.
Most importantly, everyone brings food."
"That makes sense."
"I’m not finished."
Dexter gestured for her to continue.
"We exchange meals.
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
"Exchange?"
"Yeah.
It’s a tradition around here.
You cook something, someone else cooks something, then everyone shares.
You give people some of your food and they’ll give you some of theirs."
Dexter finally understood.
"So basically, I need to cook enough food to share."
"Exactly!"
Tessa smiled brightly.
A small dimple appeared on her cheek, softening her features.
It was a smile that made her look younger, more carefree.
"And I’ll be expecting yours tomorrow."
Dexter narrowed his eyes playfully.
"Now I understand why you came all the way here to explain the tradition."
"What?"
"You just want free food."
Tessa placed a hand against her chest, feigning offense.
"Free food?
It’s a cultural exchange."
Dexter almost laughed.
"Of course."
"A very important cultural exchange."
"Right."
Tessa pointed at him.
"So make sure you save some for me.
I want to taste more of your cooking."
Dexter smiled.
"If you’re late, it won’t be my fault if everything finishes."
Tessa’s mouth immediately fell open.
Then she pouted.
"You’re trying to bully me."
"I’m warning you."
"That’s bullying."
Dexter chuckled and waved his hand.
"Goodnight, Tessa."
Tessa continued pouting for another second before eventually smiling.
"Goodnight, Dexter.
See you tomorrow."
"See you tomorrow."
She waved before turning away.
Dexter watched her leave, her figure growing smaller as she walked down the quiet street.
Then he closed and locked the gate.
He returned inside.
The house was quiet again.
Everyone had already eaten.
Selene and Lyra had woken up earlier in the evening, and Lyra had returned to the girls’ room after eating.
Mira had eaten as well.
By now, everyone had retired for the night.
Dexter entered his bedroom and sat on the edge of his bed.
Tomorrow.
He leaned backward slightly and thought about it.
Tomorrow would be the first time in quite a while that he was taking all three girls outside simply to enjoy themselves.
No fighting.
No cultivation emergency.
No business.
No thugs smashing through walls.
At least, Dexter hoped so.
He wasn’t entirely sure whether he should be nervous about taking all three of his wives to a neighborhood festival at once.
Still...
Dexter smiled.
He was looking forward to it.
The girls had spent far too much time inside the house recently.
A change of scenery would be good for them.
Especially Mira.

chapters.title: Chapter 250 | Preparations II
paragraphs: Dexter’s expression became thoughtful. He would need to wake up early and prepare enough food for the picnic. Since the tradition involved exchanging meals, making only enough for himself and the girls wouldn’t work.

Fortunately, tomorrow was also one of the rare mornings when he didn’t have to prepare food for sale. Most businesses in the neighborhood would be closed for the festival. That included Tessa’s father’s bakery.
Technically, Dexter would lose a day’s income. But considering how much work he normally did every morning, having one day where he could cook without worrying about orders wasn’t exactly terrible.
"A day off won’t kill me."
He could wake up early, prepare several dishes for the picnic, and still have enough time to get ready before they left.

Dexter began mentally arranging everything he would need. Ingredients. Containers. Utensils. He would need to make enough for four people, plus extra for sharing. Maybe some pastries, since Lyra seemed to enjoy them. Something warm and hearty for Mira. And perhaps something lighter for Selene, whose body still struggled with the Eternal Ice.
Then his bedroom door suddenly opened.
A cold current swept through the room.
Dexter didn’t even need to turn around.
"Selene."
She stepped inside.

Something about her was different tonight. During her previous visits, Selene had always hesitated at the doorway. Sometimes she would stand there awkwardly, almost as though she needed to convince herself to enter. Her pale eyes would flicker around the room, her posture rigid with uncertainty.
Tonight, she simply walked in.
She only stopped briefly when her eyes met Dexter’s. He smiled. That seemed to remove whatever tiny amount of uncertainty remained.
Selene walked forward and sat on the bed opposite him without waiting for an invitation. She crossed her legs, her silver hair cascading over her shoulders like moonlight made solid.
"Hi."
"Hey."
Selene glanced around before looking at him again. "I hope I’m not disturbing you."
"Not at all."
"You’re sure?"
"Completely."
Selene nodded. "Okay."
She closed her eyes. Almost immediately, she entered a cultivation state. Her breathing slowed, her body stilled, and the cold energy within her began to stir.
Dexter watched her for a moment. Then he activated his Heavenly Flame talent.

No visible flames appeared. He deliberately kept the manifestation suppressed, allowing only the intense warmth produced by the Heavenly Flame to flow through his body. Heat gradually spread across the bed, radiating outward like invisible sunlight.

Selene’s tense expression relaxed almost immediately. The cold energy inside her was extremely troublesome, but Dexter had already discovered that his Heavenly Flame could suppress it. The closer she remained to him, the more effective that suppression became.
Less than a minute later, Dexter spoke. "Selene."
Her eyes opened.
"Come sit closer."
Selene blinked. Dexter tapped the empty space beside him. "You’ll feel the heat better from here."
Selene looked at the space. Then at Dexter. For a brief second, the old hesitation returned. But it quickly disappeared.
"Okay."
She shifted across the bed and sat directly beside him, resting her back against the headboard. A slight flush appeared on her cheeks—barely visible against her pale skin, but there nonetheless.

Dexter noticed it. He also noticed something else. She wasn’t nearly as uncomfortable around him anymore. The first few times she had entered his room, every movement had been filled with hesitation. Now she had walked in herself. Sat on his bed without being invited. And when Dexter asked her to move closer, she had done so without arguing.
Progress.
Dexter smiled faintly.
Selene noticed. "What?"
"Nothing."
She stared suspiciously at him. "You’re smiling."
"Am I not allowed?"
Selene looked away. "I didn’t say that."
Dexter chuckled softly. "Continue cultivating."
Selene closed her eyes again. Dexter did the same.

The Heavenly Flame stirred inside him. Warmth radiated outward. The cold energy within Selene instinctively reacted, but whenever it threatened to surge, Dexter’s heat pressed against it, suppressing the icy outbreak before it could spread.

Selene’s breathing gradually became calmer. Dexter focused on maintaining the balance. Heat and cold. Two completely opposing forces existed only inches apart. Yet instead of clashing violently, they gradually settled into an unusual harmony.
Minutes became hours. Neither of them spoke again. Eventually, the night disappeared.
Dexter’s eyes opened.
For a moment, he remained completely still. His internal clock had awakened him almost exactly when he wanted. He glanced toward his phone. Five minutes before the alarm.
Dexter reached over and switched it off before it could ring.
Then he tried to sit up.
Something stopped him.
Dexter looked down.

Selene was hugging him. Sometime during their cultivation, she had apparently moved closer until she was practically wrapped around him, instinctively seeking the warmth produced by his Heavenly Flame. Her arms were draped across his chest, her face pressed against his shoulder.
Her face was peaceful. More peaceful than he had ever seen it. The permanent tension around her eyes was gone. The slight frown that usually lingered on her lips had vanished.
Dexter stared at her for several seconds. Then he smiled.
"So much for sitting closer."
He carefully loosened her arms from around him. Selene shifted slightly. Dexter froze. She didn’t wake. He waited another second before slowly slipping out of her embrace and getting off the bed.
Selene instinctively moved toward the warmth he had left behind, hugging part of the blanket instead. Dexter almost laughed.
He pulled the blanket over her properly, tucking the edges around her shoulders.
Then he quietly left the bedroom.
The house was still silent. Outside, dawn was only beginning to arrive. The sky was a pale grey, the first hints of orange just beginning to creep over the horizon.
Dexter stretched his arms.
Today was the festival. And apparently, thanks to Tessa’s warning, he had quite a bit of cooking ahead of him.

Dexter entered the kitchen, rolled up his sleeves, and looked over the ingredients he had available. Flour. Rice. Vegetables. Meat. Eggs. Spices. Everything he needed was there, organized and waiting.
A smile slowly appeared on his face.
"If everyone is exchanging food..."
He reached for the first ingredient.
"...I might as well make something worth exchanging."
And with that, Dexter began preparing the meals for the picnic.
